title: iPhone Duo Guide: Everything you need to know about Apple’s folding iPhone
content:
Macworld






Apple is unveiling the new iPhone Duo at an event. We are updating this article as the news breaks!
New iPhone Duo features at a glance
Apple’s first foldable iPhone is official: The iPhone Duo has a widescreen folding design and comes in white and Night Sky dark blue.
Adaptive interface: Controls shift from the outer display to the inner screen and dynamically adjust depending on how the phone is positioned.
Reinforced hinge: Apple says the hinge uses support ribs and ceramic-fiber inserts that are three times stronger than Grade 5 titanium.
Premium finish: A custom nanotexture reduces glare and reflections, while AI-assisted manufacturing pairs each hinge with its best-fit housing for precise alignment.
Battery life: Apple claims up to 31 hours using the inner display and 44 hours using the outer display, with around 24 hours of typical use per charge.
Cameras: The iPhone Duo uses the same dual 48MP camera system as the iPhone 17, so it falls short of the iPhone 18 Pro’s camera setup.
Price: iPhone Duo starts at $1,999.
The rumors are true: Apple’s first foldable phone is here with a widescreen design. 
Apple’s first folding phone is available in two colors: white and night sky (dark blue).
Controls on the outer screen have been moved to the side of the screen. These seamingly transtition to the inner display, and dynamically adjusts to the position its in. 
Apple describes the hinge as “The central structural plane has support ribs for added stiffness. To make the frame even more rigid, the antenna splits are reinforced with high performance inserts. They’re made from ceramic fibers that are three times stronger than grade five titanium. Together these structural details make iPhone Duo feel exceptionally solid every time you use it.”
During the presentation, Johny Srouji explained that Apple has developed a custom nanotexture finish that significantly reduces glare and reflections. The unique texture creates a perceptually flat matte surface that minimizes craft visibility and also feels premium to touch. During manufacturing Apple uses AI algorithms to precisely manage each individual hinge with its best fit housing to ensure perfect alignment.
Srouji also explained that optimizations and battery capacities mean users can get up to 31 hours when using the inner display and 44 hours when using just the outer display, for a total of 24 hours per charge during a typical day.
The iPhone Duo has the same dual 48MP camera system as the iPhone 17, it’s not as good as the iPhone 18 Pro camera. 
 iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 with 256GB of storage. Preorders start on October 16 and will begin shipping on October 23.

				
					

				
			
Apple





Read on to see the rumors from before the event while we update this article. 
We’ve been reporting on the supposedly imminent launch of a foldable iPhone for years. There have been strong and reliable rumors of a foldable iPhone being just two years away, dating as far back as 2018, at least. Back then, reliable reports from the likes of CNBC said Apple was going to have a folding iPhone on the market in 2020.
That became 2021, 2022, 2024, 2025… and now it’s expected to land in 2026 – yes, this year! The wait may finally be nearly over: Apple is expected to unveil its first foldable iPhone on September 9 alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, although reports suggest supplies could be limited and some buyers may have to wait longer to get one.
Rumors had suggest the new model could be called the iPhone Ultra, until the morning of the event when Mark Gurman of Bloomberg reported that it will be called the iPhone Duo. The folding iPhone is expected to adopt a book-style design that opens into something resembling a small iPad. It’s expected to have an approximately 7.7- to 7.8-inch internal display and a 5.3- to 5.5-inch outer screen, with a wide 4:3 aspect ratio when unfolded. Apple is also said to have focused heavily on making the display crease as unobtrusive as possible while keeping the device exceptionally thin.
Inside, we’re expecting some variation of Apple’s A20 chip, around 12GB of RAM, Apple’s C2 cellular modem and potentially the biggest battery yet fitted to an iPhone. Camera rumors point to two 48MP rear cameras and two selfie cameras, but there could be some surprising compromises: the iPhone Ultra (or iPhone Duo) may ditch both Face ID and a telephoto camera, using Touch ID in the side button instead. And all that folding technology won’t come cheap, with current estimates putting the starting price at around $1,999 and potentially as high as $2,399 for the top configuration.
Folding iPhone rumors at a glance
Expected launch date: September 9, 2026, but limited supply possible
Likely name: iPhone Duo rather than iPhone Ultra or iPhone Fold
Form factor: Book-style, opening to a landscape view about the size of an iPad mini
Display: 7.7–7.8-inch inner display, approx 5.3–5.5-inch outer
Camera: Four cameras, no telephoto
Color options: Indigo and white/silver


What will the foldable iPhone be called?
iPhone Ultra was the long-standing favorite, but Apple may instead call it iPhone Duo.
Apple’s first foldable iPhone has picked up numerous unofficial names over the years, including iPhone Fold and iPhone 18 Fold. More recently, iPhone Ultra emerged as the most credible candidate. But on the morning of September 9, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported that Apple is set to unveil a roughly $2,000 foldable called the iPhone Duo.
The Duo name would make sense given the device’s dual-purpose design: a compact iPhone when folded and something closer to a small iPad when opened.
Until now, the evidence had pointed strongly toward iPhone Ultra. In March 2026, Gurman reported that the foldable would be positioned as part of Apple’s expanding “Ultra” tier. Weibo leaker Digital Chat Station subsequently claimed Apple was considering the same name.
More recently, Gurman said on X that “everyone calls it the Ultra internally.” That made iPhone Ultra appear increasingly likely, although it now seems possible that Ultra was simply Apple’s internal name for the project rather than its final branding.
Analyst Max Weinbach had also questioned whether “Ultra” was an appropriate name, arguing that the foldable did not necessarily fit the positioning of Apple’s other highest-end Ultra products.


Everyone calls it the Ultra internally. We’ll see what happens.
— Mark Gurman (@markgurman) August 11, 2026





Other names floated over the years include iPhone Ultra Fold, iPhone Passport, iPhone Folio and iPhone Wide. “Passport” refers to the handset’s reportedly wide, passport-like proportions when folded.
With Apple’s “Surprise and Shine” event taking place on September 9, iPhone Duo is now the name to watch, although Apple has yet to confirm the branding officially.


						

							


When will the foldable iPhone launch?
September 9, 2026 launch at Apple Event expected; retail availability may follow later
Apple is expected to unveil its first foldable iPhone at its “Surprise and Shine” event on September 9, 2026, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max. The regular iPhone 18, 18e or iPhone Air 2, are instead expected to arrive in spring 2027.
There have been conflicting reports about when the foldable will actually go on sale. Nikkei Asia reported that Apple was running behind schedule, but Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman subsequently said the device was still on track, and could ship at the same time as, or soon after, the iPhone 18 Pro models. Barclays analyst Tim Long has been more cautious, suggesting the foldable may not ship until December.
There is also growing evidence in Apple’s software that the device is close. In June, product designer and engineer Sam Henri Gold found references in the iOS 27 framework to variables named “foldState” and “angleDegrees,” apparently designed to tell apps whether a device is folded and at what angle. Macworld independently confirmed those findings.


iOS 27 framework references “foldState” and “angleDegrees” but I’m sure that’s nothing pic.twitter.com/PcYNVvymms
— sam henri gold (@samhenrigold) June 8, 2026





Even if the iPhone Ultra (or Duo) launches on September 9, availability could be tight. During Apple’s Q3 earnings call, Apple then-CEO Tim Cook warned that that the impact of supply constraints would “increase significantly.” That raises the possibility that Apple could have limited stock initially, or begin shipping it later than the iPhone 18 Pro models.


						

							


What are the biggest trade-offs for the folding iPhone Duo/Ultra
Despite its expected “Ultra” branding and a price that could reach $2,000–$2,500, Apple’s first foldable iPhone may involve several compromises compared with the iPhone 18 Pro Max.
The biggest could be Face ID. Reports suggest the foldable will use a side-mounted Touch ID sensor instead, likely because its unusually thin design leaves less room for Apple’s TrueDepth hardware.
It may also sacrifice some camera capability. The foldable is not expected to include a dedicated telephoto camera, meaning buyers could miss out on the optical zoom available on Apple’s Pro models. That would be a significant omission on such an expensive iPhone.
The hinge also means Apple cannot use the same unibody-style construction as on a conventional iPhone, potentially affecting durability and dust resistance. The device is also expected to be eSIM-only worldwide.
There have been questions over MagSafe and wireless charging, partly because of the unusual construction of the rear casing, although more recent reports suggest MagSafe may ultimately be included.
Finally, the foldable is expected to run a specially adapted version of iOS rather than iPadOS. Its larger internal display should enable improved multitasking, but it may still fall short of the more desktop-like productivity experience available on an iPad.
Taken together, those compromises mean the iPhone Ultra (or iPhone Duo) could offer something genuinely new without necessarily being the most fully featured iPhone Apple sells. For some buyers, the iPhone 18 Pro Max may remain the more complete flagship.

				
					

				
			
The folding iPhone will reportedly have a Touch ID-enabled power button rather than Face ID.

Foundry



							


What will the folding iPhone look like? How will it fold? 
Book-like design with a vertical fold rumored
Intended to be an iPhone/iPad hybrid
Available in silver/white and Indigo Blue
Apple’s rumored iPhone Ultra or iPhone Duo is reportedly nearing mass production, with its design largely finalized. Here’s what current leaks suggest about how the foldable iPhone will look and how the hinge and display may work.
What color will the iPhone Ultra/Duo be?
The iPhone Ultra/Duo is expected to launch in just two color options: silver/white and dark blue.
Back in August, we reported that Apple was working on an Indigo option for its folding phone. Our sources also say that Apple does not currently plan to offer its first folding iPhone in black or space gray. The blue finish is expected to be particularly dark, reportedly closer to the iPhone 17 Pro’s Deep Blue than the MacBook Neo’s Indigo.
A subsequent leak shared by Sonny Dickson on Bluesky added weight to those reports, with photos reportedly showing camera protectors in silver and a deep blue shade that could resemble Indigo, Midnight or the iPhone 17 Pro’s Deep Blue.


These iPhone Fold camera protectors give us a look at two of the colors planned for the device: silver and dark blue.
— Sonny Dickson (@sonnydickson.bsky.social) 2026-08-08T22:44:44.846Z





The leaked camera protector matches previous design rumours, showing a horizontal rounded camera bar with openings for two cameras, a microphone and flash.
Book-style, iPad hybrid, design
Multiple leaks point to a book-style foldable with a large, tablet-like internal display, rather than a compact flip-phone design. The device is expected to function as a hybrid between an iPhone and an iPad.
This “passport-style” design will appear noticeably squarer than a traditional iPhone when closed. When unfolded, it’s rumored to resemble an iPad mini-like screen with a 4:3 aspect ratio, offering a more expansive viewing experience.
Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo reported in 2025 that Apple’s foldable will adopt a dual-display setup, with a strong focus on achieving a near crease-free screen when opened. 
Other 2025 leaks, including reports from Digital Chat Station on Weibo, also point to a vertical, book-style fold where the left and right sides close together – similar to devices like the Google Pixel 9 Pro Fold and Samsung Galaxy Z Fold.
Dummy models shared by Sonny Dickson on X in April 2026, demonstrate this book-like form factor. 

				
					

				
			The latest leaks and dummy models show the wide “passport” design of the iPhone Ultra/Duo.
Sonny Dickson




Additional dummy unit images from tech YouTuber Vadim Yuryev, further reinforce this wide, book-like “passport” design. 

				
					

				
			Vadim Yuryev
In December 2025, this 3D image of the so called iPhone Ultra, based on leaked CAD files, was created by a hobbyist and shared on MakerWorld (now removed), also aligning with these design expectations.

				
					

				
			Subsy/MakerWorld
However, alternative concepts have existed. In 2024, The Information reported that Apple had explored clamshell-style prototypes, where the device folds top-to-bottom, similar to traditional flip phones.
This design direction may already be influencing competitors. Our colleagues on TechAdvisor report that Samsung is developing a “Galaxy Z Fold 8 Wide” with a similar 4:3 aspect ratio, potentially positioning it as a direct rival to Apple’s iPhone Ultra/Duo.
How Apple is overcoming hinge design and crease reduction challenges
Adding a hinge to an iPhone introduces significant engineering challenges that Apple has spent years trying to resolve. While competitors have released multiple generations of foldables, Apple’s slower entry to the market is widely attributed to its focus on refining the hinge and delivering a more seamless user experience.
The biggest technical challenge is the visible and tactile crease where the screen folds. Apple has reportedly made this a priority, aiming to minimise it to the point of being nearly imperceptible.
Weibo leaker Instant Digital claims the iPhone Ultra’s (or Duo) internal design will make it the most repairable folding phone on the market, with elegant modular and stacked elements that minimize interconnects and ribbons.
As a result, the hinge is expected to be a defining feature of the iPhone Ultra//Duo, combining advanced materials and engineering to deliver a smoother, more durable folding experience.
To maintain both thinness and durability, Apple is reportedly testing high-end materials for the hinge:
Titanium alloy (rumored for structural strength)
LiquidMetal, according to Ming-Chi Kuo (March 2025), for improved durability, better screen flatness, and reduced creasing.
In July 2025, Kuo reported that Apple had developed a method to reduce crease visibility using metal support plates to better distribute and control bending stress. Apple may use this “laser-drilling metal plate technology” rather than conventional etching to create a more precise microstructure. 
Apple also holds several patents for foldable mechanisms which, along with several rumored technologies, may be used:
Variable Thickness Glass: A key part of Apple’s approach is said to involve variable thickness display glass, which is thinner at the fold point to reduce stress during repeated use. This is expected to work alongside an optically clear adhesive layer, designed to further minimise strain and help prevent the visible crease that commonly develops in foldable devices over time.
Stress-Reducing Adhesive: An optically clear adhesive designed to reduce strain on the display during folding.
Ultra-Thin Profile: Expected thickness of around 4.5mm unfolded and 9.5mm folded.
Internal Support: Metal plates beneath the display to maintain a completely flat surface when opened.
In March 2026, reports suggested that Samsung Display – Apple’s primary screen supplier – has developed a near-creaseless OLED panel, showcased at CES 2026 specifically to meet Apple’s standards.


						

							


How big will the foldable iPhone Ultra/iPhone Duo be?
Approx. 9.5mm thick when folded
Approx. 4.5mm when unfolded
According to Jon Prosser in December 2025, Apple’s foldable iPhone could measure around 9.5mm when closed and just 4.5mm when open. For context, the iPhone 16 Pro Max is 8.5mm thick, while the iPhone Air measures 5.6mm.
If accurate, this would make the iPhone Ultra/Duo one of the slimmest foldables, highlighting Apple’s focus on minimising bulk despite the hinge.
However, when asked about the thickness of the iPhone Ultra/Duo in April 2026, YouTuber Vadim Yuryev said it would be “exactly 11mm”, which is larger than Prosser’s prediction. He also claimed it would be 0.36mm taller and 0.39mm wider than the iPhone 17 Pro.
Other design features
A leak from Weibo account Instant Digital in February 2026 indicates the volume buttons will be on the top edge, aligned right.


						

							


How big will the folding iPhone screens be?
The iPhone Ultra/Duo is widely expected to feature:
Approx. 7.7–7.8-inch internal display
Approx. 5.3–5.5-inch external display
Ming-Chi Kuo (2025) and TrendForce (July 2025) both pointed to a 7.8-inch inner and 5.5-inch outer display, while The Information later suggested slightly smaller sizes of 7.7 inches and 5.3 inches. This suggests Apple may still be refining final dimensions.
However, a December 2025 report from The Information slightly revised these figures to 7.7 inches internally and 5.3 inches externally, indicating that Apple may still be fine-tuning the final dimensions.
When unfolded, the device is expected to feature a 4:3 aspect ratio, aligning it more closely with the iPad and reinforcing its positioning as a productivity-focused, hybrid device. This would be a notable departure from the tall, narrow displays seen in earlier foldables like the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold series. 
This wider layout is said to:
Improve multitasking
Enhance document reading and web browsing
Deliver an experience closer to an iPad mini


						

							


What specs will iPhone Ultra/iPhone Duo offer?
A20 Pro chip, 12GB RAM, C2 modem expected
The iPhone Ultra (or Duo) is expected to use Apple’s A20 Pro chip, the same flagship processor tipped for the iPhone 18 Pro models. Supply-chain reports also point to 12GB of RAM and storage options reaching as high as 2TB.
Apple is also expected to use more of its own wireless silicon. That could include the C2 cellular modem alongside an Apple-designed Wi-Fi and Bluetooth chip supporting Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth. 256GB/512GB/1TB/2TB capacities are to be expected. 
One notable feature is MagSafe charging. In September 2026, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman said the folding iPhone will support MagSafe, contradicting earlier reports that Apple might omit it because of the device’s unusual construction.
Battery capacity could be another headline feature. Weibo leaker Fixed Focus Digital has claimed the iPhone Ultra/Duo will have a combined capacity of around 5,000 to 5,500mAh, potentially making it the largest battery ever fitted to an iPhone.
That capacity may be split between the two halves of the device. References to “batteries” rather than “battery” found in the iOS 27 beta have fuelled speculation that Apple is preparing software support for a dual-battery folding iPhone.


						

							


What cameras will the foldable iPhone have?
The foldable iPhone is expected to use a dual-camera system on the rear, with two 48MP sensors arranged on a long, thin “plateau” similar to the iPhone Air. Reports suggest the camera bar will be black rather than color-matched to the rest of the phone.
There is still some uncertainty over the exact lens combination. More recent reports point to a wide and telephoto setup, while earlier rumors suggested Apple could omit the telephoto lens and instead use wide and ultrawide cameras. If the telephoto camera is missing, it would be a significant compromise for such an expensive “Ultra” model.
The foldable is also expected to have two front-facing cameras – specified to be the usual 18MP Centre Stage cameras by TrendForce in June – allowing one to be used when the phone is closed and another when it is unfolded. Leaks have suggested Apple could combine an under-display camera with a second punch-hole camera.
A November 2025 JP Morgan report also claimed Apple could omit LiDAR and optical image stabilization, although those details remain uncertain.
Not all the rumors point to cutbacks. Tech YouTuber Vadim Yuryev claimed in April 2026 that the camera sensors could actually be physically larger than those used in the iPhone 17 Pro. 


						

							


How much will the folding iPhone Ultra cost?
Premium price expected: $2,000 or more
Apple’s first folding iPhone is expected to sit at the very top of the iPhone lineup, with most reports pointing to a starting price of around $2,000.
Analyst Arthur Liao has predicted a price of up to $2,399, based on the high cost of components such as the folding display and hinge, as well as Apple’s usual premium margins.
A September 2026 TrendForce report puts the likely starting price at $2,099 to $2,299, with higher-capacity configurations potentially exceeding $3,000.
Reports from Weibo leakers have suggested a starting price of RMB 15,999 in China for the 256GB model, rising to RMB 19,999 for 1TB. Using the pricing relationship of comparable Apple products, that would broadly translate to around $1,999 to $2,399 in the U.S.
Taken together, the rumors suggest the iPhone Ultra/Duo will start at roughly $2,000, with higher-storage models costing considerably more.






FAQ
Why is Apple making a folding iPhone now?
If you’re wondering why Apple is only launching a folding iPhone now – years after Samsung introduced the Galaxy Fold in 2019 – the answer may lie in Apple’s long-standing approach to new product categories. Rather than being first to market, Apple often waits for a technology to mature before entering the space.
When Steve Jobs unveiled the original iPhone in 2007, he talked about how the rest of the market was constrained by physical keyboards and styluses, but the iPhone would instead have a multi-touch display that could change depending on the task. Apple may be taking a similar approach with foldables. The company appears to believe that display technology, durability, and consumer interest have finally reached a point where a folding iPhone could appeal to mainstream buyers rather than just early adopters.
In other words, Apple’s goal may not be to invent the foldable phone, but to make it a product that millions of people actually want to use every day.
Will the iPhone Ultra (or iPhone Duo) replace the iPhone Pro Max?
It is thought that rather than replace the Pro Max handsets, Apple will position the foldable as a new tier above it – similar to how the Apple Watch Ultra sits above the standard Watch lineup. That would allow Apple to maintain premium pricing without disrupting existing flagship models.
When will the foldable iPhone actually go on sale?
The folding iPhone is expected to be announced at Apple’s September event on Wednesday, 9 September 2026, but the phone may not go on sale for some time after that date. Reports suggest the device could go on sale sometime between October and December 2026.

title: Apple Reference Image is a new way to authenticate iPhone photography
content:
Apple Reference Image gives iPhone 18 Pro owners verifiable evidence of what the camera captured, offering a new defense against convincing AI-generated and edited images.

Apple Reference Image
The opt-in feature uses a new sensor in the Main camera that can sign every pixel it sees. Taking a photo in Reference mode captures signed sensor data that Private Cloud Compute turns into an unalterable reference image.
The Photos app displays that reference beside the main photo like a digital negative, allowing viewers to compare the two and determine whether edits were made. Apple's official release says the feature is designed for photojournalists, photographers, and everyday viewers.
Apple Reference Image first appeared in beta code in August. Apple has now confirmed that APIs in iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27 will let third-party apps display reference images.

One More Thing… but what?
“We have great respect for these words,” said Tim Cook in 2017, “and we don’t use them lightly.” Those words, of course, were One More Thing.
That little phrase has signalled the arrival of some of Apple’s most iconic products and services, including the iMac G4, the MacBook Pro, FaceTime, the Apple Watch, Apple Music, and the iPhone X. Will it be uttered this year, and if so, what will it herald?

(Debut as overall event host, that is. He’s spoken in individual segments before now.) Surprise? What surprise?
Apple has given this week’s showcase the tagline “Surprise and Shine.” But what’s the big surprise? Apple’s September events are among its most predictable, almost always revolving around new iPhones and new Apple Watches, and sometimes new AirPods.
September 2025: iPhones, Apple Watches, AirPods
September 2024: iPhones, Apple Watches, AirPods
September 2023: iPhones, Apple Watches
September 2022: iPhones, Apple Watches, AirPods
September 2021: iPhones, Apple Watches, iPads
Is John Ternus going to spring a surprise in 2026? After asking this question on TikTok we’re unconvinced by the idea of an Apple alarm clock (sorry), but another reader’s proposal of a “tabletop Pixar light robot personal assistant with Siri” is a little more plausible. That sounds a lot like the rumored smart-home hub which Apple has been working on for years, and could make an appearance this week. It could even turn up as One More Thing at the end and make for a fun encore.
But ultimately the most likely outcome is that, as far as Apple is concerned, the widely expected foldable iPhone counts as the surprise. title: Apple Announces Foldable 'iPhone Duo'
content:
Apple today announced the "iPhone Duo," a new kind of iPhone featuring two screens and a foldable inner display.


The two halves of the iPhone Duo connect into a single continuous frame with the same aspect ratio across both displays, and Apple said the transition between open and closed is designed to feel fluid. When fully open, Apple called it the thinnest iPhone ever made, with an architecture that packages its components into the camera plateau. 

Touch ID is built into the side button, and the device can also be unlocked using an Apple Watch.

A custom hinge, made from more than 100 tiny precision components, holds the display flat when open and controls the folding motion. Apple said the structure uses a multi layer lamination design with viscoelastic adhesives that let the display's layers glide against each other during folding "like pages in a book," preventing distortion over time. A titanium plate forms the bottom layer for added durability, with carbon fiber support plates creating a stiff, lightweight base for the display to rest on.



iPhone 18 Pro Max and 80% larger than the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌, while the outer display is 5.4 inches and offers 90% of the screen area of the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌. Apple Pencil support is coming to both displays later this year.

For the display surface itself, Apple said it created a custom nano texture finish that cuts down on glare and reflections. The company also described a separate micro lens texture, produced using maskless laser lithography that writes each lens pixel by pixel, which it said creates a "perceptually flat matte surface" that minimizes the visibility of the fold crease while still feeling premium to the touch.

Home Screen dock is now oriented vertically, and the status bar has been redesigned to fit into the corner of the display. Software transitions gracefully between the outer and inner displays as the device opens, with controls staying in a consistent position while content scales up.

iOS also adapts to how the device is angled or propped, and it can be used partially folded, with content sliding away from the crease where taps are harder to register. Custom audio tuning adjusts for the changing distance between the speakers depending on how the device is positioned. Users can run two apps at once or open the same app twice, and can swipe up from the bottom to switch apps or pair two apps together to reopen later. A new Standby mode adds widgets for music, calendar, or weather, and Apple said the device can double as a bedside clock with a soft glow. 

The iPhone Duo uses the same 48MP Fusion main camera design Apple has used elsewhere in its lineup alongside a 48MP Fusion ultra wide camera, the same ultra wide used in the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌, and supports Apple's upgraded Photographic Styles. Since the device can stand on its own, Apple said it opens up new options for capturing time lapses in 4K Dolby Vision HDR.

FaceTime camera hidden behind the screen, which works whether the device is fully open or propped on a surface, and the two cameras can dual capture front and rear scenes simultaneously. A new Duo ‌FaceTime‌ feature lets someone else join a video call from the outer display. A Smart Take feature tracks a scene and automatically takes the photo once everyone in a group shot is ready, removing the need to set a timer, and the outer display can play animations to help hold a child's attention for the camera.

iPhone 17 Pro. The iPhone Duo is eSIM only worldwide.

Each half of the device has its own battery, which Apple said operate together as a single battery for all day use, rated at up to 31 hours of video playback on the inner display and 44 hours on the outer display. Using both screens equally, Apple rates the device for up to 24 hours of battery life, with fast charging reaching 50% in around 20 minutes and just five minutes of charging providing up to five hours of video playback on the outer display.

New accessories include a Duo Folio case with a built in kickstand, along with an iPhone Duo case made of two separate parts that wrap around each half of the device.

The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 for 256GB, with storage options going up to 2TB. Preorders begin October 16, with availability starting October 23.

More to follow...

title: Siri on Apple Watch can remember useful parts of your day without retaining everything
content:
Your Apple Watch now listens all day to build a daily Siri Recap from the sounds around you. The catch? It actually forgets the audio the moment it understands the context.

Siri Recap
Audio Intelligence uses Sound Recognition to identify relevant information from the wearer's surroundings as events happen. Siri can combine those signals with other available data to summarize the day later.
The resulting Siri Recap doesn't include transcripts of overheard conversations, and Apple says the feature doesn't store audio. Sound processing happens continuously before the original audio is discarded.
Users can leave Audio Intelligence running throughout the day, activate it manually, or limit it to selected locations. The feature extends the AI push Apple introduced across its latest hardware.

title: Apple Watch Series 12 & Ultra 4: Everything you need to know about the new Apple Watches
content:
Macworld






Apple is unveiling the new Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 at an event. We are updating this article as the news breaks!
New Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 features at a glance:
New health monitoring: Continuous heart-rate readings power a broader health system, including a Readiness app and a redesigned Health app with a new Health Age metric.
More proactive guidance: Readiness is designed to tell users when to push harder and when to ease off based on their health data.
Live Rewind: Records and transcribes recent conversations and activity from your day.
Siri Recap: Uses ambient listening to create high-level notes and takeaways from conversations such as meetings or parent-teacher conferences, with a new Siri Modular watch face for accessing recaps.
Apple Watch Series 12 Colors: Space gray, black, light gold, and dark bronze, as well as ceramic options in white and night blue.
Apple Ultra 4: Black and natural titanium.
Prices unchanged: Apple Watch Series 12 starts at $399, while Apple Watch Ultra 4 starts at $799.
The big new Apple Watch feature is a new health monitoring system that take continuous heart rate readings to give users a better picture of their heath and enable completely new experiences.
A new Readiness app can tell you when to push and when to hold back, while a redesigned Health app can provide a new Health Age. 
Live Rewind will record everything in your day and transcribes what was just said.
Another feature, Siri Recap, uses “ambient listening to take high level notes of your conversations like takeaways from a team meeting or a parent-teacher conference.” There’s also a new Siri Modular face to access your conversations and recaps.
The Apple Watch Series 12 comes in in space gray, black, light gold, and dark bronze, as well as ceramic options in white and night blue. The Apple Watch Ultra comes in black and natural titanium.
The new watches cost $399 and $799 m- same as the previous models.
Read on to see the rumors from before the event while we update this article. 
Apple is expected to unveil the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 at its September 9 event, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and foldable iPhone Ultra. An Apple Watch SE 4 is not expected.
Don’t expect a major redesign. Both watches should look much like their predecessors, although Apple has reportedly tested white and dark gray ceramic finishes. A new, faster S-series chip is expected to be one of the main upgrades.
Health changes could include continuous heart-rate data collection, while other new sensors remain possible. However, blood-glucose monitoring still appears years away, and Touch ID now looks unlikely despite appearing in prototype code.
watchOS 27 will bring Siri AI, a redesigned Find My app and other software improvements. Pricing is less certain: the Series 12 could rise from $399 to around $429, while the Ultra 4 may stay close to $799. Read on for our roundup of all the rumors about the new Apple Watches for 2026. 


Which Apple Watches are expected on September 9?
Apple is expected to unveil two new Apple Watch models at its “Surprise and Shine” event on September 9: the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4.
Apple Watch is one of the few Apple products that receives a predictable annual update, so a Series 12 launch is widely expected. The Ultra 4 is also due to replace the current Ultra 3.
Neither model is expected to receive a major redesign. Instead, both are likely to be relatively modest “chip and ship” updates, focusing on new processors, connectivity and other internal improvements while retaining broadly similar designs.
Which Apple Watch isn’t expected to be updated?
The Apple Watch SE 4 is not expected to launch in 2026. Apple updated its budget model with the Apple Watch SE 3 in 2025, and that version is likely to remain in the lineup for another year.


						

							


What new features are expected: At a glance
Apple Watch Series 12: expected new features
The Apple Watch Series 12 is expected to be a modest upgrade, led by a faster S-series chip and potentially a larger battery. The design should remain largely unchanged, though ceramic finishes are possible. Continuous heart-rate monitoring is reportedly in testing, while Touch ID looks unlikely. Siri AI and other watchOS 27 features should provide the biggest everyday changes.
Apple Watch Ultra 4: expected new features
The Apple Watch Ultra 4 should retain the Ultra 3’s rugged design while gaining the same new S-series chip. Satellite connectivity will remain a key advantage, with watchOS 27 expected to expand its capabilities. Continuous heart-rate monitoring and Siri AI are also possible, while a major redesign, Touch ID and blood-glucose monitoring appear unlikely.


						

							






FeatureApple Watch Series 12Apple Watch Ultra 4

LaunchExpected September 9, 2026Expected September 9, 2026
DesignNo major redesign expectedNo major redesign expected
New finishesCeramic reportedly tested; new colors possibleNew colors/finishes possible
ProcessorNew, faster S-series chip, likely S11 or S12Same new S-series chip expected
BatteryLarger battery reportedly being explored; potentially longer runtimeNo firm larger-battery rumor; efficiency improvements possible
Heart-rate monitoringContinuous data collection reportedly testedContinuous data collection reportedly tested
Blood-glucose monitoringUnlikely in 2026Unlikely in 2026
Touch IDTested internally, but now considered unlikelyUnlikely
5GContinues from current generationContinues from current generation
Satellite connectivityNo strong evidence of direct satellite supportExpected to retain satellite connectivity
Siri AIYes, via watchOS 27 and compatible iPhoneYes, via watchOS 27 and compatible iPhone
Find MyNew unified Find My appNew unified Find My app
Readiness appRumoredRumored
Expected priceAround $399–$429; $429 is speculativeLikely close to $799
Overall upgradeInternal, health and software refinementInternal, health, software and satellite refinement

 






What is the Apple Watch 2026 release date?
The Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 are expected to be announced at Apple’s September iPhone event on Wednesday, September 9, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and the new iPhone Ultra.
Apple has launched a new Series Apple Watch every September since 2016, usually alongside the latest iPhones, so the arrival of the Series 12 is all but certain. The Ultra 4 is also widely expected to appear at the event.
Preorders are likely to open shortly after the announcement, with shipping expected to begin later in September.


						

							


Apple Watch 2026 chips
The Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 are expected to feature a new, faster S-series chip, although there is some uncertainty over whether Apple will call it the S11 or S12.
Unlike some recent Apple Watch generations, where processor changes have been relatively modest, the 2026 chip is expected to deliver a more meaningful improvement in performance and efficiency. It should also provide more headroom for new watchOS 27 features and increasingly demanding on-device AI capabilities.
That could be particularly important as Apple raises the hardware requirements for watchOS. watchOS 27 supports Apple Watches with an S9 chip or later, dropping several older models, suggesting newer silicon is becoming increasingly important for features such as Apple’s more advanced Siri capabilities.
As a result, the Series 12 and Ultra 4 are widely expected to be relatively straightforward “chip and ship” updates, with the processor upgrade among the most significant changes. A faster chip could also help keep the new watches compatible with major watchOS features for longer.


						

							


Will the 2026 Apple Watch get a new design?

				
					

				
			Apple Watches have looked roughly the same for years.
David Price / Foundry




A major redesign is not expected for the 2026 Apple Watch lineup. Both the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 are likely to retain the same overall design language as their predecessors, with this year’s upgrades focused more heavily on internal changes.
Last summer, a DigiTimes report raised hopes that 2026 could bring the Apple Watch its first substantial redesign in years. However, similar rumors have appeared before without materialising, including reports of a dramatically redesigned Apple Watch Series X.
More recently, Weibo leaker Instant Digital claimed that neither the Series 12 nor the Series 13 will receive a major new look, with a more significant redesign instead expected in 2028.
There has also been little evidence from Apple’s supply chain of a radically redesigned chassis. We’d therefore expect the Series 12 to retain the slimmer case and larger display of recent models, while the Ultra 4 should stick with its familiar rugged design. Smaller changes such as new colors, finishes, slightly slimmer bezels, or display tweaks remain possible.
One potentially more noticeable change could be the return of ceramic. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman has reported that Apple has tested white and dark gray ceramic Apple Watch models, which could bring back a premium material Apple last offered with the Apple Watch Edition in 2019.
Will the Apple Watch get a new display?

				
					

				
			The Series 11 has an always-on screen, but it leaves something to be desired on the brightness front.
David Price / Foundry




A more substantial display upgrade is possible eventually, but it doesn’t look certain for 2026.
Apple has used OLED displays since the original Apple Watch, with recent Series models reaching up to 2,000 nits of brightness and the Ultra 3 reaching 3,000 nits. For several years there have been reports that Apple wants to move to microLED, which could offer better color accuracy, greater efficiency, and significantly higher brightness.
At CES 2025, Samsung demonstrated a microLED smartwatch display capable of 4,000 nits, showing the potential of the technology. However, while microLED remains a plausible future Apple Watch upgrade, there is currently little evidence that it will arrive with the Series 12 or Ultra 4 in 2026.


						

							


Will the Apple Watch Series 12 have longer battery life?

				
					

				
			
Petter Ahrnstedt




There are signs that battery life could be a bigger focus for the Apple Watch Series 12, although any improvement has yet to be confirmed.
According to Weibo leaker Instant Digital, Apple is prioritising battery capacity and health sensors, and is reportedly trying to fit a physically larger battery inside the Series 12 rather than relying solely on efficiency gains from the new processor.
That could help Apple extend battery life beyond the 24 hours of normal use offered by the Apple Watch Series 11. Even a modest increase would be useful for sleep tracking and other always-on health features, which leave less time for charging.
So while a dramatic leap in battery life isn’t guaranteed, the Series 12 could combine a larger battery with efficiency improvements from its new chip to deliver longer real-world runtime.
Will the Apple Watch Ultra get a better battery?
The rumor about a larger battery currently applies specifically to the Series 12, rather than the Ultra 4. The Ultra already offers substantially longer battery life, with Apple rating the Ultra 3 for up to 42 hours of normal use and up to 72 hours in Low Power Mode.


						

							


What connectivity changes are coming with the 2026 Apple Watches?
Major connectivity changes are not currently expected for the 2026 Apple Watch lineup.
5G is already supported on current cellular Apple Watch models and there are also no strong reports pointing to a major new cellular modem upgrade this year.
However, Satellite connectivity is more significant, but it is primarily an Apple Watch Ultra feature. The current Ultra 3 already supports Emergency SOS, Find My, and Messages via satellite, and the Ultra 4 is expected to retain those capabilities.
watchOS 27 is also expected to expand what Apple Watch can do over satellite, with features including Apple Maps via satellite and the ability to send and receive photos in Messages via satellite. Those software features should be available on the Ultra 4 where supported.
There is currently no evidence that the Apple Watch Series 12 will gain direct satellite connectivity, so this is likely to remain one of the key differences between the standard Series model and the Ultra.


						

							


Will Apple Watch Series 12 get Touch ID?

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Probably not in 2026.
Macworld uncovered developer code referring to the 2026 Apple Watch models alongside “AppleMesa,” Apple’s internal codename for Touch ID. No previous Apple Watch models had included similar references, suggesting Apple has at least tested fingerprint authentication for the Watch.
At the time, that raised the possibility that Touch ID could debut with the Series 12, potentially built into a side button or beneath the display. It would be useful for Apple Pay, private apps and messages, and unlocking the Watch independently of an iPhone.
However, more recent reporting has made a 2026 launch look much less likely. One leaker has claimed Apple is not bringing Touch ID to the Apple Watch, while other reports suggest Apple is prioritising larger batteries and new health sensors over using valuable internal space for fingerprint hardware.
The earlier code may therefore relate to prototype hardware rather than a feature destined for this year’s models.
For now, Touch ID appears to be something Apple has explored for the Watch, but it is unlikely to debut with the Apple Watch Series 12 or Ultra 4. 
Apple Watch already uses passcode and wrist-detection security, and it can also act as an authenticator for other Apple devices, including automatically unlocking a Mac.


						

							


What health features are coming to the 2026 Apple Watches?
Health and fitness tracking is expected to remain a major focus for the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. The most credible new feature is continuous heart-rate monitoring throughout the day, while Apple may also make further improvements to its existing health sensors and hypertension features.
More ambitious additions, including non-invasive blood-glucose monitoring and AI-powered health coaching, remain in development but are much less likely to arrive this year.
Continuous heart-rate monitoring
One of the most significant rumored upgrades for the Series 12 and Ultra 4 is continuous heart-rate data collection.
According to a report in August from Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple has tested technology that would allow the Apple Watch heart-rate sensor to “continuously collect data throughout the day.”
Currently, Apple Watch takes periodic background heart-rate readings when you aren’t using the Workout, Mindfulness, or Heart Rate apps. Continuous monitoring could provide a much richer dataset, potentially improving health trends, alerts, and other analysis.
Will Apple Watch Series 12 monitor blood glucose?
Apple has been working on non-invasive blood-glucose monitoring for many years, but it remains unlikely to arrive with the Series 12.
Reports of Apple’s work on the technology date back to at least 2017, when we reported that the company had assembled a team of biomedical engineers to investigate continuous glucose monitoring.
Bloomberg subsequently reported that Apple had developed a system based on optical absorption spectroscopy and had reached the proof-of-concept stage. However, more recent reporting suggests a commercial Apple Watch implementation may still be several years away, potentially around 2030.
So while blood-glucose monitoring remains one of Apple Watch’s most anticipated future features, Series 12 is probably too soon.
What about AI health coaching?

				
					

				
			
Apple




Apple has also been developing an AI-powered health and fitness coaching system, previously reported under the name Health+.
The project has reportedly been scaled back from a single ambitious service into individual features that can be released progressively. That means some AI-powered health insights or coaching features could appear sooner, but there is currently little evidence that a complete Health+ service will debut with the Series 12.
For 2026, continuous heart-rate monitoring looks considerably more plausible than either blood-glucose monitoring or a full AI health coach.
What health features does Apple Watch already have?
The Series 11 and Ultra 3 already offer an extensive set of health features, including:
Blood Oxygen monitoring
ECG
Heart-rate and heart-rhythm notifications
Hypertension notifications
Wrist-temperature sensing
Cycle Tracking and ovulation estimates
Sleep stages and Sleep Score
Sleep apnea notifications
The Apple Watch SE 3 has a more limited health feature set and lacks Blood Oxygen monitoring, ECG, temperature sensing, and hypertension notifications.


						

							


What new apps are coming to Apple Watch?






watchOS 27 will bring several new apps and app experiences to the Apple Watch, although Apple appears to be focusing as much on upgrading existing software as adding entirely new apps and some older Apple Watches will not be able to run watchOS 27. 
Siri AI comes to Apple Watch
The biggest software addition is Siri AI. Apple Watch users will be able to start Siri AI conversations from their wrist, access previous conversations across Apple devices, and use newer capabilities such as personal context and web answers.
Much of the processing will still depend on a nearby compatible iPhone, but the change should make Apple Watch a much more useful entry point for Apple’s AI features.
watchOS 27 with Siri AI requires an Apple Watch Series 9 or later, Ultra 2 or later, or SE 3, alongside a compatible iPhone.
Find My gets a major overhaul
Apple is also introducing a unified Find My app, replacing the separate Find People, Find Devices and Find Items apps with a single map-based interface.
That should make it much easier to locate people, Apple devices and AirTags directly from the Watch without jumping between multiple apps.
A new Readiness app could be coming
Late-breaking code discovered in September reportedly points to a separate Readiness app for Apple Watch.
The app is thought to focus on recovery and preparedness, potentially using health and fitness data to indicate how ready you are for exercise or other activity. However, this has not yet been officially announced, so it should still be treated as a rumor.
Existing apps are getting smarter too
Apple is also improving several existing Watch apps and features rather than simply adding new ones.
Workout Buddy is becoming more capable, with smarter fitness insights, Spanish-language support and the ability to work without a direct iPhone connection. Wallet gains the ability to display card balances, while the Smart Stack adds new interactions, including a tap gesture for selecting widgets.
watchOS 27 also introduces a more dynamic app grid that surfaces five contextually relevant apps, while Apple continues to make its Watch apps look and behave more like their iPhone equivalents.
Overall, the most important software additions for 2026 are Siri AI, the redesigned Find My app and the possible new Readiness app, with broader improvements across Workout, Wallet and the Smart Stack.
watchOS 27 also expands women’s health features with pre-menopause tracking.


						

							


How much could the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 cost?
Apple has not announced pricing for the 2026 Apple Watch lineup but we can make some estimations especially in the light of Apple’s dramatic price rises for iPads and Macs in June 2026. 
The current Apple Watch Series 11 starts at $399, while the Apple Watch Ultra 3 starts at $799. Apple left Watch pricing unchanged when it raised prices across much of its Mac, iPad and home-device lineup in June 2026, which suggests the new models could still avoid a major increase.
However, Apple warned at the time that further price rises could follow, and some analysts expect higher component costs to result in a modest increase for the next Apple Watch generation.
Apple Watch Series 12 price prediction
We think the Series 12 could start at around $429, up from $399 for the Series 11, although this is a prediction rather than a firm rumor. A smaller increase — or no increase at all — remains possible.
The cellular version currently starts at $499 and would likely rise by a similar amount if Apple increases prices across the range.
Apple Watch Ultra 4 price prediction
There are fewer specific pricing rumors surrounding the Ultra 4, so the safest assumption is that it will remain close to the Ultra 3’s $799 starting price.
Apple could apply a modest increase here too, but there is currently little evidence pointing to a substantial Ultra price rise.
What about the Apple Watch SE?
An Apple Watch SE 4 is not expected in 2026, so the SE 3 should remain Apple’s entry-level model at or near its current $249 starting price.


						

							


Does it matter if these are only incremental updates?
Not necessarily. The Apple Watch is now a mature product, so Apple’s focus has increasingly shifted from major redesigns to smaller improvements in performance, battery life, connectivity, durability, and health features.
As we argued in July 2026, the Apple Watch doesn’t necessarily need another dramatic redesign or a flashy new feature. What matters more at this stage is a steady stream of quality-of-life improvements that make it more useful day to day.
That was also true of the previous generation. The Series 11 added 5G connectivity, better battery life and improved durability, while the Ultra 3 brought a slightly larger display and satellite connectivity. Neither was a radical reinvention, but both refined an already well-established design.
The Apple Watch’s overall look has changed relatively little since the Series 4 redesign in 2018, and that may be deliberate. For existing owners of a recent model, the Series 12 and Ultra 4 may not offer a compelling reason to upgrade. But for anyone coming from an older Apple Watch, several generations of incremental improvements can add up to a much more substantial upgrade.


						

							


Is Apple considering a circular Apple Watch design?
Yes — but that doesn’t mean one is likely to go on sale.
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported in August 2026 that Apple has explored several new wearable concepts, including circular displays similar to those used by the Google Pixel Watch and Samsung Galaxy Watch. Apple is also reportedly considering other ideas, such as screenless fitness trackers, as it looks for ways to reinvent its wearable lineup.
However, these concepts appear to be experimental and are not expected to arrive soon.
A circular Apple Watch would also involve significant compromises. The current rectangular design makes efficient use of screen space for text, apps and complications, while a round display would reduce usable area at the same overall width. That could also leave less internal room for components such as the battery and health sensors.
For those reasons, a round Apple Watch is best viewed as something Apple has explored rather than a likely future product.


						

							


Will Apple ever redesign the Apple Watch?
Almost certainly, but a major redesign may still be some way off.
Apple is reportedly experimenting with different form factors as competition in wearables grows, and Gurman has said the company is “determined to reinvent the lineup.” But the more radical ideas currently under consideration — including circular displays and screenless wearables — are said to be longer-term projects.
For now, Apple appears more likely to continue refining the existing rectangular Apple Watch design before making a more fundamental change.

title: Apple Announces Apple Watch Ultra 4 With Two-Day Battery Life and Upgraded Health Tracking
content:
Apple today announced the Apple Watch Ultra 4, featuring a new S11 chip, a redesigned health sensing system, and a larger battery that Apple says delivers two days of battery life.


With improved power efficiency, Ultra 4 offers up to 18 hours of workout tracking with full GPS and heart rate monitoring, or 45 hours in its maximum extended workout mode. It comes in Black and Natural titanium, alongside new band colors and a new titanium Hermès band.

The redesigned health sensing system features a larger electrode surface for improved skin contact during ECG readings, photodiodes arranged in a ring to capture light more efficiently, and larger, more power-efficient green LEDs for heart rate tracking.

More frequent readings are displayed in an updated Heart Rate app and new watch face complications. Apple says the system delivers the most accurate heart rate tracking of any wearable, citing a study involving hundreds of participants running, cycling, and performing HIIT workouts, with an ECG chest strap used as the reference.


A new Readiness feature analyzes recent activity, vitals, and sleep each morning to provide a score indicating whether users should recover, pace themselves, or take on more activity.

Apple is also redesigning the Health app to offer personalized guidance powered by Apple Intelligence. A new Health Age feature combines Apple Watch metrics such as VO2 max and sleep with blood test biomarkers to compare users' health indicators with their chronological age. A Longevity tab brings together insights across sleep, movement, heart health, and other areas.


Users can enter lab results manually or sync their medical records. In the U.S., Apple will also offer access to a Quest blood panel covering more than 50 biomarkers for $119. A new VO2 max test uses the iPhone's camera alongside Apple Watch to assess users as they perform a series of exercises, providing immediate results. The redesigned Health app is coming later this year.

The S11 chip's energy-efficient always-on processor enables new Audio Intelligence features. Sound Recognition identifies sounds such as alarms, doorbells, and a baby crying, while Live Rewind displays a transcript of what was said in the preceding 15 seconds.


Siri Recap generates titles, summaries, and key points from conversations for users to review in the Siri app. Users can schedule when it takes notes or toggle it in Control Center. Apple says the audio features do not create or store audio recordings. Siri Recap will launch in beta later this year, initially in English, with additional languages to follow.

title: Apple's A20 Pro is 40% faster, and offers improved thermal management
content:
Apple's iPhone 18 Pro offers a redesigned thermal system that's much larger and much better at dissipating heat generated by the powerful A20 Pro chip.


Apple's A20 Pro chip utilizes a new packaging method.
The A20 Pro features a six-core CPU with two super cores that are up to 20% faster, along with four efficiency cores. There's also a seven-core GPU for faster graphics rendering, offering up to a 40% increase in performance over the A19 Pro, along with a dual Neural Engine setup.
Apple has also redesigned the physical package of the silicon for the A20 Pro chip. Custom packaging, inspired by M-series chips, means that the A20 Pro silicon die is located side-by-side with the memory. Apple says this removes the memory from the thermal path of the system-on-chip and allows the chip to be connected directly to the improved vapor chamber.

title: iPhone 18 Pro & Max Guide: Everything you need to know about the new iPhones
content:
Macworld






Apple is unveiling the new iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max at an event. We are updating this article as the news breaks! 
New iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max features at a glance
A20 Pro performance: New six-core CPU with two “super cores” up to 20% faster, upgraded GPU, and neural accelerators with 2x faster 8-bit floating-point AI performance.
Much better cooling: A next-generation vapor chamber is three times larger than the iPhone 17 Pro’s and circulates deionized water to improve thermals.
Big battery gains: Apple claims up to 36 hours for iPhone 18 Pro and 45 hours for iPhone 18 Pro Max.
Improved 48MP camera: Variable aperture opens wider in low light, letting in around 50% more light and improving Night mode speed and quality.
Higher prices: iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199, while iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at $1,299, both $100 more than their predecessors.
The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Mac use the A20 Pro chip which has Apple’s latest six core CPU featuring two of our new super cores that are up to 20% faster and four efficiency cores, all integrated with neural accelerators that power low latency on device AI workloads as a significantly advanced GPU and a new version of the neural accelerators with 2x faster 8-bit floating point math. 
To keep cool, the iPhone 18 Pro has a next generation vapor chamber. It has three times the surface area as the one in iPhone 17 Pro. Deionized water is constantly cycled throughout the system for significantly improved thermals. 
Combined with the new chip’s efficiency, you’ll get 36 hours on the iPhone 18 Pro and an absolutely insane 45 hours on the 18 Pro Max. 
The 48MP Fusion Camera with variable aperture adjusts automatically based on the scene. When you’re in a darker environment, the aperture opens to let in around 50% more light, while night mode captures are faster with better quality.
The iPhone 18 Pro will cost from $1,199 (up from $1,099) while the the iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,299 (up from $1,199 for the iPhone 17 Pro Max).
The new iPhone 18 Pro also has a smaller Dynamic Island with space for three Live Activities at once, a large one in the middle and two smaller circles on either side. 
Read on to see the rumors from before the event while we update this article. 
The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are expected to launch at an Apple event on September 9, 2026 featuring several cutting-edge hardware advancements, including the debut of Apple’s C2 modem, and a shift to a 2nm manufacturing process for the A20 Pro chip. 
Other key rumored upgrades include a smaller Dynamic Island that will allow users to switch between three Live Activities at the top of the screen, rather than the two supported by current iPhones. While under-display Face ID components and camera improvements may include variable aperture on the Pro Max and enhanced sensors.
Alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max Apple is said to be planning to launch the ultra-premium folding iPhone – which it turns out could be called iPhone Duo. However, in a change to the usual schedule, the company is expected to shift the launch of the iPhone 18 spring 2027 to keep the spotlight on the Pro series during its traditional September debut.
Here’s a quick summary of what all the rumors and leaks say to expect from the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max in 2026.


What are the biggest upgrades for iPhone 18 Pro & Pro Max
Unveiling at Apple’s September 9 event
Smaller Dynamic Island, potentially with some Face ID components under the display
Variable-aperture main camera
A20 Pro chip built on TSMC’s 2nm process
Apple C2 cellular modem
New N2 wireless/networking chip
Larger battery, particularly on the Pro Max
Simplified Camera Control
Revised, more seamless rear Ceramic Shield design
Possible 5G satellite connectivity
Likely price increase due to soaring memory and component costs
How is iPhone 18 Pro/Max different from iPhone 17 Pro/Max?
Split release schedule (Pro first, base later)
Smaller or modified Dynamic Island
Some Face ID components moving under-display
New C2 modem 
Camera experimentation (rumored variable aperture on Pro Max)

 Comparing iPhone 18 Pro rumors to current iPhone 17 Pro






When will the new iPhones launch?
Apple has confirmed that it will hold an event on Wednesday, September 9, 2026, and new iPhones are highly likely to headline the event.
However, Apple is widely expected to change its usual release strategy this year. Multiple reports suggest suggest that only the premium models will arrive in September 2026: the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and a new foldable iPhone Ultra. 
The standard iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e and a second generation iPhone Air are instead expected in spring 2027. If accurate, this would represent the biggest shake-up to Apple’s iPhone launch schedule in years, creating separate autumn and spring release windows.
Evidence in iOS 27 beta 5 adds weight to those reports. System files reportedly reference six unreleased iPhones: the iPhone 18, iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone 18e, iPhone Air 2, and foldable iPhone Ultra. The references don’t reveal specifications, but they support the idea that Apple is preparing all six models while staggering their release dates. 
Availability could also be a problem. During Apple’s Q3 earnings call, then-CEO Tim Cook, now executive chairman, warned that the impact of supply constraints would “increase significantly.”
Apple is reportedly struggling to secure enough DRAM for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra, potentially limiting production ahead of launch. Processor wafers are said to be ready, but some are reportedly waiting for memory before they can be packaged and assembled.
That could leave the iPhone 18 Pro in short supply when it goes on sale, with longer shipping estimates possible. The lower-volume iPhone Ultra may be somewhat less affected.
Most likely: The iPhone 18 Pro, Pro Max, and foldable iPhone Ultra will launch in September 2026, while the iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, and iPhone Air 2 will follow in early 2027.

What will the iPhone 18 Pro/Max look like and what are the color choices?
The design of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max is said to resemble the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max, but some changes are predicted.
One possible change, shared by a Weibo leaker in September 2025, is a “slightly transparent” ceramic shield section on the back of Pro models. This glass/Ceramic Shield area around MagSafe is now rumored to become more frosted and visually seamless. 
Macworld contributor Filipe Esposito reported that a trusted source had revealed one of the new colorways for the iPhone 18 Pro to be Dark Cherry, replacing the iPhone 17 Pro’s Cosmic Orange option.
Recent rumors claimed that the new phones will be significantly thicker than previous models, but all the evidence we have seen says that’s not the case, including case maker Otter Box confidently listing their iPhone 17 Pro cases as fitting the iPhone 18 Pro. Instead, we expect the body to have about the same thickness as the iPhone 17 Pro/Max but with a thicker camera bump area.
Another report suggests that the Camera Control on the side of the iPhone will be pressure sensing instead of a touch-sensing layer. This redesign is said to be aimed at reducing the cost and complexity.  
A recent ransomware attack against an Apple parts supplier included images from an iPhone 18 Pro “drop test” and other parts, and they corroborate prior rumors about the overall shape and design of the phone, which is broadly the same as the iPhone 17 Pro.
Other shades are said to include: Light Blue, Dark Gray, and Silver. There was also a coffee shade rumored (via Digital Chat Station). 

 
 @macworld.com 
iPhone 18 Pro colors revealed! #iphone #apple
 ♬ original sound – Macworld – Macworld 
  




As with the iPhone 17 Pro, there will be no black option, according to Instant Digital.
Screen sizes are expected to remain at 6.3 and 6.9 inches. The Pro models will also retain the wider three-camera raised plateau.
If you are hoping for a more dramatic redesign, the iPhone Ultra may have more appeal. Alternatively, you could wait for the 20th anniversary iPhone which is rumored to have a “radically different design“. Reports point to a curved, near-bezel-free display, possible solid-state haptic buttons, a thinner and brighter OLED panel, and potentially under-display Face ID and camera hardware coming in fall 2027.
Most likely: Design changes will be minimal, with the biggest visible differences limited to colors and subtle refinements.


						

							


What’s new with the iPhone 18 Pro/Max camera?

				
					

				
			
Eugen Wegmann




Apple may introduce variable aperture technology to the 48MP main camera on the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max (potentially only the Pro Max), allowing mechanical control over light intake and depth of field. This has long been a perk limited to high-end professional cameras.
If the rumor (from Digital Chat Station on Weibo), and later corroborated by Mark Gurman on September 9, is true, iPhone users will be able to mechanically control how much light reaches the sensor for the first time, allowing more control over depth of field and sharpness. This could elevate portrait shots by improving the applied depth of field effect, as well as minimizing overexposure.
Wider telephoto apertures on the Pro models should also result in better low-light performance.
For some time (since January 2025) Samsung has been said to be working on a new three-layer stacked camera sensor called ‘PD-TR-Logic,’ and this could appear in the iPhone 18 series. This image sensor is expected to enhance the camera’s responsiveness, while also offering advantages such as reduced photo noise, improved dynamic range. The main Wide camera sensor is expected to be larger than usual, which offers many benefits.
The front-facing camera may also get an upgrade beyond the rumored changes to the housing (as discussed elsewhere the selfie camera may be housed in a smaller hole-punch cut out, reducing the size of the Dynamic Island). The iPhone 17 generation features 18MP sensors for the selfie camera, but this may increase to 24MP in the next generation, according to leaker WhyLab on Weibo.
More megapixels would lead to improved video calls and better low-light performance. 
Most likely: Incremental improvements, with a new variable aperture feature on the Pro Max.


						

							


Will the iPhone 18 Pro/Max Dynamic Island or front camera change?

				
					

				
			
Britta O’Boyle




Apple hasn’t changed the Dynamic Island since the iPhone 14 Pro, but the iPhone 18 Pro may introduce some adjustments.
Some reports suggest Apple could move certain Face ID components under the display, allowing the Dynamic Island to shrink. This is not expected to mean that the entire Face ID system will be hidden beneath the screen. 
A report in December 2025 from Weibo account “Smart Pikachu” claimed that Apple was testing an under-display “micro-transparent glass panel” for some Face ID sensors. That could allow Apple to reduce the size of the Dynamic Island on the iPhone 18 Pro.
Later reports, however, suggest that full under-display Face ID is not expected yet. Instead, Apple may move only some of the sensors or emitters used by Face ID beneath the display, while other components remain visible within a smaller Dynamic Island.
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman has also reported that Apple plans to “shrink” the Dynamic Island on future iPhone models, adding weight to the idea that Apple is redesigning or relocating some of the components currently housed within it.
On the morning of September 9, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman published a report claiming that the smaller Dynamic Island will let users toggle between three live tasks, versus the current limit of two Live Activities.
A spy shot published in March by noted leaker IceUniverse on X gives us a view of how much smaller the Dynamic Island could be.

				
					

				
			
IceUniverse/X




There have been conflicting claims that the position of the front-facing camera may also change: 
In December 2025 The Information claimed Apple will put the Face ID sensors under the display, and move the front camera to the upper left corner in a punch-hole design. This would make the iPhone 18 Pro/ Max the first iPhones with a front camera in the corner.
However, Prominent leaker account Instant Digital said on Weibo in January 2026 that front camera claim was based on a mistranslation, and only the infrared sensor moves under the display. Leakers ShrimpApplePro and Ross Young of DSCC corroborated Instant Digital’s claims.
Most likely: A smaller Dynamic Island, with some Face ID hardware moved under the display, rather than fully under-display Face ID.


						

							


Will the iPhone 18 Pro/Max display change?

				
					

				
			
Stephan Wiesend




Screen sizes should be consistent with the 6.3 and 6.9-inch displays on the current models, but reports suggest a massive jump in brightness from the current 1600 nits HDR and 3,000 nits peak. 
According to Weibo leaker, Instant Digital, Chinese supplier BOE has revealed that Apple is targeting unprecedentedly high brightness requirements for the display. The Elec corroborated this, claiming BOE is struggling with iPhone OLED production so panel orders have been shifted to Samsung Display.
Most likely: An increase in brightness is expected, but there are no details yet on the extent of the improvement.


						

							


How powerful will the A20 Pro chip in the iPhone 18 Pro/Max be?
The iPhone 18 Pro and Max are expected to use a new A20 Pro chip, built on TSMC’s N2 (2nm) process. The move to a smaller manufacturing process should allow Apple to pack in more transistors, with TSMC claiming up to 15% better performance or 30% lower power consumption compared with its previous-generation technology.
A September 2026 leak suggests the A20 Pro could feature a 7-core GPU, up from six cores in the A19 Pro, while retaining a six-core CPU with two performance and four efficiency cores.
Perhaps more significant is the rumored move to a 96-bit LPDDR5x memory interface, 50% wider than the A19 Pro’s 64-bit interface. Combined with possible clock-speed and architectural improvements, we estimate that GPU performance could rise by around 20–30%, benefiting local AI workloads, 3D games and other graphics-intensive apps.
The A20 is also rumored to use Wafer-Level Multi-Chip Module (WMCM) packaging, integrating the RAM more closely with the SoC. That could improve memory bandwidth and latency, while potentially reducing power consumption.
Apple could also borrow ideas from its M-series chips, with speculation that the A20 may introduce higher-performance “super cores” similar to those used in the M5.
Apple introduced vapor-chamber cooling with the iPhone 17 Pro generation, spreading heat away from the processor more efficiently than the older graphite-based system. Gurman’s report on the morning of September 9, referrs to an updated vapor chamber cooling system alongside the A20 Pro that should allow the A20 Pro sustain its performance without getting too hot. 
Most likely: A substantial underlying upgrade in performance, graphics and efficiency, although many of the improvements may be more noticeable in demanding games and AI features than in everyday use.


						

							


Will iPhone 18 Pro/Max battery life improve?
Apple works to make battery life as long as possible every year, especially in the Pro model iPhones. 
A July report claimed that the battery capacity of the iPhone 18 Pro Max will have a battery capacity of 5,235 mAh on the Nano SIM model and 5,425 mAh on the eSIM-only version. That’s about 6-8% more capacity than the current model. Further reports have puts the U.S. eSIM iPhone 18 Pro Max at 5,567mAh. 
The “Pro Max” variant of the iPhone gets a higher-capacity battery nearly every year, usually a couple hundred mAh more, thanks to better internal design and improving battery chemistry and manufacturing techniques. But battery life is a function of more than just battery capacity—the power use of the processor, display, and wireless radios all play an important point.
We think it’s likely the iPhone 18 Pro/Max will have higher-capacity batteries, and battery life at least as long as the iPhone 17 Pro/Max. But a significantly longer battery life is hard to predict.


						

							


Will connectivity improve (5G, Wi-Fi, satellite) with iPhone 18 Pro/Max?
C2 and N2 chip rumors. 
iPhone 18 Pro models are rumored to feature the second generation of Apple’s in-house 5G modem, the C2 chip. 
The C2 hasn’t launched yet, but it is expected to replace Qualcomm modems in at least some iPhone 18 Pro models. Qualcomm hardware may still be used in certain markets, depending on regional and carrier requirements:
Better power efficiency
Faster and more reliable 5G performance
Improved mmWave support
There are also reports that the new iPhone will gain full satellite internet support, expanding beyond emergency use. In October 2025, The Information claimed that Apple is gearing up to support 5G networks that are served from satellites. 
While the iPhone has offered satellite connectivity for emergency situations for years, if this rumor is true it would allow the iPhone 18 models to have full internet access via satellite, not just emergency services.
As of April 2026, Apple and Amazon have agreed to team up to provide future satellite service support. Early in April, Amazon announced that it had agreed to acquire Globalstar, who was the provider of iPhone and Apple Watch satellite connectivity (that merger is expected to close in 2027) So now iPhones and Apple Watches will now fall under Amazon Leo, Amazon’s satellite internet network.
The Wi-Fi/Bluetooth chip is less certain. Apple debuted its N1 local networking chip in the iPhone 17 line, supporting Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread networking.
Earlier in 2026, analyst Jeff Pu said that the iPhone 18 Pro models will introduce a next-generation N2 chip, but leaks of a iPhone 18 Pro motherboard in July 2026 suggested Apple could retain the N1 for another generation. There is little information about what an N2 would add beyond the capabilities of the N1.
Most likely: An incremental upgrade to wireless performance, reliability and efficiency rather than a major new connectivity feature.


						

							


How much will the iPhone 18 Pro/Max cost?
With Apple increasing prices for Macs and iPads in June due to high memory and chip costs, and the iPhone 18 Pro models are also expected to become more expensive.
In August, Mark Gurman described iPhone price increases as “inevitable” as Apple faces rising memory and component costs. 
As of September 9, Gurman is reporting that Apple plans to increase both Pro models by $100.
A roughly $100 increase may be the most plausible outcome. Google and Samsung have both raised flagship prices by about $100, potentially setting a benchmark Apple may be reluctant to exceed. That could put the iPhone 18 Pro at around $1,199 and the Pro Max at $1,299.
Apple could also absorb some of the higher costs itself. Recent warnings about pressure on gross margins suggest the company may accept lower profitability rather than pass the full increase on to customers.
More pessimistic estimates are higher. IDC has suggested increases of up to $200 for the Pro models, while analyst Jeff Pu has indicated that prices could rise by as much as $250 to $300.
The rumored folding iPhone could further reshape the top end of Apple’s pricing, with reports suggesting a starting price of $1,999 or more.
Most likely: A price rise of around $100 for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, although larger increases remain possible if component costs stay elevated.
