 FAQ 


1.
When is the new iPhone coming out?
The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are expected to be unveiled at Apple’s September 9, 2026 event, with preorders likely shortly afterward (estimates suggest September 12) and availability around mid-September (estimates suggest September 18). The standard iPhone 18, however, is expected to arrive in spring 2027.





2.
Will the iPhone 18 Pro have under-display Face ID?
Probably not fully. Current rumors suggest the iPhone 18 Pro may move some Face ID components beneath the display, allowing Apple to shrink the Dynamic Island. However, the complete Face ID system is not expected to go under-display yet.





3.
What chip will power the iPhone 18 Pro?
Apple is expected to use the A20 Pro chip in the iPhone 18 Pro.





4.
Is Apple changing its iPhone release schedule in 2026?
Apple is said to be planning to launch the Pro iPhone models, including a foldable iPhone in September 2026. The iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e may not arrive until spring 2027. 





5.
What camera upgrades are rumored for the iPhone 18 Pro Max?
Apple is rumored to be focusing on advanced lens technology and sensor improvements for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max. One prominent rumor is the introduction of a variable-aperture system in the Pro Max.

content:
Apple today introduced AirPods 5, bringing Active Noise Cancellation to its entry-level wireless earbuds at a starting price of $129.

 
Apple says AirPods 5 remove up to 50% more external noise than AirPods 4 with Active Noise Cancellation. A redesigned acoustic architecture and updated Adaptive EQ also promise richer, more detailed sound, while an improved Transparency mode makes nearby voices and sounds more natural.

Both models include Adaptive Audio, which automatically blends noise cancellation and Transparency mode, and Conversation Awareness, which lowers playback volume when the wearer starts speaking. Live Translation is also supported when paired with a compatible iPhone with Apple Intelligence enabled.

A $149 version with a Wireless Charging Case adds swipe-based volume controls on the stems and longer battery life. Apple says this model delivers up to five hours of listening with noise cancellation enabled, or up to 22 hours with the case, which supports Apple Watch and Qi chargers alongside USB-C.

title: Both iPhone 18 Pro Models Feature Variable Aperture Camera
content:
Apple has revealed at its "Surprise and Shine" event that both iPhone 18 Pro models will be equipped with a variable aperture camera.


Prior to this announcement, some rumours suggested that only the iPhone 18 Pro Max would feature a variable aperture lens, but it seems that both models will benefit from the technology.

Apple says it has developed a system of six laser-cut blades, each thinner than a human hair, to create the aperture lens. The blades are made of a specialized polymer composite for the right balance of mass flexibility and durability.

The aperture adjusts automatically based on the scene. When you're in a darker environment, for example, the aperture opens to let in around 50% more light.

It also allows you to capture cinematic mode effects from regular video after you capture, plus it now supports 60 frames per second for a half-speed effect.

"iPhone 18 Pro has a new 48 megapixel fusion main camera with variable aperture for creative control that wasn't possible before," said Apple. "This is the most advanced camera we've ever made."

title: Apple Unveils A20 Pro as First 2nm Smartphone Chip
content:
Apple today revealed the A20 Pro chip in the iPhone 18 Pro and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max, built on a brand new architecture using 2nm process technology.


Apple described the A20 Pro as "an exceptional chip that sets a new bar for mobile computing." The chip has a 6-core CPU design with two new super cores that Apple says are up to 20% faster, calling them "desktop class" and "the fastest in any smartphone," alongside four new efficiency cores.

The GPU has also been redesigned with a 7-core layout that Apple says delivers up to 40% faster graphics performance and increased memory bandwidth. New neural accelerators built into the GPU offer twice the FP8 performance of the previous generation, which helps the chip run large language models locally on the device.

The A20 Pro features an additional Neural Engine, bringing the total core count to 32. The company says the redesigned Neural Engine delivers 2x the compute of its predecessor, is more efficient, and now supports 8-bit floating point math. Apple called the A20 Pro "the ultimate chip for running advanced on-device models," adding that it ships with "the widest memory interface we've ever shipped in an iPhone."

The company said effective thermal management in the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ is critical to unlocking the chip's maximum performance, since efficient heat dissipation determines how much of that performance can be sustained. To support this, Apple redesigned the chip's silicon packaging, describing it as "custom packaging inspired by our M-series chips" that connects the silicon and memory directly to the vapor chamber for improved thermal performance.

title: Apple Announces iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max
content:
Apple today unveiled the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, which look very similar to the iPhone 17 Pro models but have several upgrades.


iPhone 18 Pro still has a 6.3-inch display, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max sticks with a 6.9-inch display. As was widely rumored, both devices have a smaller Dynamic Island that can show up to three Live Activities at once.

The devices are equipped with the A20 Pro chip and feature longer battery life. Apple says the iPhone 18 Pro matches the battery life of the iPhone 17 Pro Max with up to 24 hours of typical usage per full charge, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max has the biggest generational leap in battery life ever with up to 30 hours of usage per charge.

Apple says the iPhone 18 Pro can charge to 50% in just 15 minutes.

A20 Pro has a 6-core GPU, a 7-core GPU, and a 32-core Neural Engine. Apple says sustained performance is up to 40% faster compared to the A19 Pro chip.

The vapor chamber cooling system is three times as large in the iPhone 18 Pro models as it is in the iPhone 17 Pro models for improved thermal management.

Six laser-cut blades smoothly transition between different apertures, making it incredibly easy to capture the best shot by automatically adjusting for depth of field and lighting. Combined with a new sensor that improves image quality, the result is better low-light photography, crisper detail in the back of group photos, and more unique shots.
With a new computational imaging pipeline, Apple says the Main camera produces sharper, more detailed shots, while upgraded Photographic Styles with new texture and grain controls let users further dial in their desired appearance.

iPhone 18 Pro color options include Black, Silver, Glacier, and Burgundy. The rear aluminum and Ceramic Shield glass area are now more color matched.

In the U.S., the iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199, and the iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at $1,299. For the first time, a 2TB storage capacity is available.

title: Touchscreen MacBook, HomePad, Apple TV are coming, but probably not today
content:
Macworld





It’s “Surprise and Shine” day today! It’s been previously reported that Apple has a release schedule chock-full of products for the rest of this year. It starts today with new iPhones, AirPods, and Apple Watches.
What about the other rumored products, like the touchscreen MacBook, or the updated HomePod and the home hub? Well, before you shrug and exclaim, “That’s it?” at the end of today’s event, you should know that’s not it, according to a post by Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman.


IF you don't see the Apple TV, HomePod mini, home display and touch MacBook today, don't worry. It's only September.
— Mark Gurman (@markgurman) September 9, 2026





If you’re not familiar with Gurman’s work, he has very good sources and his reporting tends to be spot on. Of all the people who report Apple leaks, he’s the most reliable. So while Gurman doesn’t directly say it, the touchscreen MacBook, HomePod mini, home hub (that he called “home display”), and Apple TV will be coming later this year.
Apple has held October and November releases before, so it’s not unprecedented. By the sound of his post, Gurman likely knows more about these releases, but he’s going to save reporting on those for later. After all, he has to save some surprises for his weekly newsletter so you’ll want to read it.
Those are products for another day. We have “Surprise and Shine” today, and you can track the event through the Macworld live blog, if you are unable to watch it.

title: Mac Mini vs. Mac Studio Buyer's Guide: 20 Differences Compared
content:
Apple announced new Mac mini and Mac Studio models last month, with both available to pre-order now. It is the first time in years that Apple has revised its two desktop Macs simultaneously, so which should you choose?


There are now two desktop Macs to choose from following the discontinuation of the Mac Pro, but the prices have moved sharply. The ‌Mac Studio‌ starts at $2,499 and rises to $5,499 for the M5 Ultra model, while the ‌Mac mini‌ starts at $899 with the M6 chip and $1,699 with the M5 Pro.

iPad increases Apple made in June, which took the ‌Mac mini‌ from $599 to $799, the M4 Pro configuration from $1,399 to $1,599, and the ‌Mac Studio‌ from $1,999 to $2,499. The M5 Ultra adds a further $200 to the post-June M3 Ultra price, putting it $1,500 above what the M3 Ultra cost at launch.

Our guide helps to answer the question of how to decide which of these two desktop Macs is best for you. The two machines now share a large number of key features, including:
 

A boxy silver aluminum enclosure with no color options

Apple's N1 chip, bringing Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 to both machines for the first time

Neural Accelerators built into every GPU core

Hardware-accelerated ray tracing

A Media Engine with hardware-accelerated H.264, HEVC, ProRes, and ProRes RAW, plus AV1 decode

A next-generation SSD architecture that Apple says is up to twice as fast as before

Genlock support over USB-C for synchronizing a display with a camera, including the iPhone 17 Pro

An HDMI port with multichannel audio output

A 3.5mm headphone jack with support for high-impedance headphones



Beyond that, the two lines diverge on chip generation, memory capacity, ports, and external display support.

Most customers should choose the M5 Pro ‌Mac mini‌ over the M5 Max ‌Mac Studio‌, saving $800 on the base models. The gap widens across custom configurations, since the ‌Mac Studio‌'s memory and storage tiers start higher and climb further.
 
Apple's first 2nm chip. Its Dual 16-core Neural Engine, which Apple says system frameworks can drive simultaneously, is also more Neural Engine hardware than either the M5 Pro or the M5 Max provides. If your workload leans on on-device machine learning rather than sustained CPU or GPU throughput, the cheapest Mac in this comparison is not obviously the weakest one for the task. The trade-offs are Thunderbolt 4 rather than Thunderbolt 5, a 32GB memory and 2TB storage ceiling, and a single video encode engine.
 
M5 Ultra is Apple's first quad-die M-series chip, and its four ProRes engines, four video encode engines, and 1.2TB/s of memory bandwidth are aimed squarely at multi-stream video work and large local AI models. The 512GB memory ceiling has no equivalent anywhere else in the Mac lineup, and it is what allows models with hundreds of billions of parameters to run entirely on device.
 
The ‌Mac Studio‌ still has a superior selection of ports, with four rear Thunderbolt 5 ports on the M5 Max and six in total on the M5 Ultra, plus an SDXC card slot, USB-A, and 10Gb Ethernet as standard. This makes a practical difference for anyone working off fast external storage or camera media. The ‌Mac mini‌ has closed part of the distance by moving to 2.5Gb Ethernet as standard, up from Gigabit.

Clustering over Thunderbolt 5 and RDMA is not a point of difference between the two machines, since it arrived in macOS 26.2 last December and works on any Mac with Thunderbolt 5, including the M5 Pro ‌Mac mini‌ and the previous-generation ‌Mac Studio‌. The exception is the M6 ‌Mac mini‌, which has Thunderbolt 4 and cannot take part.
 
reach 165Hz at 4K, up from 144Hz on the M4 generation, and the M5 Pro model drives all three through a single Thunderbolt port. For a three-display desk setup at high refresh rates, the M5 Pro ‌Mac mini‌ is sufficient. It is only above three displays, or at 6K and 8K, that the ‌Mac Studio‌ becomes necessary.
 
A notable exception arises at the top of the ‌Mac mini‌ lineup. An M5 Pro ‌Mac mini‌ configured with additional memory and storage moves close enough to the $2,499 ‌Mac Studio‌ that the comparison changes somewhat. For an increment of a few hundred dollars, the ‌Mac Studio‌ substitutes a chip with roughly twice the memory bandwidth, a second video encode engine, far greater display support, and headroom to 128GB of unified memory. If you are already spending heavily on a ‌Mac mini‌, price the ‌Mac Studio‌ before committing.
 
If you plan to keep the machine for many years, the ‌Mac Studio‌'s ceiling matters more than its starting price, because it is the only one of the two that can be configured beyond 64GB of unified memory. Buyers weighing the M6 ‌Mac mini‌ against the M5 Pro ‌Mac mini‌ should note that the newer chip generation and the newer process node both sit in the cheaper machine, and that the M5 Pro's advantages are concentrated in multi-core and graphics performance rather than in longevity.

An M6 ‌Mac mini‌ paired with a ‌Studio Display‌ comes to $2,498, a dollar less than a bare M5 Max ‌Mac Studio‌ with nothing to plug into. title: Apple Event Today: 20 Last-Minute 'iPhone Duo' and iPhone 18 Pro Rumors
content:
Apple will be holding an event today starting at 10 a.m. Pacific Time, with the company expected to unveil its first-ever foldable iPhone, the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4, AirPods 5, and potentially more. Below, we have recapped 20 last-minute rumors about these devices.


All of the details below were reported by Bloomberg's Mark Gurman today.

Apple's foldable iPhone will be named iPhone Duo.

  
iPhone Duo will have Apple Pencil support.

  
iPhone Duo shipments to customers will begin as early as October. It is unclear if pre-orders will begin earlier.

  
iPhone Duo color options: white and dark blue.

  
iPhone Duo starts with 256GB of storage. U.S. pricing will start at around $1,999.

  
iPhone Duo will have Apple's A20 Pro chip and C2 modem for 5G.

  
iPhone Duo will have dual rear 48-megapixel cameras. No Telephoto camera.

  
iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max special color: dark red.

  
iPhone 18 Pro models will have longer battery life — the Pro Max especially.

  
iPhone 18 Pro models will have an improved vapor chamber system to reduce overheating.

  
At least one iPhone 18 Pro model's camera will have variable aperture for greater control over depth of field.

  
In the U.S., iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max starting prices will be $100 higher compared to iPhone 17 Pro models. This means the iPhone 18 Pro would start at $1,199, and the iPhone 18 Pro Max would start at $1,299.

  
iPhone 18 Pro's smaller Dynamic Island can show three Live Activities, up from two.

  
Do not expect a regular iPhone 18 model to be announced today, as Apple reportedly plans to launch that device in the first quarter of 2027.

  
Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 models will have new case color options.

  
Apple Watch Series 12 will have a ceramic case option.

  
Apple Watch Ultra 4 will have longer battery life compared to the Ultra 3.

  
An all-new Readiness app for the Apple Watch will be announced today.

  
The new Apple Watch models will offer a new daily summary feature.

  
AirPods 5 will be unveiled today — with and without active noise cancellation.

title: Surprise and Shine Apple iPhone event live blog: Latest updates

Macworld





Apple’s “Surprise and Shine” event might be the most anticipated iPhone keynote in 10 years. It all kicks off today, and like you, we can’t wait! So join us as we count down the hours and minutes with all the latest rumors, leaks, and speculation leading up to the big event on Wednesday, September 9, at 10 am PT.
Surprise and Shine iPhone event: How to watch
You can watch the full keynote right here using the embedded YouTube link below or on Apple.com on your iPhone or Mac. The “Watch Now” tab in the TV app on the Apple TV will also show the stream live.






Surprise and Shine iPhone event: What we expect
Apple might have dubbed this the “Surprise” event, but we have a pretty good idea what Apple is going to announce. Here’s what we expect to see:
iPhone Ultra: Apple is almost certain to launch its first folding phone this week. We’re expecting a passport-style design with a 5.5-inch cover display and a near-8-inch inner display when opened.
iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max: We expect a similar design with a faster chip and a better camera system, possibly including a variable-aperture lens for the first time.
Apple Watch Series 12: The latest Apple Watch update will reportedly be a minor refresh with a new chip, all-day heart-rate tracking, and maybe the return of a ceramic finish.
Apple Watch Ultra 4: Like the Series 12, the Ultra 4 is expected to be a minor refresh largely focused on a new chip tuned for Siri AI.
AirPods 5: Apple is rumored to be launching a new pair of low-end AirPods, but we don’t know much about them.
Smart home: It’s less likely that Apple’s rumored smart-home hub arrives at this event, but we could see an updated Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini.

We discussed this on the podcast, and figured it would be a nice moment if new CEO John Ternus got the chance to utter those immortal words as part of his debut. The most obvious product to get the One More Thing treatment is the iPhone Ultra, but a bigger surprise would be the arrival of Apple’s long-rumored smart home hub. Either would work.

When Apple (allegedly) unveils its first folding iPhone tomorrow, Greg Joswiak or whomever gets the honor of announcing the phone on the stream, will talk about the displays, interface, cameras, design, and anything else Apple feels is worth highlighting. What they probably won’t spend a lot of time talking about is the crease.
Ever since Samsung’s first folding phone arrived, the center display crease has been an issue. It’s gotten better over the years, but it’s still the biggest hurdle for new customers to overcome. Even on the newest phones, you can see it when it’s opened and feel a little valley while using it. It’s flies in the face of Apple’s pursuit of perfection and likely the reason why we haven’t gotten a folding iPhone until now.
Earlier this year, it was reported that Apple had devised a way to overcome the crease with a combination of ultra-thin glass (UTG) and an optically clear adhesive that allows “the folding area to be locally thinned at the bending axis to improve bendability.” Samsung’s newest flagship phone features a display with a 60-micrometer UTG layer, which is likely a similar material to what Apple will use. 
No folding phone has been able to completely eliminate the crease. Will Apple be the first?

title: The folding iPhone will support Apple Pencil after all, sources claim
content:
Macworld





A week or so ago, the Bloomberg leaker Mark Gurman made a bold claim: Apple had, “with zero doubt,” been testing and prototyping a new, stubbier version of the Apple Pencil for its upcoming foldable iPhone. Considering that the company has sold phones for 19 years and styluses for 11 years but has never brought the two things together, this seemed surprising. Some might even say a colossal mistake. But at least the idea was just that: an idea, tested for a while and probably discarded.
But hang on for a minute, because today, at the very last minute, Gurman has posted another article about Apple’s Surprise and Shine press event. And he now insists that the folding iPhone (or iPhone Duo, as he’s now calling it) will indeed be compatible with the Apple Pencil.
It’s important to note that Gurman’s latest prediction, in his own words, is merely that the iPhone Duo will have “support for the Apple Pencil stylus.” If Apple still plans to launch a special edition of the stylus, he doesn’t mention this. From the sound of this the inclusion of Apple Pencil support would be very much optional; a nice-to-have rather than an integral feature. Which sounds like something nobody could be against, right?
Except the screen, which is already a source of concern because of the dangers of a visible crease, will need the additional tech to support stylus input, and as Gurman himself has pointed out, that could result in visible marks. And the iPhone Ultra/Duo won’t be the right size for a standard-issue Apple Pencil to attach magnetically along one side, which creates all sorts of storage and charging headaches. All this to support an accessory most people won’t use.
To be fair, the foldable iPhone, when unfolded, will be more akin to a tablet than a smartphone. (Its expected screen size is virtually identical to the original iPad mini.) So there may be some demand for stylus support. It’s just hard to feel positive about what seems like a half-hearted approach to the matter. Either you do Apple Pencil support properly, with a dedicated version of the stylus that actually fits, or you don’t bother.
Then again, the Pencil gets the briefest of snippets in Gurman’s report, so perhaps there’s more to the story than he’s letting on. You can follow all the latest breaking news as we lead up to today’s announcement with our Apple event live blog.

title: iPhone 18 Pro Could Charge 25% Faster
content:
Code found in iOS 27 suggests the iPhone 18 Pro and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max could support a 33% higher charging rate than the iPhone 17 Pro models, according to a new discovery from the leaker known as "pdfu."


The findings apparently come from Apple's charging optimizer settings buried in ‌iOS 27‌, which show the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max charging at a rate 33% higher than the iPhone 17 lineup. If Apple can maintain that higher rate throughout a charge, pdfu estimates it could cut around 25% off the time it takes to complete a typical fast-charging session.

Apple's first foldable iPhone does not appear to get the same treatment. The same code purportedly shows it charging at the same rate as the ‌iPhone 17‌ and ‌iPhone 17 Pro‌, rather than the faster rate expected for the new Pro models.

iPhone 18 is said to match the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ faster charging, while the iPhone 18e is said to see an even bigger jump of around 69% over the current iPhone 17e. The iPhone Air 2 is said to charge about 27% faster than today's ‌iPhone Air‌.

Actual charging speeds depend on a multitude of real-world factors, such as the phone's temperature and how full the battery already is, so the improvement buyers notice day-to-day could end up being smaller than the numbers suggest.

title: Apple’s September iPhone event: Date, time, and what will launch
content:
Macworld





Apple has confirmed that it will hold an event on Wednesday September 9, starting at 1pm ET, 10am PT and 6pm BST. We expect that Apple will take the wraps off the new iPhone 18 Pro, new iPhone Duo and new Apple Watches during the keynote.
Read on to find out everything you need to know about Apple’s iPhone launch event for 2026, including when the Apple Event will start where you are, and the new products Apple will launch. You will be able to watch the event below once it starts. We will also run a live blog.
When is Apple’s iPhone event? What time will the iPhone event start?
The 2026 iPhone event will take place on Wednesday 9 September. It starts at the following times depending on where you are: 

U.S.: 10 a.m. (PDT), 11 a.m. (MDT), 12 p.m. (CDT), 1 p.m. (EDT)
U.K.: 6 p.m. (BST)
Europe: 7 p.m. (CEST) 8 p.m. (EEST)
Canada: 10 a.m. (PDT), 11 a.m. (MDT), 12 p.m. (CDT), 1 p.m. (EDT), 2 p.m. (ADT)
India: 10.30 p.m. (IST)
Hong Kong, Singapore and China: The following day at 1 a.m.
Australia: The following day at 1 a.m. (AWST), 2.30 a.m. (ACST), 3 a.m. (AEST)
New Zealand: The following day at 5 a.m. (NZST)
You can watch the event live on Apple’s website or YouTube stream below. We also have a live blog of the iPhone Event so you can see our analysis of the annoucements as they happen: 






Apple’s September events are usually one to two hours long.
This will be the first Apple event hosted by the company’s new CEO, John Ternus, who took over from Tim Cook on September 1 following Cook’s retirement.
What will Apple launch at the September 2026 event?
Apple’s September events typically feature the launch of new iPhones, Apple Watches, and, sometimes, AirPods. Apple’s September 2026 event is shaping up to be one of its most significant in years, with a mix of expected updates and a major new product category: 
The Headliner: iPhone Duo or iPhone Ultra (Foldable)
The biggest news is the long-rumored folding iPhone, initially expected to be called the iPhone Ultra until Mark Gurman revealed the possibility that it could be called iPhone Duo on the morning of the event. This marks Apple’s first major form-factor change in over a decade. According to reports, it will fold like a book, have a passport-like shape when closed, and feature a starting price of $2,000 or more . It’s expected to include two rear cameras (wide and ultrawide), a front-facing camera, and the return of Touch ID built into the side button. Read more here: Folding iPhone rumors.
iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max
Alongside the Ultra/Duo, Apple is expected to launch the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max . These models are rumored to feature a smaller Dynamic Island, an upgraded A20 Pro processor with revamped vapor-chamber cooling, a new C2 modem (or Qualcomm in the U.S.), and a new “Dark Cherry” signature color. Camera improvements are also expected, including a variable aperture and new sensor technology, along with a potential boost to 24 megapixels for the front-facing camera. Read more here:  iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max rumors.
Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4
As is tradition, Apple will update its smartwatch lineup alongside the new iPhones. The Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 are expected to be announced . However, reports suggest these will be relatively minor updates, primarily featuring a faster S12 processor and a few internal upgrades, with no major new health sensors or design changes expected. Read about the Apple Watch Series 12 rumors. 
Apple TV 4K and HomePod Mini
Both the Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini are long overdue for an update and are expected to launch this fall. The delay has reportedly been due to Apple waiting for the new Siri AI architecture to be ready. The new models are expected to feature more powerful chips (like the A17 Pro in the Apple TV) to support the full Siri AI experience, enabling more contextual and conversational interactions. Read about Apple’s HomePod plans.
AirPods 5
It is possible that new AirPods could be announced at Apple’s event. They are expected to offer the H3 chip, improvements to audio/ANC and possibly new health sensing such as temperature monitoring. There are also rumors that camera-equipped AirPods are in the pipeline, but we don’t expect these at the September event. 
Software
Apple is also likely to announce the date when it will release the new iOS 27 and watchOS 27 operating systems, most likely a few days after the event. iPadOS 27 and the new macOS Golden Gate may launch alongside iOS 27, but there have been years when these updates were available later. Apple is also likely to reveal when the next updates to tvOS and HomePod software will be available. 
Release dates: New OS download dates
The following launch dates are likely to be announced at the iPhone 17 event:
Monday, September 14: Downloads begin for iOS 26. If you do want to update your iPhone and you are looking for advice on how to install it read: How to update iOS on your iPhone.
Friday, September 11 or Saturday, September 12: iPhone 18 Pro and new Apple Watch preorders begin.
Friday, September 18: iPhone 18 Pro and new Apple Watch models are available for purchase.
Where to watch the iPhone event
Apple will broadcast the event live on its website, the TV app, and on Apple’s YouTube channel. If you want to refresh your memory, the 2025 keynote event is embedded above.
Will the iPhone event be live?
Apple hasn’t held a truly live event since September 2019. Instead, it shows a prerecorded video at the time a live event would be and often holds a small hands-on area to showcase the new products. It is likely that this will once again be the case in 2026, with members of the press gathering at Apple Park to watch the same video Apple will show to the rest of the world.
Interested to find out what won’t launch at the September event? Read: The iPhone event is September 9. The iPhone you want might not be there.
What won’t Apple launch at the September 2026 event?
Apple isn’t expected to unveil the standard iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, second-generation iPhone Air, or Apple Watch SE 4 at its September 2026 event. Those products are reportedly being held back for later launches, with the new iPhones expected in spring 2027.

title: Is the Apple Store down? Here’s why
content:
Macworld





When the Apple Store goes offline it’s usually an indication that Apple is about to launch a new product. Sometimes it’s for less good reasons, like an Apple event and an iPhone launch, as is the case this time.
Why is the Apple Store down?
Are you having trouble browsing the Apple Store online? There are a few reasons why the Apple Store might be offline. It could be because Apple is preparing to launch new products at an event, or it could be because Apple is about to start taking pre-orders for a new product. 
If you are reading this story and it’s the day of an Apple Event – which is the case, today: Wednesday September 9 – then yes, the store is down. Apple has taken it offline while it prepares for new product launches. The store always tends to go offline just before an event–to find out if an event is expected today read: When is Apple’s next event?
Even if there isn’t an event planned, there’s also the possibility that the Apple Store could be closed while Apple updates it with new products that will launch later–or perhaps new products are up for pre-order. Wondering whether there are new products expected? Take a look at our New Apple Products round-up. Sometimes Apple just issues a press release relating to new products that it won’t be announcing at an event.
However, don’t jump to the conclusion that if the store is down it means new Apple products are coming, that isn’t always the case. The store might be down due to connectivity issues and for scheduled maintenance. For example, on April 24, 2023, we saw the store go down twice only to go back online without an update. Check the state of Apple’s servers here. 
Why the Apple Store is down today?
As we update this article on September 9, 2026, the iPhone 18 Pro, Pro Max and the long-rumored foldable iPhone, are expected to launch. As is the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. See our Live Blog for the latest on the Surprise and Shine event.
What time does the Apple Store usually go down?
You may be wondering what time the Apple Store goes down and when Apple makes the announcement. 
Events tend to start at 10 a.m. at Apple’s HQ in California, which is 1 p.m. ET and 6 p.m. U.K. time. The Apple Store tends to go down at around 5 a.m. ET, 4 a.m. PT, 12 p.m. UK time on those days. If there is no event and the Apple Store is down it could be because Apple is about to issue new product news in a press release. The news usually arrives at around 11 a.m. ET, 8 a.m. PT, and 4 p.m. in the UK. 
If there is an event on the day you land on this article, events usually start at 10am PT, or, if you aren’t based there:
U.S.: 10 a.m. (PDT), 11 a.m. (MDT), 12 p.m. (CDT), 1 p.m. (EDT)
U.K.: 6 p.m. (BST)
Europe: 7 p.m. (CEST) 8 p.m. (EEST)
Canada: 10 a.m. (PDT), 11 a.m. (MDT), 12 p.m. (CDT), 1 p.m. (EDT), 2 p.m. (ADT)
India: 10.30 p.m. (IST)
Hong Kong, Singapore and China: The following day at 1 a.m.
Australia: The following day at 1 a.m. (AWST), 2.30 a.m. (ACST), 3 a.m. (AEST)
New Zealand: The following day at 5 a.m. (NZST)
If it is an event day expect the store to be offline until shortly after the event ends. 
When the site goes down before pre-orders start it usually happens a few hours before the pre-orders are set to start. For example, when the iPhone 15 launched on September 15, preorders were set for 8 a.m. ET, 5 a.m. PT and 1 p.m. in the U.K., the site was offline from a few hours before. In 2024 the timings are the same. 
Other reasons why the Apple Store could be down
However, there are other reasons why the Apple Store can be down, so if you are here on a day when there is no event or pre-orders planned, check the other reasons why the Apple Store could be down below.
Apple could be updating the online store
Before we explain how to check the status of Apple’s online store, we should first explain the possible reasons why the store might be down.
The most exciting reason is that Apple could be updating the store with new products. 
Apple tends to shut down the Apple Store while it updates the range of products available, whether it be removing old products and adjusting pricing or featuring the latest iPhone or iPad. The tell-tale difference between server issues and Apple updating the Store is the splash page that you land on.
If the Apple Store is down due to product changes, a message along the lines of ‘We’ll be right back’ (It used to say: ‘We’ll be back soon’) should be displayed. If this is the case, you don’t need to do anything else: there are no server issues, you just need to sit tight and wait for Apple to update the Store.
The Apple Store is down
However, if when you try to access the Apple Store you get a 404 error message (or if the site isn’t performing as you’d expect) then there may be an issue with Apple’s servers. To determine whether this is the issue, you can skip the next section and read about how to check the system status below.
You are using an outdated version of Safari or macOS
If you’re struggling to access the Apple Store, while other people are having no problems, it might be due to your outdated software. If this is the case the message ‘unsupported browser version’ will display when trying to visit the page on older versions.
The store also appears to be unavailable when any of the older macOS versions, including macOS Yosemite or Sierra, on other browsers. The likes of Chrome and Firefox will not work unless you update to a recent build.
This is thought to be an attempt by Apple to protect its customers from any potential threats.
How to check Apple’s System Status
The first step in establishing whether the Apple Store is down (apart from going on the site itself!) is to visit 
Apple’s System Status website. This site displays the current status of every Apple service, from iOS device activations to iCloud and, of course, the Apple Online Store.

				
					

				
			
It not only informs users of any potential problems with the online services, but also gives users a heads up on any scheduled maintenance that could cause issues. It also indicates whether there were recent disruptions that have now been resolved.
If you see a message next to the Apple Online Store status, click it. It should bring up more details about the issue including the duration of the outage and the issues that users would have/are experiencing.
Read next: 
How to get an education discount at Apple
Check crowdsourced status websites
Apple’s System Status site isn’t the only place to find up-to-date information on the status of the Apple Store. 
Down Detector is a hugely popular third-party status website that relies on crowdsourced information from users to provide up-to-date statuses on a range of online services from PayPal to Steam and the Apple Store too.

				
					

				
			
The site allows users to report issues and allows you to see past issues that have affected the performance of the service. It also features a handy heat map of live outages, so you can see whether the issue is local to your city/region/country.
Another good resource is the aptly named  Is It Down Right Now?. The site offers similar data to Down Detector but also features a grid displaying access speeds over the past few days.
It works in a different way to Down Detector though, as you have to search for the service via URL, and at the time of writing, it checks the status of the entire Apple website, not specifically the Apple Store.

title: iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e: Release date, rumored specs, price, cameras, and latest news
content:
Macworld





For years, Apple has followed a predictable iPhone launch schedule, introducing new iPhones in September – the standard model and the Pro model. In the spring, Apple often releases a less expensive phone – previously the “SE” iPhones and, more recently, the “e” series.
That could change with the iPhone 18 generation. This year, the most reliable rumors suggest Apple will introduce the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max in the fall, along with a more expensive iPhone Ultra folding phone, but the iPhone 18 might not join them until later.
So what can we expect from the iPhone 18 and 18e? Rumors are pretty thin right now, in part because most of the exciting new stuff will come with the Pro and folding iPhone models in the fall of 2026.
Below is a log of what we’ve heard so far about the standard iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e, based on the most recent and reliable rumors, analyst reports, and leaks, along with historical precedent.
iPhone 18 vs 18e rumors at a glance


iPhone 18iPhone 18e

Expected releaseSpring 2027Spring 2027
Expected price$849-$899$649-$699
Display size6.3 inches6.1 inches
Refresh rateUp to 120Hz ProMotion60Hz
Display cutoutDynamic Island; possibly smallerNotch or possibly Dynamic Island
ProcessorA20, expected 2nmA20, expected 2nm
RAM9GB or 12GB9GB most likely
Rear camerasTwo 48MP cameras expectedSingle 48MP Main expected
Front cameraRumored 24MPRumored 12MP
Camera ControlYes, possibly simplifiedNot expected
Cellular modemApple C2 expectedApple C2 expected
Wi-Fi/BluetoothLikely N1Likely N1
DesignSimilar to iPhone 17, unless replaced by Air-style designSimilar to iPhone 17e
Biggest uncertaintyCould potentially be replaced/reimagined as Air 2Whether it gains Dynamic Island

 






Is Apple launching the iPhone 18 in September? 
No. Apple is expected to launch the iPhone 18 Pro, Pro Max and foldable iPhone at its September 9 event, but hold the standard iPhone 18 until spring 2027.
The new split-release strategy should make Apple’s increasingly large iPhone lineup easier to manufacture, while giving its premium models the spotlight during the crucial fall launch period.
It would also create a second major iPhone launch window in spring, when the iPhone 18 is expected to arrive alongside the iPhone 18e and Air 2. There is a separate rumor that the Air 2 could effectively become the iPhone 18, but that claim remains fairly speculative at this stage.


						

							


When will the iPhone 18 and 18e release?
iPhone 18: Expected in spring 2027 with an A20 chip, improved RAM and cameras, the iPhone 18 could even disappear entirely if Apple turns the thinner dual-camera Air 2 into its standard iPhone.
iPhone 18e: The iPhone 18e is expected in spring 2027 with an A20 chip, 9GB RAM, C2 modem and 48MP camera, while retaining a cheaper 60Hz display and possibly gaining Dynamic Island.
While Apple has launched its standard and high-end iPhone models together ever since the first Pro phone arrived in 2019, this year looks to be different. While the Pro phones will launch in September 2026, all the evidence indicates Apple will push the iPhone 18 launch to the spring of 2027, leaving it on shelves for a full 18 months for the first time.
So if you bought an iPhone 17 at launch and are looking to upgrade, you’ll either need to spring for an iPhone 18 Pro or wait until March or April when Apple may hold a second iPhone event or at least launch the new iPhones via press release.
We also expect Apple to release the iPhone 18e and iPhone Air 2 at the same time – although there is a rumor that the iPhone 18 might actually be the iPhone Air 2.
“Early Apple” published a claim on X that Apple is “exploring the idea” of calling what is essentially the iPhone Air 2 the ‌iPhone 18‌ rather than launching a third device. In July Jon Prosser made a similar suggestion in a FTP video that Apple could eventually streamline the lineup around the iPhone, iPhone Pro and iPhone Ultra, with the Air serving as a stepping stone toward that strategy..


						

							







What specs will the iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e have?
A20 processor
9GB to 12GB RAM
C2 modem
While the iPhone 18 Pro and Ultra will almost certainly use the new A20 Pro chip, the iPhone 18 and 18e are expected to use the standard A20. Like the Pro version, it should be manufactured by TSMC using a 2nm process.
Based on the A19, we expect the A20 to retain a 6-core CPU while delivering improved performance and efficiency. The GPU will probably have five cores, although Apple could disable one core in the iPhone 18e. One of the biggest gains may come from the Neural Engine, as Apple continues to put more emphasis on on-device AI processing.
The standard iPhone 18 is also expected to get more RAM, up from the iPhone 17’s 8GB. Analyst Jeff Pu predicts a substantial increase to 12GB, matching the current iPhone 17 Pro, while Ming-Chi Kuo expects the iPhone 18 and 18e to use an unusual 9GB configuration made up of six 1.5GB memory chips. Macworld considers 9GB slightly more plausible given the global memory shortage and rising component costs.
More RAM would primarily benefit multitasking and AI. Both memory capacity and bandwidth are important when running advanced AI models on-device, so Apple has good reason to increase RAM across the range. However, if the iPhone 18 and 18e are limited to 9GB while the Pro models get 12GB, they could have less headroom for increasingly demanding Apple Intelligence features in future iOS releases. That could eventually mean some features are reduced or unavailable on the cheaper models.
Elsewhere, the iPhone 18 and 18e are expected to adopt Apple’s upcoming C2 cellular modem. It isn’t yet clear whether the C2 will support mmWave in the U.S., but improvements to 5G performance and power efficiency are likely, along with the potential for expanded satellite connectivity. For Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, Apple may have little reason to move beyond the N1 chip, which already supports Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.


						

							


Will the iPhone 18 and 18e’s cameras be improved?

				
					

				
			iPhone 17e camera. 
David Price / Foundry





24MP selfie camera on iPhone 18
iPhone 18e may retain a 12MP selfie camera
48MP Main cameras expected
Revised Camera Control button on iPhone 18
The iPhone 18 could get another front-camera upgrade. Apple introduced an 18MP Center Stage camera with the iPhone 17 generation, but reports now suggest the standard iPhone 18 will move to a 24MP selfie camera. That should potentially deliver more detail and give Apple more resolution to work with for cropping and computational photography.
The rumor that the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 could be one and the same may mean that the iPhone Air gets a second rear camera. 
The situation with the iPhone 18e is less clear. While some rumors have suggested that 24MP cameras could spread across the wider iPhone 18 family, a November 2025 J.P. Morgan report said the lower-cost iPhone 18e will retain a 12MP front camera. For now, we wouldn’t assume that the 18e will get the same selfie-camera upgrade as the iPhone 18.
There has been much less information about the rear cameras. The current iPhone 17 has 48MP Main and 48MP Ultra Wide cameras, while the iPhone 17e has a single 48MP Main camera. We therefore expect the iPhone 18 to retain two 48MP rear cameras and the iPhone 18e to continue with a single 48MP Main camera, although there haven’t yet been reliable reports of major sensor upgrades for either model.
Apple may also simplify Camera Control. According to Weibo leaker Instant Digital, the iPhone 18’s button will retain pressure sensitivity but drop the capacitive sensing used by current models, potentially reducing complexity and cost. The iPhone 18e isn’t expected to gain Camera Control.


						

							


Will the iPhone 18e get a display upgrade?

				
					

				
			iPhone 17e display.
David Price / Foundry




The iPhone 18 is likely to use a display similar to the iPhone 17, with up to 1,000 nits of typical SDR brightness, 1,600 nits peak HDR brightness, and up to 3,000 nits outdoors.
The iPhone 18e could get a more noticeable upgrade, although reports remain inconsistent. The current iPhone 17e uses an older display with relatively modest brightness and a notch rather than Dynamic Island. Some reports suggest the iPhone 18e will finally move to a newer panel with Dynamic Island, potentially bringing it closer to the iPhone 15, which offered up to 2,000 nits of outdoor brightness. However, the Dynamic Island upgrade remains disputed.
What does appear more likely is that Apple will continue to limit the 18e to a 60Hz display. According to Digital Chat Station, the phone will retain a 60Hz LTPS OLED panel rather than adopting the LTPO technology used for ProMotion. That would mean no 120Hz ProMotion refresh rate or Always-On display, even as those features become more widespread elsewhere in the iPhone lineup.


						

							


How much will the iPhone 18 and 18e cost?
Everything in the world of tech has gotten more expensive, thanks to chip shortages spurred on by an endless need to build more, bigger AI data centers. Apple in June raised its prices for nearly all Macs and iPads, and even aging hardware like HomePod and Apple TV. iPhone was spared, but we predict the new iPhones arriving on September 9 will carry prices at least $50-100 higher than they have in the past. And that’s likely to carry forward to the spring releases, too.
Our estimation there for is that the iPhone 18 could start at $849 or $899, and the iPhone 18e could start at $649 or $699. However, as these are Apple’s budget models, it’s possible that Apple raises prices on the Pro models but keeps the iPhone 18 and 18e at their current levels, it’s also possible that Apple could raise prices of the iPhone 17 and 17e before they are replaced. 


						

							


Should you wait for iPhone 18?
If you want the Pro models: The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will be available later in 2026. But be prepared for higher prices.
If you want a standard or budget iPhone the wait for the iPhone 18 is longer. In the meantime, the iPhone 17 and iPhone 17e remain excellent choices.
If you want to save money, the iPhone 17 starts at $799/£799 with 256GB of storage, making it one of the best values in the lineup.

title: New report claims foldable iPhone will be branded as Duo
content:
Macworld





Forget iPhone Ultra, forget iPhone Fold… the latest breaking news is that Apple’s first ever folding handset will be called the iPhone Duo. That’s according to Mark Gurman’s sources, and he’s generally well informed when it comes to information like this.
Gurman made his last-minute prediction in an article (subscription required) this morning. He also claimed the device will start at $2,000 (rising to $3,000 if you max out the storage), have a short-and-wide design, feature Apple’s new in-house C2 modem and A20 Pro chip, and go on sale in October, later than the other new iPhones. But we knew all that already. The name is the real bombshell.
You can bet that some will accuse Apple of copying Microsoft, whose Surface Duo was something of a pioneer in this field, albeit with mixed success. On the other hand, maybe Microsoft should have kept that brand going; the line was discontinued nearly two years ago. And that brand was closely intertwined with the word “Surface;” it’s debatable how many customers will associate the word “Duo” alone with Microsoft, even before Cupertino’s inevitable marketing campaign wipes the slate clean and makes it a resoundingly Apple brand.
Speaking subjectively we would add that the Duo brand also goes rather nicely with Neo, as in MacBook, and has a pleasing brevity and sound. And, please note, it was one of the options mentioned by Macworld sister site Tech Advisor earlier this week.
If Gurman’s sources are correct–by no means a sure thing, although we’d rate this as a strong likelihood–this will be tough news for case manufacturers, who have been preparing pre-launch marketing materials with iPhone Ultra and/or iPhone Fold branding.
The folding iPhone, or iPhone Duo as we may now have to start calling it, is strongly expected to be unveiled at Apple’s Surprise and Shine press event today at 10 am PT. For all the latest news and rumors, check out our regularly updated foldable iPhone superguide, not to mention our Apple event live blog. We hope you’ll follow the event here on Macworld.

Foldable iPhone name: Previous rumors and reports have clung to the name "iPhone Ultra" for Apple's first foldable iPhone – a name that Gurman himself has used several times in the past. However, in his latest report, Gurman says Apple has settled on the name "iPhone Duo" for the device.

Starting price: TrendForce estimates and other reports have suggested the iPhone Duo will start at above $2,000, and perhaps go as high as $2,500. Gurman's latest report says the starting price will be $2,000 for the 256GB model, while the highest-capacity model will be around $3,000.


Color options: Previous rumors suggested Apple would "stay away from fun colors" for its first foldable iPhone, with a darker color being described as a shade of indigo rather than black. Gurman's last-minute report backs up that idea, saying the iPhone Duo will come in white and dark blue.
Gurman says the iPhone Duo will "go on sale as early as October," suggesting it will be available to buy at a later date than the iPhone 18 Pro models, which are also expected to be unveiled today at Apple's "Surprise and Shine" event.

title: iPhone 18 Pro Details Purportedly Leaked By Verizon's AI Assistant [Updated]
content:
A series of screenshots seemingly show Verizon's AI chat assistant answering detailed questions about the iPhone 18 Pro and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max, just hours before Apple's announcement event.


The screenshots were shared privately with MacRumors by X user "mehrtosh," who says the responses came from the "Ask Verizon" AI assistant built into the carrier's app. The conversation is timestamped September 8 at 1:48 to 1:52 p.m., the day before Apple's "Surprise and shine" event. According to the screenshots, the assistant made the following interesting claims about the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max:


The ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max features the same variable aperture main camera lens as the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌.

Variable aperture lets the lens opening adjust between f/1.4 and f/4.0 for better low-light shots, natural bokeh, and sharper group photos.

The ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max gets an "advanced" Sensor-shift OIS for improved low-light video stabilization and a larger main sensor for more detail and light.

The ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max features a 48MP telephoto camera with up to 10x optical zoom, up from 8x on the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌.

The ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max has 16GB of RAM, compared to 12GB on the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌.

The ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ starts at $1,099.99, with the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max starting at $1,199.99.

The ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ comes in four colors: Dark Cherry, Titanium Gray, Titanium White, and Titanium Black.



iPhone 17 Pro's current starting prices, even though there is a general consensus from analysts that prices will increase this generation.

The color names are also seem to be incorrect. Recent leaks have pointed to Dark Cherry alongside Silver and Sky Blue, not the "Titanium Gray," "Titanium White," and "Titanium Black" names the assistant listed, which more closely resemble the finish names Apple used for the iPhone 15 Pro lineup back in 2023. This clearly raises the possibility that the chatbot pulled outdated or unrelated training data rather than surfacing a genuine leak. The assistant also made a series of more plausible claims:


The ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ has a 6.3-inch Super Retina XDR display, while the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max has a 6.9-inch display.

The ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max offers longer battery life than the Pro due to its larger size.

Both models feature a triple-lens rear camera system.

The main camera is 48MP with the f/1.4 to f/4.0 variable aperture and Sensor-shift OIS.

The ultra wide camera is 48MP, aimed at high-resolution macro and wide shots.

Both models support ProRAW and ProRes video recording.

Both models are powered by the A20 Pro chip.



We have been unable to independently verify or replicate the exchange, suggesting the chatbot may have since been patched, or that the original screenshots were altered or otherwise inaccurate. Given that, and the fact that AI chatbots are known to hallucinate plausible sounding but false information, the claims should be treated with skepticism rather than as a legitimate leak.

Update: Verizon tells MacRumors that the alleged leak from the AI chatbot is untrue.

title: Every new Apple product coming in 2026 & 2027
content:

It’s already been a huge year for Apple, with a wave of new products arriving during the first eight months of 2026, including the MacBook Neo and iPhone 17e, and then the new Mac mini and Mac Studio.
But one of Apple’s biggest launches of the year is still to come – and it could happen today. Apple is holding its September 9 “Surprise and Shine” event, where it is expected to unveil the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, new Apple Watches and, most significantly, its first foldable iPhone, recently rumored to be called the iPhone Duo.
There is plenty more on Apple’s roadmap beyond today’s event. New iPads and smart-home products could arrive later in 2026, while Apple is also believed to be preparing its first touchscreen MacBook Pro and smart glasses.
Alongside the new hardware, Apple is preparing the public release of iOS 27, macOS 27 and its other next-generation operating systems, bringing the major Siri AI overhaul first previewed at WWDC in June. Here’s everything Apple has launched in 2026 so far – and what we expect to come next.

Read on to find out what new products to expect at Apple’s next event and throughout 2026.


						

							







Every New Apple Product Launching in 2026
In the sections below we’ve split the upcoming new products into categories including Mac, iPad, iPhone, Apple Watch, Home, AirPods, and some new product categories.
Apple Intelligence, Siri and AI
iOS 27 and macOS 27 Golden Gate, will introduce a massive overhaul to Siri and expanded Apple Intelligence capabilities.
The All-New Siri AI
The most significant update is the transformation of Siri into Siri AI, a conversational assistant powered by Apple Intelligence. 
Key Siri AI features coming later in 2026 include:
Onscreen Awareness: Siri will understand and interact with what is displayed on your screen. For example, if a friend texts you an address, you can ask Siri to save it to a contact without leaving the app.
Dedicated Siri App: A new standalone app will allow you to revisit previous conversations, pin important chats, and sync history across all Apple devices via iCloud.
App Actions: Siri will be able to perform tasks within apps using natural language, such as editing a recently sent message or adding a song to a specific playlist.
Visual Intelligence: On iPhone, a new Siri mode in the Camera app will allow users to point their phone at objects to ask questions or perform actions based on what they see. On Mac, users can select onscreen content to ask Siri questions about images or documents.
Voice Customization: Users can personalize Siri with more natural voices and adjust the pace and expressiveness of the speech. This feature requires a M3 Mac with 12GB RAM or newer, or iPhone 17 Pro or iPhone Air and newer. 
Apple Intelligence Across Apps
Beyond Siri, Apple Intelligence is being integrated system-wide to automate tasks and enhance productivity. Apple Intelligence will play a larger role across the iPhone, iPad, Mac, smart home devices, and future product categories.
Major updates include:
Safari Productivity: The browser will automatically group tabs into topics, monitor pages for changes (like price drops) with a “Notify Me” feature, and even build custom extensions based on natural-language descriptions.
Smarter Photo Editing: New tools include Spatial Reframing to improve composition after a photo is taken, an Extend tool to fill in missing areas when straightening horizons, and an upgraded Clean Up tool for removing distractions.
Writing Tools and Communication: Mail and Messages will gain smarter replies that mimic a user’s writing style . System-wide Writing Tools will generate text from scratch, rewrite drafts, and adapt tone to match specific contacts.
Image Playground: This tool has been revamped with better language models to create more natural-looking photorealistic images. It also allows users to create custom wallpapers on iOS 27.
Intelligent Automation: The Shortcuts app will feature a “Describe a Shortcut” ability, allowing users to create complex automations simply by explaining what they want in plain English.

Daily Readiness and Stress Tracking: Unlike competitors such as the Oura Ring 4 or Garmin, the Apple Watch currently lacks a “daily readiness” score or native stress tracking. Experts suggest these are obvious areas for future software or hardware updates.
Other new features could include Touch ID integration and microLED displays reaching 4,000 nits brightness. A thinner case, magnetic bands, and enhanced AI capabilities could also be on the cards.

title: 2027 iPad: A18/A19 chip, release date, price and specs
content:
Macworld





Apple’s next entry-level iPad may not be the flashiest iPad update of 2027, but it could be one of the most important. The affordable model is reportedly set to receive a faster chip that will finally bring support for Apple Intelligence.
The current iPad, released in March 2025, remains a capable tablet for students, families and everyday users, but it is now the only iPad in Apple’s lineup that doesn’t support Apple Intelligence. A new model expected in early 2027 should address that limitation, potentially with an A18 or A19 chip.
Other changes are expected to be relatively modest, with Apple likely to retain the current design and LCD display while focusing on performance and connectivity improvements.
Here’s everything we know so far about the 2027 iPad, including its expected release date, price, design, chip and other specs.
What’s new vs 2025 iPad A16: At a glance


2027 iPad predictions2025 iPad

Launch dateEarly 2027March 2025
Processor A18 (maybe A19) A16 
RAM8GB6GB
Wi-Fi  Wi-Fi 7 Wi-Fi 6
Bluetooth Bluetooth 6Bluetooth 5.3
Apple IntelligenceYesNo
DesignUnchangedUnchanged

 






2027 iPad release date: When will Apple launch the next entry-level iPad?
Early 2027 launch predicted
In a July 2026 report, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman said that Apple has scheduled the release of the entry-level iPad for “as early as the first calendar quarter next year.” Previously, Gurman had reported that the new entry-level iPad was “on the roadmap for a release in the iOS 26.4 timeframe, which runs until May.” 
Why the later ship date? It’s possible that Apple needs to ensure sufficient supply of whichever chip it chooses (A18, A19, or A20) and may also be waiting for its Apple Intelligence features to be fully ready. This includes ongoing work to improve next-generation Siri AI, which is part of the iPadOS 27 update that will be released in the fall.
A delay is more likely to be strategic than technical. Apple did not update the base iPad during its March 2026 launch event, despite releasing the M4 iPad Air. Holding back the entry-level iPad helps avoid cannibalising sales of more expensive models, and staggered releases like this are typical of Apple’s product strategy.
Should you wait? 
We recommend waiting for the 2027 iPad if you’re considering an upgrade. The next-generation iPad is expected to deliver a meaningful upgrade with a faster chip, more RAM, and support for Apple Intelligence, making it a much more future-proof choice.


						

							


2027 iPad chip: Will the new iPad use the A18 or A19 chip?
A18 or A19 chip expected
6-core CPU and 5-core GPU likely
N1 chip for improved Wi-Fi and Bluetooth
The next iPad is expected to use either the A18 or A19 chip, with conflicting evidence pointing to both possibilities. Macworld has seen internal Apple code specifically linking the new J581 and J582 models to the A19, while Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported in March 2026 that Apple had prepared an A18-powered model. It’s possible Apple has tested multiple configurations or subsequently changed its plans.
The A18, which debuted in the iPhone 16 and 16 Plus in 2024, would be a substantial upgrade over the A16 in the current iPad. Crucially, it would also bring the 8GB of RAM needed to support Apple Intelligence.
However, there is strong evidence for the A19 as well. As we reported in December 2025, leaked Apple code linked the J581 and J582 iPad models to the A19 chip used in the iPhone 17.
Until further information emerges, either chip remains plausible. Reports of A18 Pro shortages, linked to demand for the MacBook Neo, shouldn’t necessarily affect supplies of the standard A18.
What to expect
A18 chip: Features a 6-core CPU and 5-core GPU in the iPhone 16. Apple could use the same configuration or a binned version in the iPad. It should provide a substantial performance increase over the A16, while 8GB of RAM would enable Apple Intelligence.
A19 chip: Also features a 6-core CPU and 5-core GPU in the iPhone 17. If Apple uses it, the A19 would offer a larger performance upgrade over the A16 while likewise providing the memory required for Apple Intelligence.
Other specs
We have seen internal-code that indicates the new iPad will contain Apple’s N1 wireless chip. First introduced with the iPhone 17 lineup, the N1 handles Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and Thread connectivity. Its inclusion could bring Wi-Fi 6E or Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.x, upgrading the current iPad’s Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5.3.
For cellular models, Apple will likely use its in-house C1 modem (or a variant of it), continuing its shift away from third-party suppliers while improving efficiency and integration.


						

							


Why does Apple Intelligence matter for the iPad? 
Apple Intelligence introduces a range of AI-powered features designed to enhance creativity, productivity, and real-time communication, including:
Image Generation: Tools like Image Playground and Genmoji allow users to create custom visuals and personalized emojis from text prompts.
Live Translation: Integrated into FaceTime and Messages, this feature provides real-time translated captions during calls, effectively giving every user a personal translator.
Photo Editing: The “Clean Up” tool uses AI to identify and remove unwanted background objects from photos, a task that previously required complex manual editing.
Writing Tools: System-wide rewriting, proofreading, and summarization in apps such as Mail and Notes. 
Smart Shortcuts: Automation of repetitive tasks using intelligent actions and text summarization. 
Priority Management: AI-driven Priority Notifications and Priority Inbox to surface time-sensitive information.
These features require at least 8GB of RAM and a more powerful Neural Engine, which means Apple Intelligence is currently limited to M-series iPads (Air and Pro) and the A17 Pro iPad mini.
By contrast, the standard iPad with the A16 chip (released in March 2025) does not support Apple Intelligence. This is a notable limitation for long-term value, especially as future versions of iPadOS are expected to rely increasingly on AI-driven features.


						

							


2027 iPad display: No OLED or ProMotion
Same 10.9-inch LCD
No OLED display
No ProMotion 
While there are reports that the other iPads (mini, Air and Pro) could get new OLED panels with richer colors and deeper contrast in 2027, the base model is unlikely to evolve from its LCD panel.
We expect the upcoming iPad to have the same 11-inch Liquid Retina display 2360-by-1640 display with 500 nits of brightness and 60Hz refresh rate that it has had since 2022.


						

							


2027 iPad design: No new design

				
					

				
			
Apple currently offers the iPad in four colors.

Apple




The A19 iPad is also expected to have the same dimensions: 9.79 x 7.07 x 0.28 inches (248.6 x 179.5 x 7 millimeters) and weigh 1.05 pounds (477 grams). 
We haven’t heard anything about new colors, but since Apple hasn’t changed the color palette (blue, pink, yellow, silver) since its original release, it’s possible we get a couple of new options.


						

							


2027 iPad cameras: Will Apple update the FaceTime camera?

				
					

				
			
Britta O’Boyle





12MP rear camera 
12MP Center Stage front camera 
The current iPad has two 12MP cameras, with the front ‘FaceTime’ camera having support for Center Stage. Apple isn’t expected to make changes to the camera for the upcoming iPad. 
However, the company did change the Centre Stage camera with the arrival of the iPhone 17, and the new ‘square’ 18MP camera could be used on the front of the new iPad, but there are no reports indicating this will be the case. 
This front-facing camera has a larger, square sensor that supports automatic subject framing, orientation-agnostic capture, and advanced video features. On the iPad the 18MP camera could translate to improved video quality. However, current iPads already support smart framing during video calls so that aspect of the design may not be necessary. 


						

							


2027 iPad price: Will Apple keep the entry-level iPad affordable?
After launching at $449 in 2022, Apple cut the price of the entry-level iPad to $349 in May 2024, then doubled the starting storage from 64GB to 128GB with the 11th-generation model. However, in June 2026, Apple raised the price back to $449 due to supply-chain shortages. That makes the current A16 model considerably less attractive with a more capable, AI-ready replacement expected in early 2027. It’s also possible Apple could raise the price again when the new model arrives.

title: When is Apple’s next event? Dates, rumors, and what to expect
content:
Macworld





Today’s the day: Apple’s September event takes place today, Wednesday, September 9. Follow our Live Blog for up to the minute analysis. It may not be Apple’s final event of 2026, however, with another launch potentially following in October. 
Apple typically has four main event windows each year: a spring event, WWDC in June, the iPhone event in September, and sometimes a further event in October. The company rarely confirms dates far in advance, and there’s no guarantee it will hold an event in every window. That leaves Apple fans – and anyone considering a new Apple device – wondering when the next event will happen and what might be announced.
Fortunately, Apple’s annual schedule is fairly predictable, while reliable rumours often provide additional clues about what’s coming. That means we can make informed estimates about the timing of future keynotes and the products most likely to appear.
From the iPhone 18 Pro lineup and folding iPhone to new Apple Watches and potential Mac and iPad updates, here’s everything we know about today’s Apple event, plus the other events Apple could hold later in 2026 and beyond.


When is Apple’s next event?
Today: Wednesday September 9, 2026
Apple announced the date of its September event on August 26, two weeks before the event was scheduled to be held – September 9. 
As in previous years, Apple will livestream the event, allowing viewers around the world to watch the company unveil its latest products. One notable change this year is that the keynote is expected to be hosted by John Ternus, who has succeeded Tim Cook as Apple’s CEO. 
Watch the stream here: 





							




Apple event calendar 2026
