March Special Experience2-4 MarchLaunched: iPhone 17e, MacBooks Neo, Pro & Air, iPad Air
JuneWWDCJune 8Unveiled plans for: iOS, macOS, other software, AI and Siri
September[iPhone event]September 9Expected: iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone Duo, new Apple Watch
October or November[Late fall event]TBCPossible: Touchscreen MacBook and iPads
Spring 2027TBCTBCExpected: iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, iPhone Air 2

 



Apple has held two events so far in 2026, although the first was not an event in the traditional sense. On March 4, the company invited select media to hands-on “experiences” in multiple locations. In the run-up to that date, Apple launched several products via press release, including the iPhone 17e, M4 iPad Air, and MacBook Pro M5 Pro and M5 Max, M5 MacBook Air and the MacBook Neo.
The second event was WWDC, which began with a keynote on June 8. At the WWDC keynote Apple outlined the upcoming changes to its operating systems, including iOS 27 and macOS 27 Golden Gate.
In August Apple issued press releases to announce the new Mac mini and Mac Studio. 
At the September 9 event Apple is expected to unveil the iPhone 18 Pro, a foldable iPhone Duo, and more at an Apple event on September 9. 
A second, late-fall event in October or November is possible, though less certain and typically focused on Macs or iPads.

				
					

				
			
Here’s when the 2026 Apple events might take place.

Foundry





 FAQ 


1.
What will Apple announce at today’s event?
Apple’s September event is the biggest and most watched Apple event of the year. It’s the venue at which Apple unveils the new iPhones and Apple Watches for the next year. 
We expect Apple to launch the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4. Apple may also reveal the new folding iPhone, thought to be called the iPhone Duo.





2.
What time does the next Apple event start in U.S., U.K. and other global time zones
Apple keynotes usually start at 10 am PT and this one is no different. That translates to the following times in the countries where most of our readers live:
U.S.: 10 am PDT, 11 am MDT, 12 pm CDT, 1 pm EDT
Canada: as above, plus 2 pm ADT
U.K.: 6 pm
Europe: 7 pm CEST, 8 pm EEST
India: 10:30 pm IST
Australia: next day — 1 am AWST, 2:30 am ACST, 3 am AEST
New Zealand: next day — 5 am NZST
The timings are generally the same for all Apple Keynotes, but can be slightly different if Apple holds the event during the period of a couple of weeks when the clocks have changed in the U.S. but not elsewhere (in 2026 the clocks will change in the U.S. on November 1, while in the U.K. they change on October 25).
Sometimes Apple holds events at different times, for example, in October 2023 the event was held in late afternoon in San Francisco, which meant it was midnight in the U.K. 
If Apple doesn’t hold an event and instead just issues a press release that usually happens around 8 am PT, 11 am ET and 4 pm U.K. time.





3.
How long do Apple events usually last?
Apple keynotes usually last between one and two hours and feature the CEO alongside various other Apple executives. With John Ternus succeeding Tim Cook as CEO on September 1, 2026, this will be his first major product keynote in the role.
WWDC and the September event tend to be longer keynotes; the spring and late-fall events can be slightly shorter.
For example, the September 2024 event was 1 hour 38 minutes.





4.
How often does Apple hold events?
There can be as many as four Apple events in a year:  
Spring Event
WWDC in June
iPhone Event in September
Late Fall Event in October
This event calendar is by no means set in stone, though, with the spring and October events being less regular. Some years, Apple doesn’t hold a spring event at all. In 2025 Apple only held two events preferring instead to announce new products via press release.





5.
Does Apple take part in other events?
Apple doesn’t participate in major industry trade shows such as CES and IFA. Instead Apple invites the press and industry professionals to Apple Park to hear all about its latest products and services. Apple calls these ‘events’ and it streams them live online to millions of viewers.





6.
Does Apple ever announce products without an event? 
Apple frequently announces products without a keynote event, often opting for press releases or multi-day announcement windows. In recent years, the company has increasingly reserved its large-scale media events for major flagship launches, such as the primary iPhone lineup in September, while using press releases for iterative updates or “chip bumps” that may not warrant a full hour-long presentation.





7.
How to watch an Apple event
Apple events are typically broadcast across several digital platforms, allowing viewers to tune in from almost any device. While the company previously restricted access to its own hardware or the Safari browser, these barriers have been removed in recent years.
You can access live Apple presentations through the following official channels:
YouTube: This is often considered the easiest way to watch. Apple streams its keynotes live on its official YouTube channel, which can be accessed via any web browser or the YouTube app on smartphones, tablets, and smart TVs .
Apple.com: The company hosts a dedicated “Events” page on its official website. For the best experience on a PC, it is recommended to use Microsoft Edge on Windows 10 or later .
Apple TV App: The stream is available within the Apple TV app on iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple TV hardware. Keynotes are usually listed in the app’s lineup a day or two before the event begins .
Apple Podcasts: Apple also showcases its events through the Podcasts app on Apple devices, where you can watch the video presentation
You may also like to tune in to our Live Blog which will provide minute-by-minute text updates and analysis as products are announced.
Following the end of the event, detailed breakdowns will also be available on the Macworld Podcast, which can be found on Spotify, Soundcloud, and Apple Podcasts. 








When is the iPhone event and what will launch?

				
					

				
			
Apple




When is the iPhone event?
September 9, 2026 
Apple’s iPhone launch event has become a regular fixture in September (aside 2020, when the event was delayed until October – and the early January launches).
What will Apple launch at the September 2026 event?
We can be pretty confident that at least one new iPhone will launch in late 2026, although there may be some changes to the line up: we may see the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max launch in September, but the iPhone 18 is expected to be held back until the spring of 2027. There are also rumors of a folding iPhone – supposedly called the iPhone Ultra or Duo launching in September.
Alongside the new iPhone 18 Pro we may see new Apple Watches. In 2026 the Apple Watch Series 12 should get a chip update, since the Series 11 is using the same chip as the Series 10 did. The Apple Watch Ultra 4 is said to be getting an update too. And we may also see new AirPods. 
Apple is also rumored to have some upgrades coming to the HomePod and Apple TV to better equip them for Siri AI. 
Find out more about the September iPhone event in our dedicated article.


						

							


Will Apple have a second fall event in 2026?

				
					

				
			
Apple




Will there be a late fall event in 2026?
The last time Apple held a late fall event was October 30, 2023, and before that October 18, 2021. So a late fall event isn’t unprecedented, but it is uncommon. Right now there is no way of knowing if Apple will hold a late fall event in 2026, or indeed, if it ever will again. Usually this event is to launch consumer Macs, but in recent years Apple hasn’t felt the need to hold an event to do that. Nearer the time we will know if there are big things planned that might warrant an event. 
What will Apple launch at the late fall 2026 event?
Mac or iPad launches are the most likely reasons for an Apple event during this timeframe, but Apple has not felt the need to hold a dedicated Mac event since the “Scary Fast” presentation in 2023, when it introduced the M3, M3 Pro, and M3 Max chips alongside updated MacBook Pro models. There could still be Mac-related announcements this year: the rumored touchscreen MacBook Pro could make an appearance.
The timing of any new Mac releases will likely depend on whether the supply chain has fully recovered from the component shortages that have affected the industry throughout the year. These shortages have also led Apple to raise prices for iPads and Macs.
As for iPads, a new iPad or iPad mini are long overdue, so an October event would be a likely venue for those launches, if they don’t arrive in September. The chip shortages may affect the iPad too. 
For more information about Apple’s late fall events read: Apple’s October Event: Date, time and what will launch.


						

							


Will Apple hold a spring event in 2027? 

				
					

				
			John Ternus: Apple’s CEO from September 2026.
Michael Simon / Foundry




Apple’s spring events have become increasingly unpredictable. The company has not held a traditional spring event since May 2024, although it did invite members of the media, including Macworld, to a “Special Apple Experience” in 2026. 
Rather than a keynote presentation, the March 4, 2026 gathering was a hands-on showcase that followed three days of product announcements, including the MacBook Neo, iPhone 17e, and M5 MacBook Air.
Will Apple take a similar approach to spring product launches in 2027? It’s certainly possible. The format appeared to work well, allowing each product announcement to receive its own media coverage rather than competing for attention during a single event. 
Apple is expected to release three iPhone models in spring 2027 – or it could be two new iPhones, with the Air and iPhone 18 merging.
iPhone 18 (base model)
iPhone 18e
iPhone Air 2
Apple may also update the MacBook Air with an M6 processor in spring 2027. A report from early August 2026 notes that Apple is currently struggling with memory shortages that are impacting MacBook Air stock, and the M6 update is seen as a potential, though not guaranteed, fix for the supply issues.


						

							


When is WWDC 2027

				
					

				
			
Foundry




When is the WWDC keynote?
In 2026 the WWDC keynote was on Monday June 8. In 2025 it started on Monday June 9. We expect WWDC will start on Monday 7 June in 2027. 
WWDC generally runs from the Monday to Friday in the second week of June. 
What Apple could launch at WWDC
WWDC is Apple’s big developer event at which it reveals plans for the operating systems that run on Apple hardware.
In June 2027 we expect Apple to unveil details of the iOS 28, iPadOS 28, the new macOS 28, updates to watchOS, tvOS, HomePod software, and an update to Apple’s realityOS.
Apple sometimes announces new hardware at WWDC, usually the high end models targeted at power users, so we could see new Macs.
Following the keynote on the Monday, developer events and sessions will run throughout the week. You can read more about WWDC date, times and everything you need to know in a separate article.


						

							


What did Apple launch at past events
So far in 2026 Apple has held an ‘experience’, which rather than being an event in the traditional sense, was a chance for journalists to get a look at products Apple had launched in the days prior, including MacBook Neo and iPhone 17e. The company also hosted the WWDC keynote on June 8, at which it revealed its plans for Apple Intelligence and Siri in iOS 27, macOS 27 and the other operating systems.
In 2025 Apple only held two events. The first was its Worldwide Developers Conference (WWDC) on June 9, at which it introduced the new features coming in the next version of its operating systems, and the second was the huge September 9 Apple Event where it launched new Apple Watches, new AirPods Pro and the new iPhones for 2025.
Apple doesn’t have to hold an event to launch new products though. Prior to WWDC, Apple launched a new iPhone 16e via press release on February 19, a new iPad and iPad Air via press release on March 4, and a new MacBook Air and Mac Studio on March 5. 
Apple then went on to launch a new M5 MacBook Pro and M5 iPad Pro in October. No event was held to mark these launches.
In 2024, Apple held three events: one on Tuesday, May 7, at which it launched new iPads; a keynote to kick off WWDC on June 10; and an event on September 9 at which Apple unveiled the new iPhone 16, Apple Watch Series 10 and the AirPods 4. In October 2024 there was no event, but Apple did announce new products (iMac, Mac mini and MacBook Pro) via press release.
In 2023 there were three events: WWDC in June, an iPhone event in September, and Apple’s second fall event on October 30 (or after midnight on October 31 if you weren’t in the U.S.).
In 2022 Apple held three events: a spring event on March 8, WWDC on June 6, and the iPhone 14 launch on September 7. In other years Apple has held four events though.

title: Apple Event Today: iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo Cheat Sheet
content:
Apple's biggest event of the year is almost here, and all eyes are on Cupertino. With the first foldable iPhone expected to headline Apple's "Surprise and Shine" event on Wednesday, September 9, at 10:00 a.m. Pacific Time, the rumor mill has been running full throttle, fuelled by the biggest single design change in the life of the iPhone.



To get you up to speed, here's a quick reference guide to the rumored upgrades, expected prices, and possible pre-order/release dates of everything we're expecting to see today.

Rumors by Model

iPhone 18 Pro / Pro Max


Similar overall design to the iPhone 17 Pro models, with a more uniform finish across the aluminum and glass back.

  
Smaller Dynamic Island, said to be achieved by Apple moving some Face ID components beneath the screen.

  
More efficient LTPO+ displays.

  
A20 Pro chip manufactured using TSMC's 2nm process.

  
12GB of RAM and 256GB starting storage.

  
Variable-aperture main camera for greater control over light and background blur – although reports disagree on whether this will be exclusive to the Pro Max.

  
Possible Samsung image sensor for improved image quality and camera responsiveness.

  
Simplified Camera Control button that retains pressure sensing but removes the capacitive layer.

  
Larger battery in the Pro Max, which could well result in a slightly thicker and heavier body.

  
Possible Apple C2 modem, although U.S. models could retain Qualcomm modems for mmWave support.

  
The strongest color rumors include Dark Cherry, Light Blue, and Silver. Other rumors have suggested no Silver, and a black finish has also been suggested.


iPhone Duo (Foldable)


Apple's first folding iPhone, with "iPhone Duo" among the rumored names, with "iPhone Fold" and "iPhone Ultra" remaining outlying possibilities.

  
Book-style design with an approximately 5.5-inch outer display and 7.8-inch inner display.

  
Chassis measuring just 4.5mm thick when unfolded.

  
Liquid-metal hinge and an extremely inconspicuous – but not completely invisible – display crease.

  
Touch ID integrated into the Side button in lieu of Face ID.

  
Wide and Ultra Wide rear cameras, plus selfie cameras on both the outer and inner displays.

  
A20 Pro chip and an expected 12GB of RAM.

  
MagSafe charging support.

  
iPad-like multitasking, including side-by-side apps.

  
Silver/white and a very dark indigo finish among the rumored colors.


Apple Watch Series 12


Familiar design, with no major change to the case expected.

  
Faster S12 chip and improvements to health and fitness tracking.

  
Possible return of a ceramic case, with white and dark gray versions reportedly tested.

  
Continuous heart-rate monitoring throughout the day among the features Apple is testing, along with a new "Readiness" app.

  
More wellness metrics through revamped Health and Fitness experiences.


Apple Watch Ultra 4


Similar design to the Apple Watch Ultra 3.

  
Faster S12 chip and related health and fitness improvements.

  
Likely continuous heart-rate collection if the Series 12 gets it.

  
Possible expansion of satellite capabilities, including Apple Maps and photo sharing in Messages.


AirPods 5 (Possible)


Two versions expected, with and without active noise cancellation.

  
Possible H3 chip for better sound quality and lower latency.


iPhone 18 (Regular)

The regular iPhone 18 is not expected to feature tomorrow. Apple is reportedly moving that model's launch to spring 2027, when the iPhone 18e and iPhone Air 2 are also expected to debut as part of a new split-year release schedule.

iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo Pricing Expectations

Higher memory costs could push up prices for both Pro models this year. Based on TrendForce's forecasts for the Pro models and Bloomberg's latest reporting on the foldable, the possible U.S. starting prices are:

  

    Model
Estimated Starting Price

  

    iPhone 18 Pro
$1,249–$1,299

  

    iPhone 18 Pro Max
$1,349–$1,399

  

    iPhone Duo
$2,199 (rumored)



Bloomberg's Mark Gurman today reported that the device will have a $2,000 starting price for the foldable with 256GB of storage, with some upgraded storage configurations potentially approaching $3,000. Reliable figures for every storage tier are not available. 

When Can I Pre-order iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo?

iPhone 18 Pro pre-orders could begin on Saturday, September 12, at midnight Pacific Time / 3 a.m. Eastern Time. The potential Saturday opening would avoid September 11, similar to Apple's approach in 2015.

manufacturing challenges potentially delaying a release until the fourth quarter of 2026. Indeed, Gurman's latest report claims the device will go on sale "as early as October."

When Do iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo Launch?

Friday, September 18 is the most likely release date for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max. It's our best educated guess, but we believe that is when deliveries and retail availability will begin. 

As already mentioned, reports remain divided on the foldable's launch schedule. There's still a possibility that its unveiling tomorrow may precede its arrival in stores by several weeks or more. 

MacRumors Coverage

Follow MacRumors.com and our MacRumorsLive account on Twitter (X) for coverage as the announcements happen. We'll have individual stories on the new products, followed by more detailed looks at their features, pricing, and availability throughout the week. Stay tuned!

title: Surprise and Shine Apple iPhone event live blog: Latest updates
content:
Macworld





Apple’s “Surprise and Shine” event might be the most anticipated iPhone keynote in 10 years. It all kicks off today, and like you, we can’t wait! So join us as we count down the hours and minutes with all the latest rumors, leaks, and speculation leading up to the big event on Wednesday, September 9, at 10 am PT.
Surprise and Shine iPhone event: How to watch
You can watch the full keynote right here using the embedded YouTube link below or on Apple.com on your iPhone or Mac. The “Watch Now” tab in the TV app on the Apple TV will also show the stream live.






Surprise and Shine iPhone event: What we expect
Apple might have dubbed this the “Surprise” event, but we have a pretty good idea what Apple is going to announce. Here’s what we expect to see:
iPhone Ultra: Apple is almost certain to launch its first folding phone this week. We’re expecting a passport-style design with a 5.5-inch cover display and a near-8-inch inner display when opened.
iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max: We expect a similar design with a faster chip and a better camera system, possibly including a variable-aperture lens for the first time.
Apple Watch Series 12: The latest Apple Watch update will reportedly be a minor refresh with a new chip, all-day heart-rate tracking, and maybe the return of a ceramic finish.
Apple Watch Ultra 4: Like the Series 12, the Ultra 4 is expected to be a minor refresh largely focused on a new chip tuned for Siri AI.
AirPods 5: Apple is rumored to be launching a new pair of low-end AirPods, but we don’t know much about them.
Smart home: It’s less likely that Apple’s rumored smart-home hub arrives at this event, but we could see an updated Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini.
Surprise and Shine iPhone event: Live blog


1 hour ago, By David Price
Don't forget the AirPods
They’ve got slightly lost in the iPhone Ultra hype, but Apple is also expected to launch the AirPods 5 today. These aren’t the camera-equipped models you may have seen doing the rounds after Apple accidentally leaked them (they’re not expected to arrive until next year). Instead, the main new feature of the AirPods 5 will be improved active noise cancellation, likely made possible by the inclusion of a new H3 chip. Bloomberg leaker Mark Gurman yesterday confirmed this–based on his sources, at any rate.

One More Thing… but what?
“We have great respect for these words,” said Tim Cook in 2017, “and we don’t use them lightly.” Those words, of course, were One More Thing.
That little phrase has signalled the arrival of some of Apple’s most iconic products and services, including the iMac G4, the MacBook Pro, FaceTime, the Apple Watch, Apple Music, and the iPhone X. Will it be uttered this year, and if so, what will it herald?
We discussed this on the podcast, and figured it would be a nice moment if new CEO John Ternus got the chance to utter those immortal words as part of his debut. (Debut as overall event host, that is. He’s spoken in individual segments before now.) The most obvious product to get the One More Thing treatment is the iPhone Ultra, but a bigger surprise would be the arrival of Apple’s long-rumored smart home hub. Either would work.
But Macworld readers put forward other ideas. At the less serious end, jimrock reckoned “It’d be really sick if he announced a $2,000 monitor stand” while Adam Moran proposed “One more thing: Now shipping iPhones with a charger.” Hashtag courage.
Moving on to things that could happen (but won’t), Rob K put forward “One more thing: iPhone Air 2 with 6,000 mAh silicon carbon battery, three cameras, and no stupid fold.” And Tower Lord suggested “AI-driven smart glasses. Minus the creep factor found in Meta glasses. Instead, true spatial computing. The ultimate personal computer.” Get rid of the AI part and we’re on board.
And finally, a note of sanity from Mike: “One more thing was Steve’s thing. Can we please stop measuring every CEO against Steve and let them be their own leaders?”
The last guy to say those three little words.

All eyes on the crease
When Apple (allegedly) unveils its first folding iPhone tomorrow, Greg Joswiak or whomever gets the honor of announcing the phone on the stream, will talk about the displays, interface, cameras, design, and anything else Apple feels is worth highlighting. What they probably won’t spend a lot of time talking about is the crease.
Ever since Samsung’s first folding phone arrived, the center display crease has been an issue. It’s gotten better over the years, but it’s still the biggest hurdle for new customers to overcome. Even on the newest phones, you can see it when it’s opened and feel a little valley while using it. It’s flies in the face of Apple’s pursuit of perfection and likely the reason why we haven’t gotten a folding iPhone until now.
Earlier this year, it was reported that Apple had devised a way to overcome the crease with a combination of ultra-thin glass (UTG) and an optically clear adhesive that allows “the folding area to be locally thinned at the bending axis to improve bendability.” Samsung’s newest flagship phone features a display with a 60-micrometer UTG layer, which is likely a similar material to what Apple will use. 
No folding phone has been able to completely eliminate the crease. Will Apple be the first?

title: Dozens of hardware IDs have been added to Apple’s services backend
content:
Macworld





At tomorrow’s Surprise and Shine event, Apple is expected to announce the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, iPhone Ultra (or whatever Apple calls its first folding iPhone), the Apple Watch Series 12, and the Apple Watch Ultra 4. Other products that might make an appearance include new AirPods, HomePod mini, and Apple TV 4K. So it’s a big event.
And Apple is geting ready. According to a social media post by Aaron Perris, dozens of hardware product identifiers have been found on Apple’s services backend. This is the list:

AppleTV18,1
HomeAccessory17,1
HomeAccessory17,2
HomeAccessory17,3
By and large these are all devices we expect to see from Apple within the next few months, but not necessarily at the Surprise and Shine event on September 9. For starters, we’re not expecting any Macs this week.
Apple adds hardware IDs to identify any specific variant of a product to its services. That means iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max both get different identifiers, and there are often separate versions for regional cellular differences. iPads of each different size get their own IDs. Same with Apple Watch: Apple has different IDs for different sizes, with and without cellular, and sometimes different materials (like the rumored ceramic option).
The interesting thing here is that there are seven iPhones listed, when we would expect to see six: US and international regional variants for the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Ultra. If there were another iPhone model on the way soon, such as the iPhone Air 2, it should have two identifiers. It’s likely the seventh is just another variant of one of the three expected models, perhaps to meet the technical needs of a specific market, but without any outwardly obvious difference in specs.
HomeAccessory listings are interesting, too. HomePods have carried the ID “AudioAccessory” in the past. Either that has changed with the new HomePod mini, or this is the listing for the rumored Home Hub device. And if that’s true, where’s the AudioAccessory listings for the new HomePod mini?
At the end of the day, this list doesn’t really tell us all that much. It includes both products that are expected soon but not necessarily at this week’s event, and also does not includes other products that are expected soon, like AirPods or HomePod mini. At any rate, we’ll know a bit more about Apple’s plans in just a few hours.

title: Foldable iPhone Duo Will Start at $2,000, Won't Launch Until at Least October
content:
Following some recent speculation that Apple could release its foldable phone under the "iPhone Duo" name, it appears that will indeed be the case, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman.


For months now, the foldable iPhone has generally been referred to as the "iPhone Ultra," even internally, but Apple is apparently going in a different direction for the official name, emphasizing the dual-screen nature of the device.

The entry-level version will include 256 gigabytes of storage, with Apple offering higher-capacity versions that will take the price all the way up to roughly $3,000. Apple blew through its cost goals due to the recent memory shortage, so it's eating some of the expense to keep within reach of $2,000. It's also passing the costs along to consumers who buy higher capacities.
As for availability, the device will reportedly come in white and dark blue and "go on sale as early as October." Rumors have long suggested the foldable iPhone could launch later than the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max due to production difficulties, although Gurman previously stressed that the gap in launch timing would be minimal.

title: 2026 iPad mini: Release date, OLED display, A19 Pro, price and latest rumors
content:
Macworld





For those who need a premium small-screen tablet, the iPad mini is a popular choice. But should you buy one now, or should you wait to see what Apple has in store for the next model? 
Most buyers should wait – the next model is expected to bring meaningful upgrades. However, Apple isn’t expected to update the iPad mini until late 2026 or maybe even early 2027, and that launch date could slip further due to chip demand and wider supply constraints.
Here’s what the latest rumors say about the release date, key upgrades, and whether it’s worth waiting. 
2026 iPad mini: Rumored changes at a glance
A19 Pro most likely
Possible OLED display upgrade
Screen size could increase from 8.3-inch to 8.5- or 8.7-inches
More water-resistant design
Vibration-based speaker system
Price increase
Improved connectivity 
iPad mini 7 vs iPad mini 8 comparison


FeatureCurrent iPad miniRumoured next iPad mini

ReleaseOctober 2024Late 2026 / early 2027
ChipA17 ProLikely A19 Pro; A18 Pro/A20 Pro possible
Display8.3-inch LCDOLED, possibly 8.5 inches
DesignCurrent designSimilar design, possibly slimmer bezels
Water resistanceNo official ratingImproved resistance rumoured
WirelessWi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.3Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, Thread
Cellular modemQualcommApple C1X expected
Cameras12MP front and rearSimilar cameras; landscape front camera is rumored
Apple IntelligenceSupportedSupported, with faster AI performance
PriceFrom $599 (was $499)Unknown; OLED could push price higher
Biggest upgrade—OLED display, faster chip and newer connectivity

 






2026 iPad mini release date: When will the new iPad mini launch?
Late 2026/early 2027
Apple has not officially announced a launch date for the next iPad mini. Earlier reports pointed to a release before the end of 2026, but more recent reporting leaves open the possibility that it could slip into early 2027. 
Back in October 2025, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported that a new iPad mini with an OLED display was among the devices Apple expected to launch before the end of 2026. Then, in July 2026, he narrowed that down further, reporting that the OLED iPad mini was scheduled for an October 2026 release.
However, in September 2026 Gurman included the iPad mini in a broader list of products expected to ship in late 2026 or early 2027, introducing some uncertainty around the exact timing.
There is still strong evidence that the new model is approaching. References to an upcoming iPad mini have reportedly been found in the macOS 26.7 release candidate, while Samsung Display is said to have begun mass production of OLED panels for the device.
The iPad mini also has a relatively unpredictable release cycle, with Apple sometimes leaving several years between updates. Wider component constraints, including pressure on RAM and other parts highlighted by Apple CEO Tim Cook earlier in 2026, could also affect the schedule, although there is no firm evidence that these have delayed the iPad mini specifically.


						

							


2026 iPad mini chip: Performance and specs 
A19 Pro chip
C1X modem
N1 chip for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6
Since it hasn’t been updated in over a year, the next iPad mini is expected to receive several silicon upgrades. The current model features an A17 Pro chip, 8GB of RAM, and Apple Intelligence support, while most rumors point to the new model adopting the A19 Pro..
In August 2025, MacRumors reported that Apple code appeared to reveal an A19 Pro-powered iPad mini. Further evidence emerged in December 2025, when Macworld reported internal Apple code indicating that the entry-level iPad would move to an A19 chip. Since Apple has traditionally given the iPad mini a more powerful processor than the standard iPad, that strengthens the case for the A19 Pro.
An A19 Pro would represent a substantial upgrade over the current A17 Pro. Users could expect faster on-device AI processing, improved gaming performance, and quicker photo and video editing. The A18 Pro, which powers the MacBook Neo, is often compared to the M1 chip and can rival the M3 in some single-core workloads. An A19 Pro-powered iPad mini would push the device even closer to iPad Air-level performance.
An A19 Pro would deliver a substantial performance boost over the A17 Pro, particularly for on-device AI, gaming, and photo and video editing, while bringing the iPad mini closer to iPad Air-level performance.
There have also been suggestions that Apple could use either the A18 Pro or A20 Pro, depending on timing and chip availability, but the A19 Pro currently appears the most likely option.
Alongside the processor upgrade, Apple is expected to bring its latest wireless technologies to the iPad mini. The N1 chip, introduced with the iPhone 17 lineup, supports Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread, and is expected to spread across the iPad lineup. Cellular models are also expected to adopt Apple’s C1X modem.
Alongside processor upgrades, Apple is expected to bring its latest wireless technologies to the iPad mini. The N1 chip, introduced with the iPhone 17 lineup, supports Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread, and is expected to spread across the iPad lineup. Cellular models are also expected to adopt Apple’s C1X modem.


						

							


2026 iPad mini: Display
OLED display upgrade

				
					

				
			
The M4 iPad Pro’s OLED Display could make its way to the iPad mini next.

Mahmoud Itani / Foundry




The biggest display upgrade rumored for the next iPad mini is the adoption of OLED technology. Following Apple’s transition of the iPad Pro to OLED in 2024, multiple reports have suggested that the iPad mini will be the next iPad to make the switch. Ross Young of DSCC was first to claim, in a tweet in October 2024, that the next iPad mini would have a OLED. 
The current iPad mini, released in October 2024, still uses a Liquid Retina IPS LCD display, but industry sources, including Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, indicate a move to OLED is increasingly likely.
The transition from LCD to OLED would represent one of the most significant upgrades in the iPad mini’s history. Unlike LCD panels, which rely on a backlight, OLED displays illuminate each pixel individually. This allows pixels to switch off completely when displaying black content, resulting in deeper blacks, higher contrast ratios, and improved HDR performance.
Key benefits of OLED include:
Superior contrast and true blacks: Individual pixel control allows OLED displays to produce true blacks and extremely high contrast.
More vibrant colours: OLED can make images appear more vivid and punchy, particularly in high-contrast scenes and HDR content.
Faster response times: Quicker pixel response can reduce motion blur and ghosting when gaming or watching fast-moving video.
Better viewing angles: Colours and contrast remain more consistent when the display is viewed from the side.
Potential efficiency benefits: OLED can use less power when displaying darker content and can enable thinner display assemblies, although bright screens may consume more power, so battery-life gains aren’t guaranteed.
An OLED panel could also enable Apple to reduce bezel sizes, potentially increasing the display area slightly without significantly changing the tablet’s overall dimensions. Some reports suggest the screen could grow from 8.3 inches to around 8.5 inches as a result – more on that below.
While the iPad mini is unlikely to inherit premium display technologies such as ProMotion or the tandem OLED architecture used in the iPad Pro, the move to OLED would still deliver a noticeable improvement in visual quality, with richer blacks, better contrast, improved colour reproduction, and stronger HDR performance.
For users who prioritise display quality, an OLED iPad mini would address one of the most frequently cited limitations of the current model and bring the compact tablet much closer to the viewing experience offered by Apple’s premium devices.


						

							


2026 iPad mini: Design
Same size, bigger screen possible
More water-resistant design rumored

				
					

				
			
Apple




The iPad mini has retained the same design since its major redesign in 2021, and the 2026 model is expected to keep that overall look. However, Apple could increase the display size slightly while maintaining the device’s current dimensions.
In December 2024, analysts at Display Supply Chain Consultants (DSCC) suggested in a supply chain analyst report that the next-generation iPad mini could feature an 8.5-inch display, up from the current model’s 8.3-inch panel. The reports indicated that the chassis size would remain unchanged, meaning Apple could achieve the larger screen through slimmer bezels rather than a larger body.
A larger display may also help the iPad mini maintain its place in Apple’s lineup as foldable devices arrive. Apple’s long-rumored foldable iPhone – often referred to as the iPhone Fold or iPhone Ultra – is expected to feature an inner display measuring between 7.6 and 7.8 inches with a 4:3 aspect ratio, putting it close to the iPad mini’s screen size. While still smaller than the iPad mini, such a device could appeal to some users who currently favour Apple’s smallest tablet. 
Another rumor gaining traction is that the new iPad mini will be more water-resistant. That rumor comes from Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, who in October 2025 claimed Apple was developing a next-generation iPad mini with a significantly more water-resistant chassis. 
The design changes could include: 
Redesigned casing with improved sealing around ports. 
According to Gurman, a new speaker system could use vibration-based audio technology to eliminate traditional speaker holes.
There’s also a strong possibility of new colour options. Apple currently offers the iPad mini in Blue, Purple, Starlight, and Space Gray, while the previous generation was available in Pink, Purple, Starlight, and Space Gray.


						

							


2026 iPad mini: Cameras 
Little or no camera upgrade expected

				
					

				
			
Apple is not expected to upgrade the cameras in the next iPad mini.

Foundry




The current iPad mini has a 12MP Wide rear camera and 12MP Ultra Wide Center Stage front camera, and there are no credible reports suggesting major camera system upgrades for the next iPad mini.
The most likely change concerns camera placement rather than camera hardware. Apple has moved the front-facing camera to the landscape edge on its latest iPad models, and the iPad mini could follow suit to improve the experience during video calls and FaceTime sessions when used with a keyboard or stand.
While the cameras themselves may remain unchanged, image quality could still benefit from improvements to the image signal processor and computational photography capabilities of a newer A-series chip.


						

							


2026 iPad mini: Price 
The iPad mini had held the same $499/£499 starting price since its 2021 redesign. That changed in June 2026, when Apple increased the entry-level price to $599/£599.
With Apple having already raised the price this year, we think another increase with the next iPad mini is unlikely, although the move to OLED could put some pressure on costs.


						

							


Should I wait to buy a new iPad mini? 
The current iPad mini’s A17 Pro chip is still plenty fast for everyday use, gaming and creative apps. An OLED display could make the next model significantly more appealing, but its launch timing remains uncertain. With discounts likely on the current model, buy now if you value portability and performance; wait if display quality matters most.

title: The Apple Watch SE 3 is unavailable everywhere for some reason
content:
Macworld





In less the 24 hours, Apple will kick off its Surprise and Shine event and unveil its latest slate of new devices, including at least two new Apple Watches, the Series 12 and Ultra 4. But some pre-event shuffling at the Apple Store could point to a third watch announcement during the keynote.
Based on the rumors and its usual cadence, we expected the Apple Watch SE 3 to stick around for another 12 months. But on Monday afternoon, all models and colors suddenly disappeared from the online Apple Store. Whichever case, size, connectivity, or band you pick shows “Currently Unavailable” for shipping or pickup. Even on third-party resellers such as Amazon, the Apple Watch Series 3 doesn’t list a delivery date.
You can purchase an Apple Watch Series 11 or Ultra 3 without a problem.
It’s unclear what this means. Apple doesn’t typically stop selling old models ahead of announcements, instead opting to upgrade buyers to the latest model for devices that haven’t shipped. This could mean Apple plans to discontinue the line or change it significantly, requiring an immediate halt to sales.
We should find out what’s going on with the Apple Watch SE 3 after tomorrow’s keynote, which begins at 10 a.m. PT.

title: Potential iPhone 18 Pro camera software features found in iOS 27 beta code
content:
Macworld





The iPhone 18 Pro is almost here. On the eve of Apple’s big Surprise and Shine event, we have some last-minute info on what we might expect from the camera on Apple’s new Pro iPhone.
This latest leak comes via MacRumors, where one of its regular forum members found some code in the iOS 27 beta that points to five potential new Camera software features:
Exposure scopes: Adds waveforms or histograms for the viewfinder to better see exposure across your shot.
Focus peaking and highlight warnings: Another common professional camera feature, focus peaking highlights edges that are in focus, and highlight warnings mark areas of the viewfinder (usually with zebra-stripes) that are overexposed and will be blown out.
Repeated self-timer shots: Lets you take several shots in a row, with a countdown timer in between.
Manual focus: A control to set and lock focus, similar to what is found in the Final Cut Camera app. There was something like this in iOS 26, but the first iOS 27 beta removed it. MacRumors says the underlying focus-locking code is still there, but Apple has restricted it to devices that ship with ‌iOS 27‌ or later.
Aperture-based image correction: This is a change to the image processing pipeline to account for variable apertures on the same camera. A variable-aperture wide camera is one of the expected features of the iPhone 18 Pro Max and possibly the regular iPhone 18 Pro as well.
Only that last feature—which is more of an internal processing change—would rely on the new camera hardware in the iPhone 18 Pro, which has been rumored. The rest could easily come to all modern iPhone cameras, and in fact those exact features have been found in third-party camera apps for years (and the Manual Focus in Apple’s own apps). Still, Apple sometimes locks software features to new devices even when not strictly necessary as a way to make a new hardware purchase more appealing.
We’ll find out more on September 9 at Apple’s Surprise and Shine event.

title: Code leak reveals four new Apple Watch Series 12 features
content:
Macworld





The headline announcements of tomorrow’s Surprise and Shine press event will revolve around the iPhone, but don’t forget the Apple Watch. We’re expecting some quietly valuable updates to the market-leading smartwatch, and a new code leak offers hints about what exactly Apple is about to reveal.
According to pdfu, a regular contributor to the MacRumors forums, the new models (the Series 12 and Ultra 4) will get four upgrades on the previous generation. This prediction is based on insights gleaned from watchOS 27 and iOS 27 beta code. Here are the highlights from what they’ve found:
1. A new optical sensor
watchOS 27 mentions a new optical sensing family called Sunstone4p0, which suggests the new watches will get a hardware upgrade in this area. According to pdfu’s findings, the new sensor seems likely to feature improved signal filtering and lower electronic noise for more accurate heart readings when the pulse signal is weak. It’s also been previously reported that the new watches will have continuous heart-rate tracking, which also somewhat corroborates the need for a new sensor.
2. Extra storage
A storage profile associated with T8320, widely believed to be the CPU of the Series 12 and Ultra 4, is labelled 1024gb. This suggests the new watches will have 1,024 gigabits, or 128GB, of storage, up from 64GB on current models. That’s a lot for a watch and probably means at least some Apple Intelligence stuff wil be stored on the device.
3. A new app
The Apple Watch is about to get a new pre-installed app called Readiness. This feels like something that would be included in the watchOS 27 announcements at WWDC in the summer, but it wasn’t: pdfu thinks Apple “may be holding back some of the biggest features in watchOS 27 for its September launch.”
It isn’t clear what Readiness will do, but the name and placement in the default app grid suggest something to do with preparing for or recovering from a workout. In a partial corroboration of this prediction, Mark Gurman says Readiness will be a variant of the Vitals app and “compete with software from Whoop & Oura.”
4. Better strength workouts
The Workout app is one of the Apple Watch’s greatest strengths. Ironically, however, strength workouts specifically are currently quite weak. You simply can’t record a lot of data about your weights sessions. As of this fall, and based on iOS 27 and watchOS 27 betas, that’s about to change. You’ll be able to record multiple sets, with varied weights and reps, as part of a single workout.
The Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 are expected to be announced as part of the Surprise and Shine event on Wednesday, September 9. For all the latest news and rumors heading up to the event, check our regularly updated Apple Watch Series 12 superguide.

title: Apple Sued Over Alleged Face ID Patent Infringement
content:
TrinamiX, a subsidiary of the German chemical giant BASF, is suing Apple in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Texas, accusing the company of infringing seven patents related to face authentication technology used in Face ID.


In its complaint, first reported by Reuters, trinamiX said it spent years developing technology to stop people from fooling face unlock systems with a photo, a fake mask, or a silicone copy of someone's face.

The complaint says Apple's original version of ‌Face ID‌, introduced with the iPhone X in 2017, did not use trinamiX's technology, but that newer iPhones and iPads do. TrinamiX's system is designed to tell real skin apart from things like photos or masks, essentially adding a check that catches fakes conventional optical face scanning methods would miss.

The complaint alleges that "Apple knew or should have known of the high probability that updating its iPhones and iPads to incorporate ‌Face ID‌ using material and skin detection" infringed seven trinamiX patents, causing "substantial damages and irreparable injury." The seven patents cover two areas: detecting skin during face unlock and identifying what material something is made of.

iPhone 16, iPhone 16e, ‌iPhone 16‌ Plus, ‌iPhone 16‌ Pro, ‌iPhone 16‌ Pro Max, iPhone 17, iPhone 17e, iPhone 17 Pro, ‌iPhone 17 Pro‌ Max, iPhone Air, 11-inch iPad Pro (4th generation), 12.9-inch ‌iPad Pro‌ (6th generation), and the 11- and 13-inch ‌iPad Pro‌ models with the M4 and M5 chips. 

IP Fray.

title: Apple Acquires Startup Working on 'Breakthrough Sensing Technology'
content:
Earlier this year, Apple acquired California-based startup Sonera, according to a notice published today on the European Commission's website.


Sonera previously announced that it had developed "breakthrough sensing technology" that "non-invasively measures magnetic fields" generated by the brain and body. The company said its technology can analyze neural data without direct skin contact, giving it an advantage over traditional electrical sensing techniques.

"This proprietary technology holds the key to making brain activity as easy to measure as heart rate, temperature, and other physiological signals," said Sonera, in a 2023 press release. The company said its technology was "poised to enable an entirely new class of consumer wearables and experiences based on muscle activity."

title: Foldable iPhone Development History and Price Revealed in New Report
content:
Former Apple CEO Tim Cook played a major role in the development of the foldable iPhone, which could reach around $3,000 with storage upgrades, according to new details shared by Bloomberg's Mark Gurman. 


Early in the development of the foldable iPhone, the company reportedly targeted a starting retail price of $1,999, hoping to come under the "potentially controversial $2,000 barrier." The idea was to replicate the debut of the iPhone X in 2017, which started at $999.

Amid the impact of the global memory shortage, Apple is said to have recently discussed pricing the foldable at $2,199. Some storage configurations could approach $3,000. While the company anticipates some "sticker shock" for consumers, the willingness of customers to spend around $2,000 on iPhone models with upgraded storage convinced the company that an "upscale foldable device was worth bringing to market."

Gurman also revealed details about the history of the foldable iPhone inside Apple. Around 2020, Cook apparently returned from a visit to Asia "unusually energized" about foldable phones. During the trip, he saw growing numbers of consumers using foldable devices from the likes of Samsung and Huawei. He came to believe that Apple needed an equivalent offering in the market and pushed the company to accelerate its development efforts. 

iPad mini that could unfold into a larger tablet. Cook wanted the final device to be more mainstream in the form of a foldable iPhone, and his level of involvement in the project was unusual. 

The project was conceived under Dan Riccio, who preceded John Ternus as head of hardware engineering. The company apparently prioritized resolving four main challenges: reducing the visibility of the display crease, improving hinge reliability, creating a new flexible cover glass for the inner display, and developing under-display camera technology. 

The company eventually settled on a hinge system made using titanium and aluminum and custom cover glass developed with Corning. Despite being less durable than other existing iPhone models, Apple is said to believe that the construction quality of the foldable iPhone is industry-leading for the foldable market, and thinks it has an advantage over Android devices in terms of software. 

Gurman restated several of the device's rumored specifications, including a 7.8-inch inner display, a 5.5-inch outer display, and a wide form-factor design. During development, Apple designers apparently compared the folded proportions of the device to a passport and the unfolded proportions to a Magic Trackpad. The short-and-wide design was chosen to provide a point of differentiation with rival foldable and generate  consumer interest.

He reiterated that the foldable iPhone may be less durable than a conventional iPhone, with an inferior camera system and less battery life. Despite these drawbacks, Apple employees are said to believe "the company will sell every foldable phone it can produce."

Gurman also noted that the foldable iPhone's engineering complexity "makes it an ideal showcase" for new CEO John Ternus, following his career as Apple's hardware chief. Ternus was apparently a major champion of the device and played a major role to "push it over the finish line," alongside Cook.

title: 2024 vs. 2026 Mac Mini Buyer's Guide
content:
Last month, Apple announced a new Mac mini built around the all-new M6 chip and the M5 Pro, replacing the M4 and M4 Pro models that had been on sale since October 2024. Pre-orders are open now, with the machines arriving to customers and in stores on September 22.


The M6 model starts at $899 and the M5 Pro model at $1,699, each $100 above what its predecessor was selling for by the end of its run and $300 above what their predecessors launched at. The ‌Mac mini‌ rose from $599 to $799 in May, and the M4 Pro configuration went from $1,399 to $1,599 in June, both as a consequence of the memory shortage driven by AI demand. Education pricing brings the new models down to $799 and $1,599 respectively.

What Changed Across Both Models

A number of upgrades apply equally to the standard and Pro configurations, regardless of which chip you choose:
 


‌Mac mini‌ (2024)
‌Mac mini‌ (2026)



Neural Accelerators in each GPU core



Variable refresh rate and HDR support


Wi-Fi 6E connectivity
Wi-Fi 7 connectivity



Apple N1 wireless networking chip


Bluetooth 5.3
Bluetooth 6



Thread networking technology


Gigabit Ethernet or 10Gb Ethernet
2.5Gb Ethernet or 10Gb Ethernet



Genlock support over USB-C




Mac Mini With M4 vs. M6

Here is everything else that differs between the M4 and M6 versions of the ‌Mac mini‌:
 


‌Mac mini‌ (M4)
‌Mac mini‌ (M6)


M4 chip
M6 chip


10-core CPU with four performance cores and six efficiency cores
12-core CPU with two super cores, four performance cores, and six efficiency cores


10-core GPU
12-core GPU


16-core Neural Engine
Dual 16-core Neural Engine


120GB/s memory bandwidth
153GB/s memory bandwidth, rising to 170GB/s with 24GB or 32GB of unified memory


Two displays up to 6K at 60Hz, plus a third up to 5K at 60Hz
Two displays up to 6K at 60Hz or 4K at 165Hz, plus a third up to 5K at 60Hz



Up to two external displays over a single Thunderbolt port


Now discontinued
From $899




Mac Mini With M4 Pro vs. M5 Pro

The comparison below outlines the remaining differences between the two Pro configurations:
 


‌Mac mini‌ (M4 Pro)
‌Mac mini‌ (M5 Pro)


M4 Pro chip
M5 Pro chip


Base: 12-core CPU with eight performance cores and four efficiency cores
Configurable to: 14-core CPU
Base: 15-core CPU with five super cores and 10 performance cores
Configurable to: 18-core CPU



Enhanced shader core and third-generation ray tracing


273GB/s memory bandwidth
307GB/s memory bandwidth


Three displays up to 6K at 60Hz
Three displays up to 6K at 60Hz or 4K at 165Hz


Two displays: one up to 8K at 60Hz or 4K at 240Hz, plus a second up to 6K at 60Hz
Two displays: one up to 8K at 60Hz, 5K at 120Hz, or 4K at 240Hz, plus a second up to 5K at 120Hz or 4K at 200Hz



Up to three external displays over a single Thunderbolt port


Now discontinued
From $1,699




How Much Faster Is It, Really?

The latest refresh is minor for ordinary work and significant for AI workflows. Against the M4, Apple claims 40% faster CPU performance and 2x faster graphics, which is a normal generational step, alongside unusually large gains of up to 4x faster AI performance and up to 4.8x faster prompt processing in LM Studio. Almost all of the engineering appears to have gone into AI optimization, in the form of Neural Accelerators built into every GPU core for the first time on the ‌Mac mini‌ and a Neural Engine doubled to two 16-core units. The M5 Pro follows the same pattern, at up to 4x faster than the M4 Pro for prompt processing but only 1.4x faster for ray-traced rendering in Blender.
 
Display support is the one significant change beyond the chips. Both models add 4K at 165Hz and variable refresh rate, which the 2024 machines never supported, and the M5 Pro can drive a second display at 5K at 120Hz where the M4 Pro capped it at 6K at 60Hz. If you own a high refresh rate monitor, this is perhaps the most noticeable difference in the entire update.

It is worth noting that Apple's figure of up to 170GB/s for the M6 only applies to the 24GB and 32GB configurations. The 16GB models run at 153GB/s, so the gain over the M4's 120GB/s is around 28% for many buyers rather than the 42% implied. Bandwidth governs how fast a model's weights move out of memory, which makes the 32GB configuration a faster machine.
 
The memory ceilings are also not the increases they appear to be. The M4 shipped with a 32GB option and the M4 Pro with 64GB when they launched in October 2024, and Apple removed both in May as memory prices climbed. The new models restore those ceilings rather than raising them, so a 32GB M4 or 64GB M4 Pro already has the same ceiling as its 2026 equivalent.

Which to Choose?

If you own a 2024 ‌Mac mini‌ and do not run AI models on it, skip this generation. A 40% CPU improvement is not something you will notice in daily use, and nothing else meaningful about the machine has changed. The exception is display support: if you have a high refresh rate monitor stuck at 60Hz, that is a real problem the new models solve and the old ones never will.
 
If you do run models locally, the upgrade is easy to justify from an M4, but more difficult from an M4 Pro. Roughly 4x faster prompt processing changes what you can attempt. From an M4 Pro you get unchanged GPU core counts, a 12% bandwidth increase, and a $300 rise over what you paid, so wait for the next year's revision unless you specifically need to upgrade to a 64GB model.
 
For new buyers, the gap between the two 2026 models is wider than the $800 price difference suggests: the M5 Pro has 80% more memory bandwidth, double the memory ceiling, and 50% more CPU cores at the top. Since tools like LM Studio and Ollama run on the GPU rather than the Neural Engine, capacity and bandwidth are what matter. Memory capacity decides which models you can load at all, while bandwidth determines how fast they run. If your models fit in 32GB, buy the M6 at $899. If they do not, the M5 Pro is your only option here.
 
The 2024 models remain worth considering even though Apple has stopped selling them new, with availability via third parties, Apple's refurbished store, or second-hand.
 
Do not expect prices to collapse in the usual way, whichever route you take. The memory shortage pushed Apple's prices up, twice during the M4's final year, so a modest discount off $799 is unremarkable. The M4 model is worth buying nearer the $599 it launched at, and much above that, the stretch to buy a new M6 is difficult to argue against.
 
The 32GB M4 and 64GB M4 Pro were only sold between October 2024 and May 2026, so they exist on the used market but were unavailable new for the machine's final months. A 64GB M4 Pro matches the memory ceiling of a $1,699 M5 Pro at 273GB/s against 307GB/s, for considerably less. For running larger models on a budget, that may be the most cost-effective configuration.

title: Apple acquires brain imaging firm for health and accessibility features
content:
Apple has bought Sonera, a California company that makes non-invasive sensors that can measure neural signals from the brain, with health benefits ranging from muscle monitoring to active thought control of devices.


Nishita Deka (left) and Dominic Labanowski, co-founders of Sonera - image credit: Sonera.

content:
Apple may be considering scrapping the standard iPhone 18 entirely and rebranding the iPhone Air 2 as its new $999 entry point when the more affordable iPhone models launch in spring 2027, a sketchy rumor claims.


The claim comes from the X account "Early Apple," who said Apple is "exploring the idea" of having the Air 2 simply take over the ‌iPhone 18‌ name and price point rather than launching as a separate device. 

iPhone 18 Pro models and Apple's first foldable iPhone arriving later this month. Given how firmly that three way split has held up in the rumor cycle so far, a rebrand this drastic looks unlikely for 2027.

covered leaks from the account before, including an alleged ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ prototype photo back in April, but as we noted at the time, Early Apple is a relatively new account of unknown origin with no established track record, so the claim is best treated as an informed guess. That makes it plausible that a future standard iPhone could eventually resemble the Air, even if an outright merger during the upcoming product cycle remains a stretch.

title: Is the John Ternus honeymoon already over?
content:
Macworld





John Ternus has been Apple CEO all of a week so it’s time to start stirring things up! Hey, he’s had seven whole days!
Writing for Bloomberg, Mark Gurman is here to dish the dirt and lob some Baby Ruths over the fence and into Ternus’s pool, and he’s all out of, uh, dirt, I guess, in this metaphor? That one kind of got away from the Macalope.
“Tim Cook’s CEO-Like Pay Package Shows He Isn’t Going Anywhere” (subscription required)
In regard to the timing of Cook’s exit, Gurman says it’s to give Ternus “a massive tailwind” while Apple is at the top of its game.
If Cook waited another two or three years to give the job to Ternus, the cupboard of genuinely new and impressive products could be bare.
BREAKING: APPLE ALMOST OUT OF IDEAS. ONLY TWO OR THREE YEARS UNTIL COMPANY SHIPS VISION PRO SOCKS.
It’s also unclear where Apple would sit in the technology hierarchy after OpenAI and Anthropic become public companies…
Right where it sits now? The Macalope will just leave this piece by Horace Dediu right there for you. Pondering AI’s “killer app” moment, which has yet to happen, Dediu says:
I don’t think it’s ChatGPT. That’s like saying TCP/IP. That’s like saying Intel 8088…
Having worked first for 9to5Mac and now Bloomberg, Gurman has not seen the world from the trenches of corporate America (“IT WAS HELL,” RECALLS SURVIVOR).
It would mark a first for Apple, whose previous CEO transitions were anything but orderly, including Cook’s own succession of Jobs amid the company co-founder’s illness.
While you could point to a few things that could have gone better (Scott Forstall), the transition from Jobs to Cook was hardly a “The Purge”-style nightmare of fear, bedlam, and anarchy. It’s not like Jobs died and the Board of Directors broke a pool cue and locked Apple executives in a meeting room to fight for the position. Jobs made Cook CEO. That was pretty much that.
Again, other than Scott Forstall, whose dog apparently ate the memo.
Gurman is not wrong, however, about Cook’s new salary and position being an unusual arrangement that raises a lot of questions about just how this is all going to work. It’ll probably be fine, but it’s probably also not going to be that different, which makes one wonder how Ternus will be able to make his mark on the company.
Gurman has one more decidedly not “fun-sized” Baby Ruth to lob, this time into the Apple community’s collective pool.
But there’s a bit more to the story, I’m told.
TERNUS IS MIKE MARKKULA’S SECRET LOVE CHILD… wait, no, that’s not it.

				
					

				
			
If you’d like to receive regular news and updates to your inbox, sign up for our newsletters, including The Macalope and Apple Breakfast, David Price’s weekly, bite-sized roundup of all the latest Apple news and rumors.

Foundry





Ternus and services chief Eddy Cue want to make even more money from the App Store and figure out ways to raise margins and squeeze additional recurring revenue from the platform. Schiller, on the other hand, seems to believe that such moves will only further irk developers and governments. While there was no internal blowup or anything like that, it’s something he wanted no part of.
It would be ironic if, after years of developers dragging Schiller for App Store woes, he turned out to be the one keeping it from being even worse all along. (If this turns out to be the case, in lieu of sending Phil a nice fruit basket, developers can just send donations to the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution.)
But you have to wonder who Gurman’s sources are here. It’s not like Schiller called him and said, “Mark, it is time I told you the dark secret about the App Store! Do you have a pen? Because I’ll be naming names. First off… CUE. That’s with a ‘C,’ not a ‘Q’.” Certainly no one close to these executives spoke to Gurman. So who else would be in a position to know (or think they know) and be willing to talk out of school? Certainly a former Apple employee might be willing, which makes it possible that the sound you hear is the grinding of some axes.
No, not that sound. That sound is your CD of “Pocket Full of Kryptonite” by The Spin Doctors that fell behind the credenza in 1998 and landed in front of the air vent and has been rattling ever since. This is more of a GEEENEEERRRRRTTTT noise. Yeah, that’s the one.
Let’s just be clear that the Macalope really hopes Gurman is wrong about this. Apple has already been blinkered enough on the issue, and the idea of it doubling down and raising its take or worsening terms for developers really boggles the imagination. Maybe this represents attitudes Ternus and Cue no longer have; maybe cooler heads will still prevail.
Or maybe we’re just going to keep complaining about the App Store until the heat death of the universe.

title: Five iPhone 18 Pro Camera Features Seemingly Leak in Code
content:
Apple is working on a broader set of Camera app improvements in iOS 27 it has announced, according to a new deep dive from MacRumors forum member "pdfu."


‌iOS 27‌ beta code apparently points to five features that could arrive alongside new iPhone models this week or in a future software update:


Exposure scopes: The Camera app can display a waveform or histogram to help judge exposure while shooting. A histogram shows how much of the image is too dark, too bright, or in between, while a waveform shows similar information but keeps it lined up with where those areas are in the frame.

Focus peaking and highlight warnings: New code overlays helpful information right on top of the camera preview. Focus peaking highlights the edges of whatever's in sharp focus using a colored outline, while a separate overlay warns when part of the image is getting overexposed, using a solid color, a pulsing color, diagonal stripes, or a checkerboard pattern.

Repeated self-timer shots: Apple is adding the ability to take several timed photos in a row rather than just one. After each shot, the countdown starts again right away instead of waiting for the photo to finish saving, so the shots can be taken back to back.

Manual focus: A control for manually setting and locking focus, rather than relying on autofocus, has also turned up in testing, similar to what's already available in Apple's Final Cut Camera app. A version of this existed in iOS 26 with a focus slider, but that slider was removed in ‌iOS 27‌ beta 1. The underlying focus-locking code is still there, but Apple has restricted it to devices that ship with ‌iOS 27‌ or later, so it won't work on any current iPhone.

Aperture-based image correction: A change to how photos are processed could be tied to a future iPhone with a variable aperture, a lens opening that can widen or narrow rather than staying fixed. ‌iOS 27‌ can adjust lens corrections depending on the aperture setting, blending between up to four reference points to smooth out the results.
 

iPhone 18 Pro is widely expected to offer a variable aperture main camera suggests that at least some of the capabilities could arrive with the new models.

title: Xiaomi Announces Foldable iPhone Rival
content:
Xiaomi today officially announced the 18 Fold, its first wide-format foldable, at a product event in China, two days before Apple is expected to unveil its own first foldable iPhone.


The Xiaomi 18 Fold uses a similar wide-folding design to the Samsung Z Fold8 and Apple's upcoming foldable iPhone. It features a 5.38-inch outer display and a 7.58-inch inner display, both with 120Hz LTPO technology and 4000 nits of peak brightness. The display is protected by a new double-layer ultra-thin glass structure.

The phone folds around a redesigned hinge Xiaomi calls the "Dragon Bone" hinge, which the company says underwent 492 structural optimizations, facilitating a noticeably more rounded design than Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold8. It launches in four finishes, including a Nishino Red colorway and a limited Ceramic Special Edition capped at 1,500 units.

3nm process with a 10-core CPU clocked to 4.35GHz and a 16-core GPU. Xiaomi says the chip delivers a 60% multi-core CPU gain and an 85% GPU performance gain over its predecessor, with power draw down 25% and 64% respectively, alongside a dedicated NPU rated at 200 TOPS.

The rear camera system was developed with Leica and is led by a 200-megapixel main sensor, alongside a 50-megapixel ultrawide and a 50-megapixel periscope telephoto lens with 3.5x optical zoom. Apple's first foldable iPhone is expected to feature two rear cameras only, with no dedicated telephoto camera. 

The device ships with Xiaomi's HyperOS 4 software and a 6,000mAh battery supporting 67W wired and 50W wireless charging. Pricing starts at 10,999 yuan (approximately $1,638), for the base 12GB RAM and 256GB storage configuration, rising to 14,999 yuan (approximately $2,235) for the top 16GB/1TB model, with a limited Ceramic Special Edition at 15,999 yuan (approximately $2,384). Apple's foldable is widely expected to be priced above $2,000.

Xiaomi also introduced the Xiaomi Pad 9 Pro Max tablet at the event, which shares the Xring O3 chip, along with three electric vehicles under its Pengcheng brand. The company has not announced global availability for the 18 Fold; its earlier Mix Fold foldables have stayed exclusive to China.

title: iPhone 18 Pro Event Could Hit Apple Shares, KeyBanc Warns
content:
Apple's September 9 iPhone announcement event could become a negative catalyst for the stock, KeyBanc Capital Markets warns.  


In a research note seen by Investing.com, KeyBanc said the event could motivate investors to weigh pricing decisions against the impact of higher costs on demand and margins. KeyBanc added that Apple faces a choice to either raise prices broadly to offset gross margin pressure, which could hurt unit volumes and trigger "sticker shock," or raise prices more selectively.

This could invite greater scrutiny of margins and raise the prospect of further price increases later down the line. The firm maintained an "Underweight" rating on Apple and a $250 price target, against a share price of $324.96 at the time of publication.

iPhone 18 lineup builds at around 80 million units across the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 and first quarter of fiscal 2027, down from roughly 91 million units a year earlier. The firm attributed most of the decline to the absence of a base ‌iPhone 18‌ model in this part of the product cycle, with higher pricing and a richer product mix expected to partially offset the lower volumes.

On Wednesday, Apple will hold a press event with the tagline “Surprise and Shine.” Officially we don’t know what products will be announced, but in reality we’re 95% sure the day’s reveals will include iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max handsets. And that number might have just gone up even further with the leak of a video showing demo models of the new phones.
A very brief video clip posted this weekend to the Naver platform appears to show two devices: an iPhone 18 Pro Max, and an iPhone 18 Pro. We can tell this partly because there’s a retail-style label in front of them, but also because they’re finished in colors that aren’t available as part of the current or recent iPhone range. In the video, one iPhone is a dark red/burgundy, the other a light blue, appearing to provide the strongest visual evidence yet for the iPhone 18 Pro colors exclusively revealed by Macworld.
The only other phone we see is a dark-blue iPhone 17 Pro Max, which the poster holds against the Dark Cherry 18 Pro Max for comparison.
The poster doesn’t offer much context for the video; the headline (via Google Translate) reads simply “iPhone 18 Pro Max Dark Cherry & 18 Pro Blue demo devices exposed” and the body text adds nothing further. But from the items in the background, including the aforementioned label, clear plastic stands, and security cables, it appears that we’re looking at a retail display for the new phones. Given how soon they will need to appear in stores, it’s plausible that outlets will have already received demo units, although it’s obviously risky for one to allow footage to leak online before the announcements.
We can’t guarantee that the video is genuine, and it wouldn’t be hugely difficult to fake footage of this sort. But there isn’t a strong reason to doubt it, and the evidence for these two colors is growing stronger with each passing day.
The iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max, unless something very unexpected happens, will be announced at the event on Wednesday, starting at 10 a.m. E.T. Our iPhone event live blog is already up and running and will report all the breaking news and rumors as we find them.
And if you’d like to read the announcements before they happen… our crack reporters managed to get their hands on the script. Just don’t tell anyone, or we’ll get in trouble.

title: iPhone 18 Pro: Nine Reasons Not to Upgrade This Year
content:
Apple is set to unveil new iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max models on Wednesday, September 9, and the devices are expected to feature a design that's largely similar to the iPhone 17 Pro models, with a peppering of enhancements inside. Major changes are not expected until next year, when Apple is expected to introduce a radically redesigned 20th-anniversary iPhone.


If you're thinking of trading in your current iPhone for this year's latest, consider the following features rumored to be coming to next September's iPhone 20 models (Apple is expected to skip the iPhone 19 for its commemorative edition). Taken together, they may just give you pause for thought.

  
A quad-curved, all-glass design: The display glass reportedly curves away on all four sides of the iPhone 20, concealing the metal frame during normal use for a borderless effect. Apple is said to be working with Samsung on an "equal-depth quad-curved" display to achieve the feat.

Advanced OLED technology: Apple is planning to use a brighter, thinner OLED panel for the 20th anniversary iPhone. Rumors suggest that Apple will adopt Samsung ‌OLED‌ displays with Color Filter on Encapsulation (COE) technology, which reduces the thickness of the overall display stack, and lets more light through to improve brightness while reducing power draw.

  
Under-display Face ID and camera: Apple is reportedly continuing to test hardware that would eliminate the Dynamic Island – the visible cutout – from the front of the device, with Face ID components moving under the screen and an under-camera display said to be in development. Whether the technology will be ready in time for a fall 2027 launch remains uncertain.

Custom Apple image sensor: Apple is said to be developing its own stacked image sensor to replace the Sony sensors it has traditionally used for the iPhone. Apple has reportedly already developed a working prototype. The sensor is said to use LOFIC technology, which would let each pixel store varying amounts of light and potentially reach up to 20 stops of dynamic range.

  
Solid-state buttons: Apple is said to be testing haptic replacements for the Side, Volume, Action, and Camera Control buttons. The buttons could be integrated directly into the device's frame, with no actual physical movement when pressed, yet retaining a tactile responsiveness.

  
A 2-nanometer A21 chip: The 20th anniversary models are expected to feature a second-generation 2-nanometer chip. With the upcoming iPhone 18 Pro models widely expected to debut the A20 Pro chip, the anniversary models would likely be powered by the A21 Pro.

  
Silicon anode battery: Apple is reportedly exploring a new battery technology that uses a silicon anode capable of storing more lithium ions per gram, potentially delivering longer battery life without increasing the physical size of the battery.

  
Mobile high bandwidth memory: Apple is rumored to be evaluating vertically stacked DRAM technology to improve memory bandwidth and boost on-device AI performance.

  
Two sizes: The two anniversary models could have a larger display size compared to this September's iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, which are expected to use 6.3-inch and 6.9-inch displays similar to iPhone 17 Pro models. In contrast, Apple is rumored to be prototyping a 6.4-inch display for the iPhone 20 Pro, and a 7-inch display for the larger 20 Pro Max.

With all that said, we're still 12 months out, and Apple's plans shift constantly behind closed doors, plus features this ambitious have a habit of slipping a year or two. Under-display Face ID in particular has been "two years away" for about five years now.

Instead, the app complements Apple’s existing iPhone security by concentrating on areas where users can still expose themselves to risk: insecure Wi-Fi, unprotected internet connections and important iOS security settings that haven’t been enabled. That distinction matters. iPhones are resistant to traditional malware because of Apple’s tightly controlled security architecture, but they aren’t immune from spyware, exploits, malicious websites, compromised accounts and other privacy and security threats.
The new iPhone app is available to new and existing Intego ONE Complete subscribers. Intego is also currently a Back to School promotion that cuts the price by 50% until September 30. Intego confirmed that you don’t need to prove you are a student to take advantage of the offer.

What is Intego ONE?
Intego ONE is the successor to Intego Internet Security X9, combining Mac antivirus protection with additional security and maintenance tools. It’s currently our top recommendation in our Best Antivirus for Mac guide. 
It comes in three tiers:

We’ve already reviewed Intego ONE Complete on the Mac, where its malware detection, scanning performance and firewall controls particularly impressed us. In our testing, it handled more than 130 malware samples extremely well and scanned more than two million files in around eight minutes.
