What does Intego ONE do on an iPhone?

				
					

				
			
Intego’s iPhone app
adds a VPN, Wi-Fi security checks and iPhone security monitoring, but not antivirus scanning.

 
The iPhone version of Intego ONE is essentially a combination of privacy protection, network security and security configuration checking.
There are three main elements.
Intego VPN
When you’re using hotel, café, airport or other Wi-Fi that you don’t control, Intego’s VPN can encrypt your internet connection.
The VPN was already included with Intego ONE Complete on the Mac, where it encrypts internet traffic, masks the user’s IP address and can help protect data when using public or unsecured Wi-Fi.
When we tested it as part of our Mac review we found it simple to use, with 51 server locations and good bandwidth and streaming performance, although it isn’t as fully featured as some dedicated VPN services.
Adding the VPN to the iPhone arguably makes the feature more useful, because your phone is much more likely to connect to unfamiliar Wi-Fi while you’re travelling or away from home.
Wi-Fi security checks
Intego can also check the security of the Wi-Fi network your iPhone is currently using.
The test takes around 10 seconds and reports on connection speed as well as any potential security issues it identifies. Intego told us that one of the main things it checks is whether the network is using strong encryption.
iPhone security check-up
The app can also inspect some of the protections already built into your iPhone and tell you whether they are enabled or being used.
Intego says its Device Check-Up can check whether:
A passcode is enabled.
Face ID or Touch ID is enabled.
Apps are permitted to track you.
The iPhone is running the newest version of iOS it supports.
Something has been changed that removes Apple’s security protections.
Screen recording is active.
The key benefit is not that Intego provides these protections itself. Apple already does that. Instead, Intego checks whether important security features are enabled and flags potential weaknesses.
Intego confirmed that its warning about changes that remove Apple’s built-in protections refers primarily to jailbreak detection. It does not generally treat MDM profiles as suspicious, since these are commonly used by businesses to manage and secure devices. Intego also told us that it plans to add Developer Mode detection in a future update, subject to the access Apple’s APIs allow.


						

							


But can an iPhone actually get a virus?
If Intego ONE is an antivirus suite, you might reasonably assume that its new iPhone app scans the iPhone for viruses.
It doesn’t.
Traditional iPhone viruses are extremely uncommon because iOS apps are sandboxed, Apple tightly controls software distribution and the operating system incorporates substantial security protections.
That doesn’t make an iPhone invulnerable. Spyware, security exploits, malicious websites, compromised accounts and other threats can still put personal information at risk.
Intego isn’t claiming to replace Apple’s malware protection. Its proposition is effectively this: Apple protects the operating system, while Intego helps with some of the connections and security decisions that remain under the user’s control.

title: Surprise! We found Apple’s iPhone Ultra keynote script
content:
Macworld





Excited about Apple’s “Surprise and Shine” event on Wednesday? Can’t wait to hear about the iPhone Ultra, Apple Watch Series 12, and other new products? Wish you could read about the announcements before they’re, well, announced? Then you’ve come to the right place.
As is traditional at this time of year, we sent a team of crack reporters down to Apple Park, and after a few hours of rummaging in the bins, they hit paydirt: the script for Wednesday’s presentation, rehearsal tapes, marketing videos, everything we need to construct a minute-by-minute preview of the entire event. And we’re excited to present it here, to you.
(For the avoidance of doubt, none of that is true; this is for entertainment purposes only. But other than a few silly jokes and fake names, what follows is our genuine prediction, based on rumors, leaks, and a long history of covering these events. Return to Macworld on Wednesday to follow all the announcements as they happen and see how we got on.)
Here’s John Ternus!
9:59 am PT: We’re up and running! Black metal fans will recognise the toe-tapping sounds of Leviathan’s “Vesture Dipped In The Blood Of Morning.” That’s a California band, of course. Perhaps John Ternus is a fan.
10:00: Speaking of… here’s the man himself, in trademark t-shirt and sneakers. We’ve seen Ternus present at events before (notably covering much of the iPhone Air segment last fall, alongside since-departed design hotshot Abidur Chowdhury), and he’s a confident, relaxed speaker. But this is a different ballgame. Will we see his usual blend of positivity and technical detail, or will he default to vague platitudes in his new role as compère?
10:01: Today, we’re going to be hearing about three Apple products that have changed the world, Ternus says. The AirPods, the Apple Watch, and the iPhone.
10:02: “Technology is all about priorities,” he says. “And at Apple, we believe in logistical efficiency, upsell marketing, and delivering sustainable value to shareholders amid economic headwinds. Over to Neil.”

				
					

				
			John Ternus, the new boss.Apple
AirPods 5
10:03: Here’s a new face, likely the first of many following Apple’s recent exodus of senior talent. It’s Neil Overall, AirPods marketing VP and a rising star at Apple Park.
10:04: “The AirPods are one of the most iconic tech products in history,” says Overall. “But here at Apple, we refuse to rest on our laurels. This year, we’re going to make the best wireless earbuds in the world very, very slightly better. This is AirPods 5.”
10:05: We’re seeing a product video. The new AirPods look… yes, exactly the same as the 4th-gen models. No redesign. Which, to be fair, was what we expected following the revamp we got on the AirPods 4. They still don’t have silicone eartips. No sign of alternative color finishes either. It ends on the marketing slogan: “AirPods 5: Who Cares? You’ll Obviously Buy Them.™️”
10:06: But here’s a solid upgrade: the AirPods 5 get a new H3 chip. That’s a bold step, because the AirPods Pro 3 and AirPods Max 2, obviously both more expensive than the standard AirPods, remain on the H2… unless there’s more news to follow! Overall says the H3 will give the AirPods 5 better active noise cancellation (which is important since they don’t have the physical, passive noise cancellation of the AirPods Pro eartips) and access to Siri AI features.
10:07: The H3 chip also means improved battery life. The ANC version now lasts up to 6 hours with ANC enabled, up from 4 hours on the previous model. Obviously, that’s for just the earbuds; you’ll get more battery life by topping up in the case (which appears to be unchanged).
10:08: On to health, and the standard AirPods are getting a temperature sensor, which will enable them to feed more data into Apple Health. But it looks like they still won’t have a heart rate sensor. That’ll help Apple continue to upsell the AirPods Pro, which do have that sensor.
10:09: And we’re done: no sign of H3-equipped AirPods Pro or Max. (Or any AirPods with cameras.) AirPods 5 are available to pre-order on September 12, Overall announces, and will ship on September 18. They’re $179 with ANC or $129 without, so phew, there’s no price rise. “Back to you, Tim,” he adds. “Er, I mean John.”

				
					

				
			The AirPods 4, which look exactly like the AirPods 5.
Petter Ahrnstedt




New Apple Watches
10:10: Ternus is summing up the AirPods announcements. “We think you’re going to love them,” he says. “I’ve spoken to our accountants, and it’s just so exciting to work at a company that makes this much money.”
10:11: What’s up next? It’s the Apple Watch. Ternus says Tim Cook has forwarded to him dozens and dozens of letters and emails from people whose lives were saved by health notifications on their watches. “And frankly,” Ternus adds, “I couldn’t care less. I wish people would stop sending these messages.”
10:12: Another new face, this time from the Apple Park design department: Georgia de Giungle, Apple Watch product manager. “We know you love Apple Watch,” she says. “We love Apple Watch too. But we think you’re going to love the new Apple Watch even more, and pay us money so you can have it.”
10:13: Product video time. Lots of visuals of happy thin people doing sports. It looks like the basic design is unchanged. (Those of us who’ve been doing this for a while will know that the endlessly rumored redesigned Apple Watch is always just around the corner.) But there are clearly lots of new colors and new band designs.
10:15: The video ends on the inevitable slogan. “Apple Watch Series 12: Realistically The Only Option.™️”
10:16: “We’re thrilled to welcome back Apple Watch Edition,” gushes de Giungle. This isn’t the ludicrously expensive 18-karat gold model from the initial launch, we should note, but the somewhat more recent ceramic model. It’ll still be expensive, though. It looks nice, and comes in white and dark gray.
10:17: The Series 12 comes with an S12 processor, so as suspected, Apple is skipping the S11 generation. (The Series 10 and Series 11 both came with an S10 chip. Not that these designations matter a great deal.) Apple isn’t making any claims about performance here, despite the nominal double upgrade, and we wouldn’t expect a noticeable speed bump. It will just make things a little easier for Siri AI and similar on-device processing tasks.
10:18: “For millions of our customers, Apple Watch is the health device they rely on most,” says de Giungle. “Here’s Boswell to explain how Apple Watch Series 12 will take that to the next level.”
10:19: And here’s Dr. Boswell Boyce, Apple Watch and Health Product Marketing VP, to discuss health features on the new watch. “Thanks, Georgia,” he smiles.
10:20: The major upgrade is an all-day heart sensor. It will track your heart rate continuously, whether you’re working out or not. Boyce says this is going to be a game-changer for health data and will help millions of people to diagnose potential medical problems at an earlier and more treatable stage.
10:21: Boyce is walking us through the redesigned health and fitness apps on the watch, which now offer a wider range of metrics.
10:22: “That’s the new health features on Apple Watch. We think you’re going to love it. Back to you, Georgia.”
10:23: Now de Giungle is moving on to Apple Watch Ultra 4. This looks to be largely the same as the Series 12: no physical redesign or new buttons, an S12 processor, and continuous heart-rate tracking. 
10:24: And that’s it for the Apple Watch: the SE isn’t getting an update this year. Both new models will be available to pre-order on September 12 and will ship on September 18. Series 12 starts at $429 and the Ultra 4 at $829, which in both cases is a $30 increase on the last generation. Not ideal, but it could have been worse.

				
					

				
			Two Apple Watches from the 2025 batch.
David Price / Foundry




iPhone 18 Pro (and 18 Pro Max)
10:25: We’re back with John Ternus. “It’s time to talk about the iPhone,” he says. “Every year we release a new model and tell you it’s our best iPhone yet, and that’s always technically true. And this year is no exception. Here is iPhone 18 Pro. We think you’re going to love it.”
10:26: We’ve segued into a marketing video. The new phones look as attractive as ever, but (with apologies if this is getting repetitive) the designs appear to be the same as last year. The only obvious difference is that Cosmic Orange has been killed off, very sadly, and replaced by two new colors: light blue and dark red. The latter is called Dark Cherry and is sure to be the most popular option this year.
10:27: Here’s the slogan: “iPhone 18 Pro: So What If It Can’t Fold?™️”
10:28: “Over to you, Bill,” says Ternus. That’s iPhone Marketing Manager Bill Whittlingham, for those who aren’t familiar with the personnel at Apple Park.
10:29: Whittlingham says iPhone 18 Pro is designed from the ground up to deliver market-leading performance. The A20 Pro processor is Apple’s most powerful mobile chip, “optimized for our best-ever AI computation and even stronger battery life.” The company is claiming that the new chip is 10 percent faster than last year’s model.
10:30: As expected, and like the A19 Pro, the new chip has a 6-core CPU, with two performance and four efficiency cores. Pre-event rumors indicated the A20 Pro would be a 2nm chip (unlike the A19 and A19 Pro, which were 3nm chips), but that hasn’t been confirmed. Read our A20 Pro preview for more info.
10:31: To get specific, that battery life Whittlingham mentioned has gone up from 33 hours of video playback on the iPhone 17 Pro to 36 hours on the 18 Pro. On the Pro Max model, it’s gone up from 39 hours to 44. These are smaller improvements than last year (when Pro went from 27 to 33 and Pro Max from 33 to 39), but it all helps. It isn’t clear at this point how much of the increases are down to the new processors and how much is affected by battery capacity. There were rumors that the batteries would get bigger this year, but as always, Apple is keeping quiet about this spec.
10:32: There are more upgrades inside the 18 Pro. It gets the C2 cellular modem with mmWave for the first time and the N2 wireless networking chip, which brings unspecified battery life improvements.
10:33: We’re getting to a crucial part of the presentation: the cameras. Whittlingham is handing over to Finbarr Saunders, Manager, iPhone Camera Architecture, for more information on that topic.
10:34: Saunders says he’s proud to announce “the biggest improvement in iPhone photography since the iPhone 4 got a front-facing camera.” Which means the rumors were true and we’re getting a variable aperture on the main camera.
10:35: With this new feature, iPhone owners will be able to manually adjust the amount of light reaching the sensor, allowing for far better depth-of-field effects and more artistic control. This puts the iPhone on a par with high-end cameras and gives iPhone users the same capabilities as professional photographers, Saunders claims. But it’s worth bearing in mind that most iPhone owners use the Camera app on the default automatic settings, so this may affect only a small proportion of the user base.
10:36: The main camera isn’t the only lens to get an upgrade. The telephoto lens is getting a wider aperture, which should result in improved low-light performance.
10:37: “We can’t wait to see what you do with these cameras!” says Saunders. “And now back to Bill.”
10:38: Whittlingham is wrapping up. Ah, here’s a catch: while both 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max get the upgraded telephoto lens, the “bento box” displaying the new features indicates that only the 18 Pro Max gets the variable aperture. Both models will be available for pre-order this Saturday, September 12 (for reasons discussed elsewhere) and will ship on September 18.
10:39: This part could be painful. Yes, we’re looking at substantial price rises on both models. The iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,249, and the iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at $1,399. Ouch.

				
					

				
			A pre-release render of the iPhone Ultra.
Foundry




iPhone Ultra
10:40: We’re back with Ternus, who is summing up the iPhone 18 Pro announcements. “It’s our fiduciary responsibility to pass on increased manufacturing costs to the consumer,” he smiles.
10:41: But we’re moving on. The screen darkens. Something dramatic is happening.
10:42: Product video time! Yes, it’s the foldable iPhone. And for the first time this morning, we’re seeing a completely new design. For Apple fans, of course, it’s a completely new product category.
10:44: As we revealed some time ago, the phone is available in just two color finishes: silver/white or Indigo Blue. But the plateau housing the camera module on the back is always black; it isn’t matched to the main color.
10:45: The folding iPhone appears to have the stubbier dimensions that were leaked several months back; more passport than paperback. This is becoming an increasingly popular format (Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 uses it, possibly inspired by Apple) because it results in an unfolded screen that’s rectangular rather than square.
10:46: And here’s the slogan. “iPhone Ultra: Offensively Expensive.™️” So Apple did decide to go with the Ultra branding. Even though this may be a controversial choice.
10:47: “To tell you more about iPhone Ultra,” Ternus says, “here’s Barbara.” That’s Barbara Lighthouse, Industrial Designer, iPhone, for those who aren’t familiar with her work.
10:48: Lighthouse is talking about the screen. This segment is reminiscent of the iPhone Air launch last year; Apple is making a special effort to anticipate and pre-empt customers’ concerns about the design. In this case, the company knows that anyone who’s used or even seen a foldable will be wary about marks or creases appearing on the screen over time, but Lighthouse insists that Apple has solved the crease using ultra-thin glass and optically clear adhesive. The glass is thinner at the fold point to reduce stress during repeated use.
10:50: Just to cover the numbers, the Ultra’s screen specs are as follows: 5.4-inch (2088 x 1422) outer screen, 7.8-inch (2713 x 1920) inner screen. For comparison, the largest screen previously seen on an iPhone was the 6.9-inch display on the Pro Max. The Ultra (when unfolded) is pushing towards tablet territory; the first five generations of iPad mini had 7.9-inch screens, barely bigger at all.
10:51: The Ultra’s hinge (another potential concern for wary buyers) is made out of LiquidMetal, a zirconium-based alloy which is used for small, high-precision, high-performance parts. (Apple bought worldwide rights to this material 16 years ago, yet has found very few applications up to now: SIM ejector tools and possibly some watch parts.)
10:53: “As a result of this unique advantage, the iPhone Ultra has the most durable hinge in the entire foldables market,” says Lighthouse. The company has tested hundreds of thousands of folds, she says.
10:54: On the inside of that carefully designed chassis, the iPhone Ultra has some, but not all, of the capabilities of the iPhone 18 Pro. It does get the A20 Pro, so (depending on the RAM allocation, which Apple never announces) it should offer extremely fast performance. It also gets the C2 modem.
10:55: But the cameras aren’t quite on a par with the Pro models. The main camera is a dual- rather than triple-lens setup. There’s no telephoto lens and no variable aperture.
10:56: And there’s no Face ID. The Ultra unlocks using a Touch ID sensor hidden in the power button.
10:57: Lighthouse says the Ultra contains the “largest battery we’ve ever put in an iPhone.” And talks about software optimisations which should ensure users get all-day life despite running two screens. Nevertheless, as we saw with the iPhone Air last year, the numbers are mildly disappointing for what is likely to be a very premium product: the Ultra lasts up to 34 hours, less than the 18 Pro, and a lot less than the 18 Pro Max. Still, it’s more than the 17 Pro (33 hours) and a lot more than the iPhone Air (27).
10:59: Talking of a premium product, here’s the most important number. The iPhone Ultra starts at $2,199. And here’s another bombshell: it isn’t available right away. Apple says only that it’s coming “later in 2026.” There had previously been rumors that it might arrive in December despite being announced in September, so we’ll have to wait and see.
11:00: We’re back with Ternus, who’s wrapping up the iPhone Ultra announcements. “If it’s too expensive,” he says, “you don’t have to buy it.”
11:01: “But you will,” he adds.
11:02: It seems the event is drawing to a close. Except…

				
					

				
			
Apple




One more thing…
11:03: Those three little words: “One more thing…”
11:04: Time for another video. What’s Apple got in store for us? We’re seeing screens: screens on the wall, screens on shelves, screens sitting on the nightstand. Their owners are using them to FaceTime, talk to Siri, check the weather, search the web, control the lights, and adjust the heating. Some are just being used as clocks. It’s Apple’s long-rumored smart home hub.
11:06: Here’s the slogan: “HomeHub: Because What You Really Need Is Another Screen.™️”
11:07: John Ternus is pumped. “Apple is excited to push into the smart-home market and diversify our revenues going forward,” he says.
11:08: The HomeHub comes in two versions, both based around a 7-inch screen. The more slimline version is essentially just the screen and can be hung on the wall (there’s a magnetic attachment for this purpose); the second mounts this screen on a half dome like a HomePod mini cut in half.
11:10: There’s a clever feature based on facial recognition: the device is able to determine who’s looking at it and adjust preferences in real time, with apps and content displayed that vary according to the user. It has Center Stage, of course, and looks perfect for videoconferencing.
11:11: The HomeHub costs $349 and is available to pre-order from September 12. It will ship on September 18.
11:12: “We’ve got lots more smart-home products on the way to drive growth metrics,” says Ternus. And that wraps up the event for today.

				
					

				
			
Foundry

title: Tim Cook Won't Appear in Apple's September 9 Event Video
content:
Tim Cook will attend the screening for Apple's "Surprise and Shine" event this Wednesday, but he will not feature in the event video itself, according to sources cited by Bloomberg's Mark Gurman. Cook stepped down as Apple CEO on September 1 to become executive chairman of the company, paving the way for John Ternus to take over the top job.

Power On newsletter, Gurman said that Apple has "carefully orchestrated this transition to make Ternus the face of the foldable iPhone and all the new products to come. Putting Cook in the presentation would just undermine that."

title: iPhone 18 Pro: Everything M6 Tells Us About the A20 Chip
content:
Apple announced the M6 chip last week, just ahead of its September iPhone event, providing the clearest indication yet of what the A20 will bring to the iPhone 18 lineup.


Apple silicon generations share much of their architecture across the A-series and the M-series, so a new A-series chip normally functions as a partial preview of the M-series chip that follows it. This year the order reversed; the M6 was revealed on August 25, ahead of the A20 Pro expected in the iPhone 18 Pro this month.

18% faster and up to 30% more power efficient than the A19 Pro, which is broadly similar to the M6 over the M5.

Apple's First 2nm iPhone Chip

The M6 is Apple's first chip built on TSMC's 2nm (N2) process, with the second almost certain to be the A20. Being a smaller manufacturing process, N2 has higher transistor density, allowing Apple to pack more performance into a smaller area. 

Mac mini represents a change. As such, reports that the A20 and A20 Pro will move to N2 are now supported by a shipping product rather than analyst predictions. The consequence for the iPhone event is that the "Apple's first 2nm chip" claim is no longer available.

Dual Neural Engine?

The iPhone's Neural Engine has remained at 16 cores and approximately 35 trillion operations per second since the A17 Pro, spanning three generations. The M6 introduces a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, which Apple says system frameworks can address simultaneously for up to 2x the peak compute of previous generations.

WMCM packaging, which integrates memory onto the same wafer as the CPU, GPU, and Neural Engine to shorten the path between them. It is possible that die area and thermal constraints may limit a dual engine to the A20 Pro.

GPU AI Gains Are Now Incremental

Apple said the M5 delivered over 4x the peak GPU compute for AI compared to the M4, reflecting the introduction of Neural Accelerators within each GPU core. The M6 is rated at nearly 30% over the M5.

iPhone 17 Pro last September for the same architectural reason. Second-generation Neural Accelerators consequently appear to represent a refinement rather than another step change, suggesting the A20 Pro will not repeat the A19 Pro's headline figure.

Graphics Improvements Should Carry Across

The M6 adds 50% increased geometry rates, an updated shader core architecture, revised Dynamic Caching, and hardware-accelerated ray tracing. These are architectural changes and comparable graphics work has historically appeared across both the A-series and M-series within the same generation.

Memory Bandwidth Suggests a Modest A20 Gain

Memory bandwidth determines how quickly data moves between the memory and the processor, and it is the main constraint on running large language models on device. The M6 provides up to 170GB/s, which Apple describes as a 10% increase over the M5's 153.6GB/s.

That increase is small enough to indicate Apple is using a faster grade of the same LPDDR5X memory rather than moving to the newer LPDDR6 standard, which would have delivered a far larger jump. Reports indicate Apple is sourcing high-speed LPDDR5X from Samsung for the ‌iPhone 18‌ lineup, and the M6 is consistent with that.

WMCM packaging shortening the distance data travels than from the memory itself.

AV1 Encode Remains Absent

The M6 Media Engine supports hardware-accelerated H.264, HEVC, ProRes, and ProRes RAW, with AV1 decode but no AV1 encode, matching the M5. The omission on a new process node in a desktop chip makes its inclusion in the A20 Pro highly unlikely.

title: Top Stories: 'Surprise and Shine' Apple Event Preview, John Ternus Takes Over, and More
content:
After years of rumors, the highly anticipated foldable iPhone is almost here, but that's not all we're expecting to see at next week's big event, and we've got full coverage of expectations for the "Surprise and Shine" event.


Beyond the event, this week also saw John Ternus take over from Tim Cook as Apple CEO, while we learned a bit more about what's coming in iOS 27 and how Apple has been trying to respond to massive demand for its desktop Macs amid the surge in AI computing, so read on below for all of the details!

Top Stories

iPhone Ultra, iPhone 18 Pro, and More: Apple's September 9 Event Preview

Apple's September event will take place on Wednesday, September 9, at 10:00 a.m. Pacific Time. At the event, Apple will announce its 2026 iPhone lineup, and this year is a big one. Along with the slab-style iPhones we've been using for years, Apple is going to debut its first foldable device. We'll also get new Apple Watches, a new set of AirPods, and possibly some other surprises.


Everything we expect to see at the "Surprise and Shine" event is recapped in our event guide and overview video, so make sure to check it out.

Read John Ternus' First Memo to Apple Employees as CEO

This week marked the end of an era, with Tim Cook stepping down as Apple CEO after 15 years and hardware engineering chief John Ternus taking over the reins. Cook will remain active with Apple as Executive Chair.


In his first memo to employees as CEO, Ternus thanked employees for a warm welcome, expressed thanks to Cook for his contributions to Apple and assisting with the transition, and shared excitement about the future including "a huge launch" next week.

iPhone 18 Pro Pre-Orders May Start at an Unusual Time

Following next Wednesday's event, pre-orders for the new iPhone hardware may start at an unusual time. Pre-orders for the new iPhone models typically start at 5:00 a.m. Pacific Time on the Friday immediately following the event, but this year that falls on the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks.


As it did back in 2015 when pre-orders would also have fallen on the 11th, Apple will reportedly push things back this year and begin accepting pre-orders at midnight Pacific Time on Saturday, September 12.

iOS 27 Introduces New 'iPhone Handoff' Feature

Back at WWDC in June, Apple made the briefest of mentions about iOS 27 offering the ability to share a phone number between devices, and now we know how that feature will work.


MacRumors forum member pdfu this week shared a video showing how users will set up the feature, dubbed iPhone Handoff, from the Cellular section of the Settings app. iPhone Handoff will require carrier support, with the user's main eSIM remaining on their primary phone and a companion eSIM being sent to another iPhone. Once activated, a single phone number will be used across both devices, with the phone number automatically switching back and forth to whichever device is unlocked at the moment.

Foldable iPhone Ultra Likely Has MagSafe Charging

In addition to the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, next week's event will also see the long-awaited introduction of Apple's first foldable iPhone. The device will sacrifice a few features in order to enable its ultra-thin profile, and until recently it was thought that MagSafe charging might be one of those things.


In a recent interview with Tom's Guide, however, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman says "all indications" point toward MagSafe support being included on the phone.

Apple Caught Off Guard by AI Demand for Mac Mini and Mac Studio

Apple's unusually timed announcement of new Mac mini and Mac Studio models last week was driven by unexpectedly strong enterprise appetite for AI hardware, according to The Information. Apple normally releases new Mac models in the fall, closer to October or November, but Apple pulled Mac announcements ahead of the anticipated arrival of new iPhone models as it has sought to meet strong demand for its desktop Macs.


Apple highlighted the ‌Mac mini‌ and ‌Mac Studio‌'s shift toward business buyers back in June, with a "Business at the Park" event involving executives from major companies Ford, Disney, and Anthropic. The ‌Mac mini‌ was said to be the "darling" of the event.

A surge in demand for Mac hardware to run AI models has coincided with the global memory shortage, leaving many ‌Mac mini‌ and ‌Mac Studio‌ configurations out of stock for months and making the new models a priority to allow Apple to offer improved performance and higher production volumes.

MacRumors Newsletter

Each week, we publish an email newsletter like this highlighting the top Apple stories, making it a great way to get a bite-sized recap of the week hitting all of the major topics we've covered and tying together related stories for a big-picture view.

title: Get ready, Apple’s iPhone event is massive this year
content:
Macworld





Apple always holds its events at 10 am PT, with iPhone launches usually taking place on the second Tuesday or Wednesday of September. This year, that means the event, dubbed Surprise and Shine, will take place on Wednesday, September 9. Additionally, Apple always introduces its new iPhones and Apple Watches at its September special event, and this year is no different.
Except this year, everything is different. The iPhones are different. The CEO is different. The event may be different. Here’s what we expect from Apple’s big September show.
The John Ternus show
Tim Cook stepped down from his position as CEO after 15 years, though he will remain on the board of directors. He has named John Ternus, who was most recently senior vice president of hardware engineering, as his successor.
That means this is the first Apple Special Event in which Ternus will be the headliner, introducing the start of the event and thanking everyone at the end. Individual products are likely to be demonstrated by other Apple executives—they always are—but this is a big opportunity to shake up the format of Apple events in general. 
Will we see a return to live stage events? Will the structure and format of the pre-recorded video events change at all? Or will Ternus be essentially interchangeable for Tim Cook, with nothing else about these big product reveals changing at all? Will Apple make a “Turn” pun at some point? We’ll have to wait and see.
iPhone Ultra
For the first time in over a decade, Apple is going to dramatically change the iPhone’s form factor.
Apple is going to release a folding iPhone, which most are expecting to be called iPhone Ultra. It will fold in half like a book and be shaped sort of like a passport when closed; an unusual aspect ratio for any phone and especially an iPhone.

				
					

				
			This should be the relative size and shape of the folding iPhone Ultra.
Foundry




We expect two cameras (wide and ultrawide) on the back, one on the front, and the reintroduction of Touch ID in the side button for authentication. This is going to be a very premium product, with most rumors citing a starting price of $2,000 or more.
Not much is known about the software experience, though. Obviously, Apple will need to change some of how iOS looks and feels, and offer impressive new software features, to justify a folding phone with displays on the outside and inside and all new aspect ratios and sizes.
Check out our roundup of rumors about the iPhone Ultra for more.
iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max
The iPhone Ultra won’t be the only high-priced iPhone hitting the market this fall. With the standard iPhone 18 supposedly getting bumped back to a spring release, the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are going to be the only other iPhones launched this fall.
We expect an upgraded A20 Pro processor, a better modem (the C2 in many countries, possibly a Qualcomm modem in the U.S.), and a new Dark Cherry signature color.

				
					

				
			A dark red/cherry color should be the signature shade of the iPhone 18 Pro, along with Light Blue, Dark Gray, and Silver.
Foundry




For the most part, the iPhone 18 Pro will resemble the iPhone 17 Pro, but there should be a big upgrade to the rear camera (variable aperture, new sensor technology) and possibly a boost to 24 megapixels for the front camera. Battery capacity may go up by 6-8 percent, which could lead to longer battery life in conjunction with other improvements and optimizations.
Check out our roundup of rumors about the iPhone 18 Pro for more.
Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4
Apple always updates its Apple Watch line at the same time as the iPhone, whether it needs to or not. 
That means that this year, we’ll see the Apple Watch Series 12 and the Ultra 4. So far, none of the rumors suggest much of a change from the previous model. There will be a somewhat faster S12 processor, but major new health features or other changes don’t seem to be in the cards this year. Rumors say there won’t be a new SE 4 this year.
Apple TV and Homepod mini
Both long overdue for an update, Apple has been waiting to release a new Apple TV 4K set-top box and the HomePod mini until it figured out how to really make the new Siri work.
Now, with a whole new Siri architecture coming in the OS 27 updates this fall, it’s finally ready to ship these products. Because Apple TV set-top boxes and HomePods act as a “home hub” for Apple’s smart home controls, Apple needed to make sure they’re capable of running the all-new Siri.
That said, we haven’t heard of any major new software features that make use of the improved hardware coming to Apple TV or HomePod. These new products will give you the new Siri experience just as a modern Apple Watch will, but the tvOS interface and features probably won’t get a big change. It’s more like: you’ll ask Siri something, and you’ll get Siri AI answers, not the old Siri.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




HomePad preview
The new Apple TV and HomePod mini will mark the start of a bigger, more ambitious smart home plan for Apple that all revolves around the new Siri and the expanded AI features that will be built out on top of it in the coming months and years. The main device we’re waiting for is the so-called HomePad smart hub that has long been rumored.
The device is expected to have an iPad-like squarish screen that can either hang on a wall or dock to a speaker. It will reportedly run a new operating system dubbed HomeOS that is powered by Siri AI.
In his August 9 Power On newsletter, Mark Gurman reported that “a September preview of that product is plausible.” That could very well be Ternus’ surprise “One more Thing” to close the show. However, it is unlikely to go on sale until later in 2026 or early 2027.

title: IFA 2026: The best accessories we found for your iPhone, iPad, and Mac
content:
Macworld





IFA 2026 in Berlin is Europe’s answer to CES, attracting global brands and huge crowds. Macworld walked its 27 halls to find the most interesting Apple-related products, breezily ignoring Windows PCs and Nintendo Switch accessories. More importantly, this year’s best launches offered a glimpse at where Apple accessories are heading next.
Who’s the coolest? Charging was the biggest theme, as was keeping power banks cool enough to keep charging at peak rates. Qi2 25W is quickly becoming the premium wireless-charging standard, while Ugreen, Anker, ESR and Adam Elements all showed active cooling systems designed to control the extra heat. Belkin and Momax also showcased semi-solid-state batteries promising slimmer power banks, improved safety and longer lifespans.
Dark Cherry was another major trend, with Baseus, ESR and Momax betting on the rumored iPhone 18 Pro color becoming 2026’s must-have shade. Elsewhere, replaceable batteries, a folding OLED portable monitor and local-AI smart-home hubs showed manufacturers experimenting beyond the usual annual refresh.
Mac accessories were also more ambitious, with Thunderbolt 5 docks, 6K touchscreens, Neo colors, super-high refresh-rate multi-monitor hubs and displays with integrated docking and KVM functionality. Rather than catalog every launch, we picked the products that genuinely did something different. Here are the accessories that impressed us most.


UPerfect Omega One bendable display – A Mac monitor that actually folds

				
					

				
			
Simon Jary




We’ve tested some of the best portable monitors for Mac but none has literally bent in half like the UPerfect Omega One. It’s the iPhone Ultra of monitors, and loks perfect for traveling MacBook users.
This compact display pulls out to a flexible 16.3-inch 2K OLED touchscreen, and you can hardly spot the bend point when fully flat. It uses an advanced flexible substrate and seamless hinge design for seamless folding and optical consistency. The panel is subtly curved so that the top and bottom edges naturally lean toward the viewer.
Pre-orders will ship at the end of October.


						

							


Ugreen CryoPulse and new MagFlow Pro range – 25W Qi2 with liquid cooling

				
					

				
			
Simon Jary




Ugreen unveiled its new MagFlow lineup at IFA 2026, claiming the world’s first Qi2 25W magnetic power bank with active micro-pump liquid cooling. The new lineup tackles the heat challenge of faster wireless charging by combining active cooling with passive heat-dissipation structures in a system the company calls CryoPulse.
Ugreen refreshed its MagFlow Pro family with a 3-in-1 Magnetic 25W Wireless Charging Stand (€139.99 / £119.99), pictured above, designed for desks and bedside tables and a 2-in-1 Foldable Magnetic 25W Wireless Charger (€49.99 / £43.99) that measures 60 × 72 × 27mm when closed.
The flagship 10K, 25W MagFlow Pro Magnetic Power Bank ($149.99 / €119.99 / £109.99) features CryoPulse micro-pump liquid cooling, VC copper heat-spreading foil and separated charging components to reduce heat buildup, while ThermalGuard adjusts power automatically and a transparent window shows coolant circulation, claims Ugreen. A tiny pump circulates coolant to pull heat away from the cells, and you can watch it all happen through a clear Cyber Window. In Ugreen’s testing, peak temps ran up to 18°F cooler than the industry benchmark, with temperature rise cut by up to 44%. Alongside the 25W wireless charging is 45W max wired output via a built-in cable.

				
					

				
			Ugreen also showed off a pair of new travel chargers for iPhone, AirPods and Apple Watch.
Simon Jary



							


Baseus Dark Cherry Collection – Dark Cherry done comprehensively

				
					

				
			
Baseus




Dark Cherry is the Cosmic Orange of 2026, long rumored to be Apple’s new look-at-me colorway for its iPhone 18 Pro series.
Baseus has a whole charging and protection collection in Dark Cherry, including products such as its AH22 100W Digital Display Charger ($59), AM52 Qi2.2 Power Bank ($79), Air Ultra-Slim Power Bank ($79), and Inspire XC1 earbuds all shipping with discounts of up to $38 until the end of October.
The Baseus PicoGo Pro USB-C Charger Fast Charging with Smart Display is a 3-port charger for any modern Apple device and includes a Dark Cherry 100W USB-C cable.
The Baseus Picogo Air magnetic power bank is super-slim at 0.27 inches (6.9mm) thick, but you’ll be too busy marvelling at its Dark Cherry color to even notice!


						

							


Anker chargers and refresh-champ hub – Smarter charging, cooling and 240Hz displays

				
					

				
			
Simon Jary




The Anker Desktop USB-C Hub is really a docking station, having four USB ports (two 10Gbps USB-C and two 5Gbps USB-A), Gigabit Ethernet, SD and microSD memory card slots, and both DisplayPort and HDMI ports. It’s special because Anker claims it can run HD monitors at an ultra-smooth 240Hz refresh rate or two 4K displays at 120Hz. The connected MacBook can receive up to 100W of power. A built-in display shows real-time port status, charging power, data transfer rate, and device temperature, and you can upload custom images for a rotating slideshow, or double-tap to start a Pomodoro timer with gentle health reminders.
Anker also unveiled a pocket-sized (3.74 x 1.98 x 1.59 inches) Nano Universal Charger (4-in-1, 100W, Smart Display), pictured above, with built-in U.S. / U.K. / E.U. plugs supporting use in 200+ countries and regions. It can charge up to four devices and supply 100W for your MacBook.

				
					

				
			
Simon Jary




Joining the fight to keep its portable chargers as cool as possible, Anker claims that its new 25W MagGo Power Bank 2 Pro, shown above, is “the world’s fastest and coolest wireless power bank.”. We’ll test this when we have a sample in the Macworld Labs, but Anker showed us an intriguing test where it lay a slab of butter on a series of charging power banks to show just how hot they can get. A patented fan-control algorithm, dual air ducts and a three-layer graphene heat-spreading system pull heat away continuously, keeping the back of the power bank below 96.8 degrees Fahrenheit (36 Celsius) throughout charging. Anker compares this to competing magnetic power banks that typically reach 113 degrees (45 Celsius) or higher, forcing the connected phone to throttle power. Anker’s butter slab didn’t melt.
Anker also showed off its new MagStand Charging Station, Laptop Charger Pro, and Nano Charging Station.


						

							


Belkin UltraCharge Pro Power Banks – Next-generation semi-solid-state battery technology

				
					

				
			
Simon Jary




Belkin showed off its new range of semi-solid-state portable chargers. Semi-solid-state technology is the next-generation of battery tech that promises improved safety and durability, slimmer design and longer battery life.
Belkin’s new UltraCharge Pro uses a BoostSolid Cell that adds a gel-like layer alongside the liquid electrolyte, enabling a slimmer, more compact design while improving reliability and performance, and increasing thermal stability. Belkin claims that the new products will last up to 3x longer than other power banks.


						

							


ESR cool chargers and iPhone protection – Cooler charging and stronger protection

				
					

				
			
Simon Jary




ESR showcased its latest charging, protection, and productivity products at IFA 2026, including Dark Cherry versions of many of its iPhone accessories such as the super-adjustable and lightweight Cyclone 25W Magnetic Charging Pad with CryoBoost. The company claims that the integrated active cooling reduces heat generation by 6.5°C, reducing the risk of overheating that can slow down or even stop device charging.
Under its “Designed for What’s Next” philosophy, ESR showed off the new Atelier Case for iPhone that is made with silicone-based vegan leather pioneered in luxury car interiors and resists stains, wear, and fading.
Less visible by design are new screen protectors that ESR claims defend screens with up to 10x impact absorption, while its Armorite Pro Edition features Accessory Glass by Corning to provide up to 2x better scratch resistance compared with other screen protector glass.


						

							


Mobile Pixels Prisma – Curved screen for Mac Studio or Mac mini

				
					

				
			
Simon Jary




Owners of the Mac Studio and Mac mini will swoon over this monitor that hosts a special adjustable stand that holds either of the two Macs—or a 15W Qi2 magnetic iPhone charger if you prefer a MacBook.
It’s an ultrawide 40-inch 5K2K curved monitor with a built-in hub that not only connects with the Mac but has ports including USB-C, USB-A, and SD/MicroSD card readers. At the back there’s an enclosure for an NVMe SSD (up to 8TB).
Mobile Pixels expects the Prisma to be available in spring 2027.


						

							


Belkin’s MacBook Neo accessories

				
					

				
			
Simon Jary




We’re excited to test Belkin’s new range of color-matching gadgets for our best MacBook Neo accessories roundup. The fresh four-color series includes the BoostCharge Compact USB-C Wall Charger 30W that will complement the latest MacBook Neo colorways in Citrus, Blush, Indigo and Silver. 
The new Belkin Neo collection delivers a coordinated charging experience with charger, 2m braided charging cable, Neo power bank and magnetic wireless charger, with prices starting at $26.99 / £27.99 / €29.99 this September.
Satechi, which announced its own Neo-color accessories earlier this year, was also at IFA with its range, including the Satechi USB-C Snap Hub.


						

							


Alogic shows off its Vision – Ambitious displays, docking and Thunderbolt 5

				
					

				
			
Simon Jary




Mac monitor fans will have loved the raft of new displays shown by Alogic at IFA 2026. These included a higher-resolution Aspekt displays and a new Vision series of monitors for business.
For maximum screen space and peak resolution, the Aspekt Touch 32” 6K steps up to a 6016 × 3384 resolution with its touchscreen. The smaller Aspekt Touch 27” 5K combines a 5120 × 2880 IPS touchscreen display with 600-nit brightness and wide color coverage. Both Aspekt Touch models will be available at the end of October and support DisplayPort daisy chaining, making it easier to build a multi-monitor setup without adding another dock to the desk. Stretching to a wider canvas, the Aspekt Touch 5K Ultrawide 34” (available end of November) takes the same idea into a 21:9 format with a resolution of up to 5120 x 2160, a 100Hz refresh rate and 10-point multitouch. 
The business workplace Vision series includes the Vision 27-inch QHD Docking Monitor that provides a 2560 × 1440 IPS display with a 100Hz refresh rate, 300-nit typical brightness and 100% sRGB coverage. The Vision 34-inch Ultrawide QHD Curved Docking Monitor is designed for larger workspaces, with a 3440 x 1440 resolution and 21:9 aspect ratio. Both include USB-C docking with up to 90W laptop charging and built-in KVM functionality, allowing users to switch between two computers while keeping the same keyboard, mouse and display setup.
Alogic also showcased its new Flash Thunderbolt 5 Docking Station at the show., which is an 80Gbps Thunderbolt 5 docking station with 13-in-1 ports that can support up to three external displays for the latest MacBooks.


						

							


MOFT – Super-thin flexible wallet

				
					

				
			
Simon Jary




Origami-like folding is a MOFT super power, and it claims that its new Snap-on Phone Stand & Wallet AERA is the world’s thinnest three-card magnetic wallet stand.
Weighing just 45g, it offers three viewing angles, and over 20 color choices in its Movas vegan leather. There is also a trackable FindMy version available.


						

							


AI home hubs – Local AI to control the autonomous home

				
					

				
			
Ugreen




Not content with leading the charging accessory market, both Ugreen and Anker announced local AI home hubs at IFA.
Under its “Smarter Living Starts Here” theme, Ugreen showcased its new HomeAgent local AI-powered, voice-control and smart-recognition products that combine storage, computing, and control in one device to connect AIoT devices such as security cameras, smart speakers, and smart photo frames. The emphasis is on local (NAS-based) storage and local AI to keep your personal data private. The hub is Ugreen’s HomeAgent and ultimate MasterAgent devices that sync with home camera systems, speakers, and smart frames. Ugreen SynCare cameras can continuously capture everyday moments as they happen, which you can later discover to display through spoken keyword search.

				
					

				
			
Simon Jary




This will compete with Anker’s MindBase, a local AI home hub that functions as the central brain for an autonomous home, bringing together three core capabilities: whole-home connectivity, local intelligence and memory, alongside the company’s security, energy, cleaning and audio ecosystems. Anker EasyOmni Link is a software system that brings the Anker ecosystem and compatible third-party smart home devices into a central local intelligence system, supporting close to 100 Anker devices and hundreds of Matter-compatible products, working alongside Apple HomeKit, Amazon Alexa, Google Assistant and Home Assistant.


						

							


Krafted Edge – Replaceable battery, unusually thoughtful design

				
					

				
			
Simon Jary




This slim 20000mAh power bank looks like no other as it sits under your MacBook, and has two USB-C and two USB-A ports plus a removable 20cm colored USB-C cable that magnetically slots into the power bank.
The Krafted Edge can charge a laptop at 65W, which should be enough for any MacBook unless under an extreme performance load.
Also unlike most power banks, its battery is replaceable, meaning zero obsolescence.


						

							


Adam Elements CQ3 25W Cooling Car Mount Charger – Actively cooled 25W car charging

				
					

				
			
Adam Elements




This powerful magnetic car charger with suction mount and air-vent clips supports up to 25W in-car wireless charging, backed up with advanced cooling plus quiet performance. The built-in silent cooling fan has claimed noise levels as low as 35dB, while reducing heat to 10°C in standby to maintain peak charging.


						

							


Momax Dusky Cherry – Ultra-thin semi-solid-state charging

				
					

				
			
Simon Jary




Another Dark Cherry range comes from Momax, which showcased its Dusky Cherry color direction, as well as its super-slim semi-solid-state battery technology, under the mission to Recharge for Life.
At IFA 2026, Momax showed its 1-Power S.Pass Air 5,000 mAh Magnetic Wireless Battery Pack that is only 6mm thin. Its semi-solid-state battery uses a hybrid electrolyte composition designed to reduce leakage and flammability risks while improving battery stability for everyday charging.


						

							


Orbitkey tech organizers – A smarter answer to cable clutter

				
					

				
			
Simon Jary




There’s a lot of tech at IFA but where and how do you stop this taking over your home or office? If your tech exists in a tangle living loose in a drawer or shoebox, Australian accessory maker Orbitkey has five new handy tech organisers, from a 0.5L everyday pouch to a full cable kit, all in Black, or more fetching Terracotta and Lilac colors.
The Tech Organiser Mini (0.5L) is for those who carry light: a cable, charger, earbuds, a power bank. The Tech Organiser (1.5L) opens flat for a working setup with everything immediately visible. Its Tech Organiser Plus (2.5L) is designed for bigger loads, such as multiple chargers, mouse, hard drive, longer cables, and a hub. For an organiser you can wear the Tech Sling (3L) works best for a commute or day of travel. Finally, the Cable Organiser Pouch has space for charging bricks, spare leads, adapters, and dongles.

title: iPhone Ultra, iPhone 18 Pro, and More: Apple's September 9 Event Preview
content:
Apple's September event will take place on Wednesday, September 9 at 10:00 a.m. Pacific Time. Apple will announce its 2026 iPhone lineup, and this year is a big one. Along with the slab-style iPhones we've been using for years, Apple is going to debut its first foldable device. We'll also get new Apple Watches, a new set of AirPods, and possibly some other surprises.

Subscribe to the MacRumors YouTube channel for more videos.

Everything we expect to see at the "Surprise and Shine" event is below.

Foldable iPhone

Apple's 2026 iPhone lineup will include its first foldable device. We don't know what Apple will call it, but rumors suggest it might be named the iPhone Ultra.

OLED outer display, which is what you'll use when the iPhone is closed. It will unfold into a larger ‌OLED‌ display that's approximately 7.8 inches.


The design is wider than it is tall when it's open, and you can picture it as something like an iPad mini that folds in half. Samsung's recent Galaxy Z Fold8 matches the foldable iPhone rumors, so it may be the best look at the size and layout of Apple's device.

optically clear adhesive that will fill in any micro-cracks caused by repeated folding.

iPhone 17 Pro Max. With a chassis that thin, Apple had to make design compromises.

Face ID, so it's going to use Touch ID instead. There will be a ‌Touch ID‌ side button, similar to the iPad Air and ‌iPad mini‌. Though ‌Face ID‌ isn't included, there will be front cameras for both the inner and outer displays.

Apple also didn't have room for a three-lens rear camera system, so the ‌iPhone Ultra‌ won't have a telephoto lens. Rumors suggest it will have an Ultra Wide lens and a Wide lens located on the back of the device, so the rear camera works whether the ‌iPhone Ultra‌ is folded or unfolded.

MagSafe would be included because leaked dummy models didn't feature a magnetic ring, but Bloomberg says ‌MagSafe‌ charging will indeed be a feature.

18 percent faster and up to 30 percent more power efficient than the A19 Pro, and it could have a 7-core GPU, a wider memory interface, and a larger L2 cache for its efficiency cores. We're expecting 12GB of RAM.

Apple's 2026 iPhones could use its house-designed C2 modem, which is expected to be faster and more efficient than the C1X. It's not yet clear if Apple has added mmWave technology to the C2, and if it hasn't, foldable iPhone models sold in the U.S. could use Qualcomm modems instead. mmWave 5G isn't widely used outside of the U.S., but it is an expected feature for U.S. iPhones. The other alternative is limiting the foldable iPhone to sub–6GHz 5G speeds worldwide.

Each half of the ‌iPhone Ultra‌ will have a battery inside, and it could have a total capacity in the 5,400 to 5,800 mAh range. The ‌iPhone 17 Pro‌ Max has a 5,088 mAh battery for comparison.

Apple isn't taking risks with color. The ‌iPhone Ultra‌ will come in silver/white and a second color that's been described as a very deep shade of indigo that's close to black.

iPad.

Apple's first foldable won't be cheap. According to rumors, it will cost at least $2,000, and higher-capacity models could be upwards of $2,500.

iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max

The iPhone 18 Pro models will look a lot like the ‌iPhone 17 Pro‌ models, with no major design changes expected. There are rumors that the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max might be a little bit thicker and heavier because of a larger battery, but ‌iPhone 17 Pro‌ cases are expected to fit the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ models. The camera plateau could be slightly thicker to accommodate a new variable aperture lens.


Apple has new colors planned, including a dark cherry shade, light blue, and silver. Rumors suggest there won't be a black ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ option.

might be more subtle with the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌. While the overall shape isn't being updated, the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ and Pro Max could have a smaller Dynamic Island. There were early rumors about under-display ‌Face ID‌ with no Dynamic Island at all, but that's not going to happen.

LTPO+ display that's more efficient than the current ‌OLED‌ display.

variable aperture, giving users more control over the light that reaches the lens. An option for a smaller aperture in bright lighting could improve exposure, while a larger aperture in lower lighting conditions would let in more light to reduce grain and produce sharper images. A variable aperture also gives more control over background blur. Some rumors suggest this might be a feature exclusive to the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max, but it's not clear if that's accurate.

There might be changes to the Camera Control button. Apple is supposedly simplifying it to eliminate the capacitive layer that lets you swipe to adjust camera settings on the button.

As with the foldable iPhone, some or all of the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ models could get Apple's C2 modem, but again, it's possible U.S. models will have Qualcomm modems for mmWave 5G.

will be more expensive. Apple is paying more for memory and storage, and prices for Macs and iPads already went up. We could see a price increase ranging from $100 to $300.

Apple Watch Series 12

The Apple Watch Series 12 won't design changes, but Apple could bring back the ceramic case option. We're expecting an updated processor that could bring improvements to health and fitness tracking.

Apple is testing a feature that would let the heart rate sensor continuously collect data throughout the day, powering a new Health app feature that could show wellness-related info similar to what the Oura Ring offers.

Apple Watch Ultra 4

Like the Apple Watch Series 12, the Apple Watch Ultra 4 will have no major changes. It's likely to get the same upgraded processor and related changes.

AirPods 5

References to AirPods 5 were found in the macOS 26.7 release candidate, and the new earbuds could launch alongside the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ models. Apple could add an updated H3 chip for improved sound quality and lower latency, and we're likely to still get an ANC version and a non-ANC version.
Possible Product Launches


Home hub - Apple is working on a home hub with a 7-inch square display, an integrated camera, presence detection sensors, and more. It will control smart home devices, but it will also run apps. Rumors suggest it can be used to make video calls, play content, and interact with Siri AI, the new version of ‌Siri‌ in iOS 27. Apple has been waiting to launch the home hub because ‌Siri‌ AI is a central feature of the new device.

 
Apple TV 4K - There's a new Apple TV with a faster processor in the works, and it could come at the September event. No design changes are expected, but an updated chip could support ‌Siri‌ AI and new gameplay features. There are also signs of a new remote in Apple code.

 
HomePod mini - The HomePod mini is due for a refresh, and it's also expected to get a faster processor. We haven't heard word of design changes, but it could come in new colors.



Software Updates

At the September 9 event, Apple will announce the release dates for ‌iOS 27‌, iPadOS 27, macOS Golden Gate, tvOS 27, watchOS 27, and visionOS 27. Apple will also likely seed release candidate versions of the updates to developers and public beta testers following the event.

Based on historical release timelines, ‌iOS 27‌ and its sister updates could come out as soon as September 14.

What Not to Expect

There are several other products rumored to be launching before the end of 2026, but they'll likely come at a second event in October or November. There's also a notable omission from the lineup, because Apple is going to delay the iPhone 18.

 
iPhone 18 - The standard ‌iPhone 18‌ will not launch in September 2026, with Apple instead planning to debut it in spring 2027 alongside the iPhone 18e and the iPhone Air 2. In the fall, we're only getting the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌, ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max, and foldable iPhone.

 
Apple Watch SE 4 - There won't be a new Apple Watch SE 4 this year.

 
M6 MacBook Pro - A new entry-level MacBook Pro with an M6 chip is coming before the end of the year, but not at the September event.

 
M6 iMac - There's also an M6 iMac rumored to be coming in 2026, but Apple is likely to hold a Mac event to announce it, or do it via press release at a later date.

 
OLED MacBook Pro - We've been waiting on an ‌OLED‌ touchscreen ‌MacBook Pro‌, and it's rumored for late 2026 or early 2027. It's not a candidate for Apple's September event.

 
OLED iPad mini - There's an ‌OLED‌ ‌iPad mini‌ in development, and it's expected to launch before the end of October. It's another one that's unlikely for an iPhone event.



Apple's New CEO

New Apple CEO John Ternus has presented at Apple events before, but the iPhone event will be the first he hosts as CEO in place of Tim Cook.

Cook was Apple's CEO for 15 years, so a transition to Ternus leading an event is a major change.

Cook is now Apple's executive chairman, and he may not make an appearance during the event at all.

iPhone Preorders

Apple almost always holds preorders on the Friday after an event, but this year, that Friday is 9/11. It's unlikely Apple will do iPhone preorders on Friday because of the date, so orders could happen on Saturday instead. The last time iPhone preorders overlapped with the 9/11 date in 2015, Apple pushed orders to Saturday.

If Apple follows the same pattern, the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ models and the ‌iPhone Ultra‌ could be available for preorder on Saturday, September 12. Back in 2015, Apple started preorders at 12:01 a.m. Pacific Time, but in recent years, preorders have started at 5:00 a.m. Pacific Time. Preorders this year could take place at 5:00 a.m. on September 12.

The new iPhones will likely launch on Friday, September 18, regardless of preorder date.

How to Watch

Apple's "Surprise and Shine" event will start at 10:00 a.m. Pacific Time on Wednesday, September 9. Apple will livestream the event on its website, on YouTube, and through the ‌Apple TV‌ app on supported devices.



For those unable to watch the livestream, MacRumors will have full event coverage on MacRumors.com and the MacRumorsLive X account. We'll also take a much closer look at all of the new products after the event.

title: Foldable iPhone Ultra: The Latest Rumors Before Apple's Event
content:
We're less than a week away from the debut of Apple's first foldable iPhone, and rumors have been picking up as the event date approaches. Here's the latest.

Subscribe to the MacRumors YouTube channel for more videos.


MagSafe - Even though foldable iPhone dummies we saw earlier this year didn't have a MagSafe ring, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman claims all signs indicate MagSafe charging will be supported.

 	
Crease - Some of the early language about the foldable iPhone's crease suggested Apple might have found a way to make it invisible, but later rumors are more realistic. The crease is minimal, but Apple hasn't found a magic way to get rid of it.

 	
Touch ID - Touch ID is still expected for the foldable iPhone. Apple didn't have room for the Face ID hardware because the device is rumored to be just 4.5mm thick. There will be volume buttons at the top of the iPhone Ultra, with a ‌Touch ID‌ side button for unlocking.

 	
Software - iOS 27 makes it clear Apple is making sure apps will work with the foldable iPhone. There's a big push for app resizability and layout flexibility. The iPhone is expected to support multitasking, sidebars, and side-by-side app usage.

 	
Cameras - Camera rumors haven't changed. We're expecting a two-lens camera setup with Wide and Ultra Wide lenses.

 	
Chips - Early rumors said Apple would transition to the C2 and move away from Qualcomm, but it looks like Apple might still use Qualcomm modems in the United States. It hinges on whether the C2 supports mmWave 5G. The ‌iPhone Ultra‌ will also adopt Apple's A20 Pro chip, the same as the iPhone 18 Pro models.

 	
Colors - The foldable iPhone is expected in white/silver and dark blue.

 	
Apple Pencil - Apple tested an Apple Pencil with the foldable iPhone, but it's probably not going to launch.

 	
Launch Timing - Rumors on ‌iPhone Ultra‌ launch timing and production have been mixed, with some sources reporting delays. Gurman says he will be "very surprised" if the device doesn't launch at the same time as the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ models or "very close to it." It's still possible supplies could be constrained, leading to long waits for those who don't pre-order early.

 	
Price - The ‌iPhone Ultra‌ is expected to cost over $2,000, possibly up to $2,500 depending on storage capacity.

title: Is Apple working on its own game controller?
content:
Macworld





According to a sharp-eyed MacRumors reader, the first macOS 26.7 release candidate included references to a pair of game controllers. The same release candidate included code numbers for a slew of other in-development Apple products.
The two hardware devices are referenced as T6502 and T1057 and they include most standard game controller features: dual thumbsticks, face buttons, triggers, home and menu buttons, and different haptic features. One notable difference: the T1057 controller includes gryscope and accelerometer support (so games can tell how you tilt or move the controller) while T6502 does not. 
While this is an interesting find, I caution readers not to assume that Apple is working on its own game controller. There have been rumors of Apple making its own game controller for over a decade, and nothing has ever come of it. Apple has instead done a lot to provide proper support for third-party game controllers, whether that’s its own MFi program or controllers for home console systems.
For years, you have been able to sync an Xbox or PlayStation controller to your Apple devices, including iPhones, iPads, Macs, and Apple TV. That includes the latest controllers for the Xbox Series X and PlayStation 5.
These code numbers probably reference test devices that are used in testing support for core game controller functions, or legacy references to R&D projects for Apple game controllers that may never be built. Apple famously has many products in various stages of development and only a few of them are ever released.
Apple could be building its own game controller, but there would be little reason to. Find My support and automatic switching between devices would be useful, but it’s hard to argue that modern controllers are missing features that require Apple to do its own thing. It makes much more sense for Apple to support the tens of millions of Xbox and PlayStation controllers than to make its own, especially as Apple’s platforms are not very popular for the kinds of games one usually plays with controllers.

title: iPhone Duo?
content:
While the long-awaited foldable iPhone has often been referred to as the iPhone Ultra or the iPhone Fold in rumors, another name making the rounds is iPhone Duo.


There is no actual evidence that Apple will use the iPhone Duo name, but it is certainly a possibility. Apple has used Duo branding in the past, for its PowerBook Duo line of laptops in the 1990s and for its MagSafe Duo Charger in the early 2020s. 

In this case, Duo would refer to the foldable iPhone's dual screens.

Microsoft released a dual-screen Android smartphone called the Surface Duo in 2020 that has since been discontinued, and Intel had its popular lines of Core Duo and Core 2 Duo processors in the 2000s, so perhaps Apple will want to avoid using Duo branding due to that history. However, competing companies have devices with Ultra and Fold branding too, such as Samsung's Galaxy S26 Ultra and Galaxy Z Fold8.

Macworld reporter Filipe Espósito cited a source familiar with Apple's plans who said the foldable iPhone will be named iPhone Ultra. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman said many Apple employees refer to the device as the iPhone Ultra within the company, but he has never firmly reported that it will be the official name.

Apple has used Ultra branding for the Apple Watch Ultra, CarPlay Ultra, and its M1 Ultra, M2 Ultra, M3 Ultra, and M5 Ultra chips.

There's also a 34-inch 5K Ultrawide model, which offers a resolution of up to 5,120 x 2,160 and a 100Hz refresh rate, plus the 10-point multitouch functionality

The 27-inch 5K ($1,899.99) and 32-inch 6K ($2,999.99) models will be available by the end of October, while the 34-inch Ultrawide 5K model will be priced at $2,799.99 and launch by the end of November.

Clarity 6K display

Alogic has also expanded its Clarity family of displays, adding a 12-megapixel webcam to the 27-inch 5K ($1,899.99) and 32-inch 6K ($3,099.99) models, with availability by the end of October. Both displays similarly offer touchscreen support, USB-C, HDMI 2.1, and DisplayPort 1.4 connectivity options, USB-A and audio connections, and up to 90 watts of upstream charging.

Vision displays

There's also a new 34-inch Edge 5K Ultrawide option priced at $1,599.99 launching by mid-November, and finally, on the low end of the display lineup, Alogic is introducing new 24-inch ($199.99) and 27-inch ($299.99) options in its Vision family of business-oriented displays, plus a 34-inch Ultrawide model.

FlashDock 5

Turning to peripherals, Alogic has announced the FlashDock 5 docking station, a 13-port Thunderbolt 5 dock supporting full bandwidth of up to 80 Gbps in symmetric mode or up to 120 Gbps in asymmetric mode. It supports up to three external displays (depending on capabilities of the host computer), with two HDMI 2.1 ports, two USB-C 3.2 Gen 2 ports, three USB-A ports, a 2.5 Gigabit Ethernet port, SD and microSD card readers, a 3.5mm combo audio port, and an additional downstream Thunderbolt 5 port. There's also an integrated M.2 NVMe SSD slot to allow you to add external storage. It's available now and is priced at $399.99.

Crux mouse

And on the input side, Alogic is now shipping several previously announced accessories including the ergonomic multifunction Crux productivity mouse, priced at $79.99. The Hush full-size keyboard ($89.99) with backlit keys and multi-device support is also shipping, as is the Hush mouse ($29.99) with a slim design and multi-device support.
